items.stem: Monochromatic light of vacuum wavelength 515 nm (c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) propagates inside dry air of refractive index 1 during a bathymetric laser-ranging tank. The ray meets a planar interface with fused-silica glass of refractive index 1.46 at an incidence angle of 18° measured from the normal. Calculate the refracted angle in fused-silica glass.
items.workedSolution: By Snell's law, n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂, so sin θ₂ = (1 × sin 18°) / 1.46 = 0.2117. Taking the inverse sine gives θ₂ = 12.2°.

markScheme.criterion: Applies n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂ to obtain θ₂ = 12.2° (A).

options.distractorRationale: Inverts the refractive index ratio in Snell's law, computing arcsin((n₂ / n₁) sin θ₁).

items.stem: A parallel-faced optical crown glass plate of thickness 0.04 m and refractive index 1.52 sits in dry air (n₀ = 1) on a gemstone goniometer calibration rig. A monochromatic beam enters at 32° to the normal. Calculate the perpendicular lateral shift d of the emerging parallel beam.
items.workedSolution: By Snell's law, sin θ₁ = (1 sin 32°) / 1.52 ⇒ θ₁ = 20.4°. The perpendicular lateral displacement of the emergent ray is d = t₁ sin(θ₀ − θ₁) / cos θ₁ = 0.00858 m.

items.stem: A 350 m step-index optical fiber used in a transoceanic telecommunications link has core refractive index 1.5 and cladding refractive index 1.44. A laser ray in air (n_ext = 1.00) enters the center of the flat end-face at θ_in = 8.7° to the fiber axis. What angle of incidence θ_w does the refracted ray make with the normal to the core–cladding wall?
items.workedSolution: At the entry face, 1 sin 8.7° = 1.5 sin θ_axis ⇒ θ_axis = 5.79°. Since the core wall is parallel to the axis, its normal is perpendicular to the axis, giving θ_w = 90° − θ_axis = 84.2°.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Gives the refracted angle θ_axis relative to the fiber axis instead of subtracting from 90° to find the angle to the wall normal.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts the external launch angle θ_in from 90° without accounting for refraction at the entry end-face.

items.stem: A multimode step-index fiber of length 240 m in an astronomical echelle-spectrograph feed has n_core = 1.62 and n_clad = 1.51 in air (n_ext = 1.00, illustrated with a 14.4° launch ray). Taking c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹ and neglecting material dispersion, what is the maximum multipath (modal) pulse broadening Δt between the fastest axial ray and the slowest guided ray?
items.workedSolution: Axial transit time t_min = n_core L / c = (1.62 × 240) / (3.00 × 10⁸) = 1.30 × 10⁻⁶ s. At the critical angle sin θ_c = n_clad / n_core, t_max = t_min / sin θ_c = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 1.39 × 10⁻⁶ s. Modal delay Δt = t_max − t_min = 9.44 × 10⁻⁸ s.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δt = (n_core L / c)(n_core / n_clad − 1) = 9.44 × 10⁻⁸ s (B).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes 1/v = 1/f + 1/u instead of 1/f − 1/u (equivalent to treating the converging lens as diverging or adding reciprocals).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts focal length directly from object distance |u − f| instead of using reciprocal distances.

items.stem: During optical testing on a myopia-corrective ophthalmic spectacle trial, a 0.05 m illuminated target sits 0.56 m from a thin diverging lens of focal length −0.4 m. Determine the signed image position v under the real-is-positive sign convention.
items.workedSolution: For a diverging lens, f = −0.4 m. Using 1/f = 1/u + 1/v gives 1/v = −1/0.4 − 1/0.56 = -4.286 m⁻¹, so v = -0.233 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses negative f = −0.4 m in 1/v = 1/f − 1/u to obtain v = -0.233 m (C).

options.distractorRationale: Forgets that a diverging lens has negative focal length f < 0, substituting +|f| into 1/v = 1/f − 1/u.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes the correct magnitude |v| but omits the negative sign required for a virtual image in the real-is-positive convention.

items.stem: In an inertial seismometer calibration trolley, a 1.2 kg mass hangs from a vertical spring of constant 25 N m⁻¹ and executes vertical SHM of amplitude 0.018 m (take g = 9.8 m s⁻²). Calculate the static equilibrium extension Δx_eq from the spring's unstretched length.
items.workedSolution: At static equilibrium, upward spring tension balances weight: k Δx_eq = mg ⇒ Δx_eq = (1.2 × 9.8) / 25 = 0.470 m.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Divides mass m directly by spring constant k without multiplying by gravitational field strength g.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Hooke's law as k / (mg) instead of mg / k.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Adds the oscillation amplitude x₀ to mg / k, finding maximum total stretch rather than static equilibrium extension.

items.stem: A simple pendulum of length 0.95 m and bob mass 0.12 kg in a long-case regulator clock calibration rig executes small-angle oscillations of arc amplitude 0.057 m in a field where g = 9.8 m s⁻². Determine its period T.
items.workedSolution: For small angles, T = 2π√(L / g) = 2π√(0.95 / 9.8) = 1.96 s (independent of bob mass).

markScheme.criterion: Obtains 1.96 s using g = 9.8 m s⁻² (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Swaps L / g and g / L inside the square root, computing 2π√(g / L).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes the half-period π√(L / g) for a single swing from one extreme to the other rather than a complete cycle.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Incorrectly includes the bob mass m inside the pendulum period equation.

items.stem: During calibration of an ultrasonic surgical transducer tip vibrating at f = 2.5 Hz and amplitude 0.06 m, a laser sensor records an instantaneous displacement x = 0.036 m. Determine the signed SHM acceleration a at that instant.
items.workedSolution: Angular frequency ω = 2πf = 2π(2.5) = 15.71 rad s⁻¹. By the defining SHM equation, a = −ω²x = −(15.71)²(0.036) = -8.88 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ω = 2πf and obtains -8.88 m s⁻² (D).

items.stem: Engineers monitoring a piezoelectric laser-mirror dithering stage measure simple harmonic motion of amplitude 0.05 m and angular frequency 8 rad s⁻¹. Determine the speed |v| = ω√(x₀² − x²) at displacement x = 0.025 m.
items.workedSolution: Using v = ω√(x₀² − x²) gives v = 8 × √(0.05² − 0.025²) = 0.346 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into v = ω√(x₀² − x²) to obtain 0.346 m s⁻¹ (D).

options.distractorRationale: Calculates the maximum speed ωx₀ at equilibrium (x = 0) instead of the speed at x.

options.label: C

items.stem: A monochromatic beam with free-space wavelength 780 nm (vacuum speed 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) enters dense flint glass (n₂ = 1.65) from optical crown glass (n₁ = 1.52) at 18° to the interface normal in a precision Abbe refractometer cell. Calculate the optical wavelength in dense flint glass.
items.workedSolution: Wave frequency remains unchanged across the boundary, while phase speed decreases to v₂ = c / n₂. Hence λ₂ = λ₀ / n₂ = 780 / 1.65 = 473 nm.

markScheme.criterion: Uses λ₂ = λ₀ / n₂ = 780 / 1.65 to obtain 473 nm (A).

items.stem: A collimated ray inside synthetic sapphire (n₁ = 1.77, vacuum light speed c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) strikes a flat interface with liquid ethanol (n₂ = 1.36) at 63° to the normal during a microfluidic refractive-index sensor. Through what angle is the ray deviated from its original forward path at this boundary?
items.workedSolution: Since sin θ_c = 1.36 / 1.77 gives θ_c = 50.2° and θ₁ = 63° > θ_c, the beam undergoes total internal reflection with θ_r = 63°. The angular deviation from the original forward direction is δ = 180° − 2(63°) = 54.0°.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies TIR (θ₁ > θ_c = 50.2°) and computes δ = 180° − 2θ₁ = 54.0° (B).

items.stem: In a laboratory autocollimator test rail, a specimen of height 0.015 m is placed 0.096 m in front of a convex magnifying lens of focal length 0.24 m. Calculate the upright virtual image height h_i.
items.workedSolution: From 1/v = 1/0.24 − 1/0.096, v = -0.160 m. Linear magnification m = −v / u = 1.667, so upright image height h_i = m h_o = 0.0250 m.

items.stem: A test rig using a silicon MEMS accelerometer proof-mass flexure test model has mass 1.5 kg, horizontal spring constant 160 N m⁻¹, and oscillation amplitude 0.075 m. What is the natural frequency f of the oscillation?
items.workedSolution: Natural frequency f = (1 / 2π)√(k / m) = (1 / 2π)√(160 / 1.5) = 1.64 Hz.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Swaps k/m and m/k, computing (1 / 2π)√(m / k) instead of (1 / 2π)√(k / m).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Reports angular frequency ω = √(k / m) in rad s⁻¹ without dividing by 2π.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes the period T = 2π√(m / k) instead of frequency f = 1 / T.

items.stem: In a robotics compliant-actuator test carriage, a 0.2 kg mass hangs from a vertical spring of constant 32 N m⁻¹ and executes vertical SHM of amplitude 0.032 m (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Calculate the static equilibrium extension Δx_eq from the spring's unstretched length.
items.workedSolution: At static equilibrium, upward spring tension balances weight: k Δx_eq = mg ⇒ Δx_eq = (0.2 × 9.81) / 32 = 0.0613 m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Divides mass m directly by spring constant k without multiplying by gravitational field strength g.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Adds the oscillation amplitude x₀ to mg / k, finding maximum total stretch rather than static equilibrium extension.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Hooke's law as k / (mg) instead of mg / k.

items.stem: A 0.4 kg pendulum bob suspended from a 1.6 m wire in an evacuated bell-jar precision timing pendulum oscillates in SHM with arc amplitude 0.352 m (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). What is the maximum speed v_max of the bob?
items.workedSolution: Angular frequency ω = √(g / L) = √(9.81 / 1.6), so maximum speed v_max = ω x₀ = 0.872 m s⁻¹.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Treats the horizontal arc amplitude x₀ as a vertical free-fall drop height h in √(2gh).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes ω² x₀ = (g / L) x₀ (maximum acceleration) instead of ω x₀ = √(g / L) x₀.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts g / L inside √(g / L) when computing ω x₀.

items.stem: In a vibrometer calibration shaker table, a stage oscillates in simple harmonic motion with angular frequency ω = 30 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude x₀ = 0.04 m, tracing the velocity–displacement ellipse shown. What is the speed v of the stage when its displacement from equilibrium is x = 0.0144 m?
items.workedSolution: Using v = ω√(x₀² − x²) gives v = 30 × √(0.04² − 0.0144²) = 1.12 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into v = ω√(x₀² − x²) to obtain 1.12 m s⁻¹ (C).

options.distractorRationale: Uses ωx instead of ω√(x₀² − x²), mistakenly assuming speed is directly proportional to displacement.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates ω(x₀ − x) linearly instead of taking √(x₀² − x²).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the maximum speed ωx₀ at equilibrium (x = 0) instead of the speed at x.

items.stem: In a marine wave-tank oscillating piston paddle, a 1.2 kg oscillator moves harmonically at ω = 15 rad s⁻¹ with amplitude x₀ = 0.06 m (sampled at 0.03 m). At what positive displacement x from equilibrium is its kinetic energy equal to its potential energy (E_k = E_p)?
items.workedSolution: Setting E_p = ½E_tot gives ½mω²x² = ½(½mω²x₀²), so x² = x₀² / 2 and x = x₀ / √2 = 0.06 / √2 = 0.0424 m.

markScheme.criterion: Solves x² = x₀² / 2 to obtain x = x₀ / √2 = 0.0424 m (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes (√3 / 2)x₀ (where E_p = ¾E_tot) instead of x₀ / √2.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Assumes E_k = E_p occurs at half the amplitude (x₀ / 2, where E_p = ¼E_tot) instead of x₀ / √2.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Squares the ½ factor to obtain x₀ / 4 instead of taking the square root x₀ / √2.

items.stem: During refractive testing with a photovoltaic encapsulant test coupon, a ray inside a high-index optical block meets a flat layer of fused-silica glass (n₂ = 1.46) and grazes the interface along the boundary when the incident angle to the normal reaches 49.5°. Calculate the block's refractive index n₁.
items.workedSolution: At the critical angle, n₁ sin θ_c = n₂ sin 90° = n₂, so n₁ = 1.46 / sin 49.5° = 1.92.

markScheme.criterion: Computes n₁ = n₂ / sin θ_c = 1.46 / sin 49.5° = 1.92 (C).

items.stem: A parallel-sided optical window of dense flint glass (refractive index 1.65, thickness 0.06 m) immersed in dry air (n₀ = 1) is illuminated at 44° to the normal in an interferometric metrology window. Calculate the transverse shift t₁ tan θ₁ of the ray along the exit boundary.
items.workedSolution: Inside the dense flint glass slab, sin θ₁ = (1 sin 44°) / 1.65, giving θ₁ = 24.9°. The transverse shift along the exit face is Δy = t₁ tan θ₁ = 0.06 × tan 24.90° = 0.0278 m.

items.stem: A monochromatic ray in water of refractive index 1.33 is coupled at 14.7° to the axis into a straight 450 m optical fiber (n_core = 1.58, n_clad = 1.49) during a tethered deep-sea ROV umbilical waveguide. Calculate the total ray path length inside the 450 m fiber.
items.workedSolution: Inside the core, sin θ_axis = (1.33 sin 14.7°) / 1.58 ⇒ θ_axis = 12.3°. The total zig-zag geometric path length is L_ray = L / cos θ_axis = 450 / cos 12.33° = 461 m.

markScheme.criterion: Finds θ_axis = 12.3° and computes L / cos θ_axis = 461 m (D).

items.stem: In a railway trackside acoustic-sensing fiber, light from air (n_ext = 1.00, illustrated at 18.7°) propagates along a 1200 m step-index fiber with n_core = 1.54 and n_clad = 1.45. Taking c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, what is the transit time t_max of the slowest guided ray that meets the core–cladding wall at the critical angle?
items.workedSolution: Wave speed in the core is v = c / n_core, and the critical-angle ray travels path length L / sin θ_c = L (n_core / n_clad). Therefore t_max = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 6.54 × 10⁻⁶ s.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates t_max = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 6.54 × 10⁻⁶ s (D).

items.stem: An observer using a metrology profile-projector optical train adjusts the position of a 0.008 m scale mark in front of a thin convex lens of focal length 0.12 m until its virtual image lies at the near point 0.360 m on the object side of the lens (v = −0.360 m). Calculate the object distance u.
items.workedSolution: For a virtual image in the real-is-positive convention, v = -0.360 m. Thus 1/u = 1/f − 1/v = 1/0.12 − (1/-0.3600) = 11.11 m⁻¹, giving u = 0.0900 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes negative v = -0.360 m into 1/u = 1/f − 1/v to obtain u = 0.0900 m (D).

items.stem: In a wide-angle security peephole assembly, an object of height 0.036 m is positioned 0.56 m from a concave lens of focal length −0.4 m. Calculate the signed linear magnification m = h_i / h_o = −v / u.
items.workedSolution: With f = −0.4 m, 1/v = −1/0.4 − 1/0.56 gives v = -0.233 m. Therefore m = −v / u = −(-0.2333) / 0.56 = 0.417 (upright and diminished).

markScheme.criterion: Finds v = -0.233 m and m = −v / u = 0.417 (C).

options.label: B

items.stem: A 0.6 kg mass suspended vertically from a spring of stiffness 64 N m⁻¹ in a university mechanics oscillation sled is pulled down 0.055 m below equilibrium and released (take g = 9.8 m s⁻²). What is the period T of the resulting vertical simple harmonic motion?
items.workedSolution: Gravity shifts the equilibrium position without altering effective stiffness k, so T = 2π√(m / k) = 2π√(0.6 / 64) = 0.608 s.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes the oscillation amplitude x₀ into a pendulum-style formula 2π√(x₀ / g) instead of 2π√(m / k).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Incorrectly adds weight mg to spring stiffness k, assuming gravity changes the vertical mass-spring period.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Swaps m/k and k/m inside the square root.

items.stem: On a Foucault-style brass sphere suspension apparatus, a simple pendulum with a 0.35 kg bob swings through a small arc amplitude of 0.105 m with a measured period of 2.66 s. Taking g = 9.8 m s⁻², what is the effective length L of the pendulum?

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Forgets to square T / (2π) when rearranging T = 2π√(L / g), computing gT / (2π).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Divides gT² by 2π instead of 4π².

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the rearranged expression for L.

items.stem: The acceleration–displacement line shown models an atomic-force microscope cantilever tip oscillating harmonically at 6 Hz with amplitude 0.06 m. Using a = −ω²x, calculate the signed acceleration at displacement x = -0.036 m.
items.workedSolution: Angular frequency ω = 2πf = 2π(6) = 37.70 rad s⁻¹. By the defining SHM equation, a = −ω²x = −(37.70)²(-0.036) = 51.2 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ω = 2πf and obtains 51.2 m s⁻² (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Omits the restoring minus sign in a = −ω²x, giving acceleration in the same sign as displacement instead of toward equilibrium.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates −ωx instead of −ω²x, forgetting to square the angular frequency.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes cyclic frequency f directly for angular frequency ω, computing −f²x instead of −(2πf)²x.

items.stem: A 0.15 kg resonator in a dynamic mechanical thermal-analyzer probe executes simple harmonic motion of amplitude 0.12 m and angular frequency ω = 12 rad s⁻¹ (probed at x = 0.06 m). At what cyclic frequency f_E does its kinetic energy oscillate with time?
items.workedSolution: Mechanical frequency f = ω / (2π) = 12 / (2π) = 1.910 Hz. Because kinetic energy reaches a maximum twice per mechanical period, f_E = 2f = ω / π = 3.82 Hz.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates 2ω in rad s⁻¹ without dividing by 2π to convert to hertz.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Gives the mechanical displacement frequency f = ω / (2π) instead of recognizing that E_k ∝ cos²(ωt) oscillates at 2f.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Halves the mechanical frequency instead of doubling it.

items.stem: In an immersion-microscopy optical stage, a narrow optical ray travelling in distilled water (refractive index 1.33) meets a polished dielectric block at 48° to the normal and refracts to an angle of 36.8° to the normal inside the block. Determine the refractive index n₂ of the block.
items.workedSolution: Rearranging Snell's law n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂ gives n₂ = 1.33 × sin 48° / sin 36.8° = 1.65.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates n₂ = n₁ sin θ₁ / sin θ₂ = 1.65 (C).

items.stem: Engineers aligning a spectrophotometer cuvette wall pass a narrow beam in distilled water (n₀ = 1.33) through a flat crystalline zircon window (n₁ = 1.92, thickness 0.03 m) at 26° to the normal into distilled water. Determine the perpendicular lateral displacement of the transmitted beam.
items.workedSolution: By Snell's law, sin θ₁ = (1.33 sin 26°) / 1.92 ⇒ θ₁ = 17.7°. The perpendicular lateral displacement of the emergent ray is d = t₁ sin(θ₀ − θ₁) / cos θ₁ = 0.00456 m.

items.stem: In an industrial laser-welding delivery cable, a straight step-index fiber of length 120 m has core index n_core = 1.48 and cladding index n_clad = 1.41. A test ray enters the flat end-face from air (n_ext = 1.00) at a steep angle θ_in = 38.7° to the fiber axis, exceeding the acceptance cone so light refracts into the cladding. What is the angle of refraction in the cladding measured from the core–cladding wall normal?
items.workedSolution: At entry, sin θ_axis = (1 sin 38.7°) / 1.48 ⇒ θ_axis = 25.0°. The angle to the wall normal is θ_w = 90° − θ_axis = 65.0° (< θ_c = 72.3°). Refracting into the cladding: sin θ_clad = (1.48 sin θ_w) / 1.41, giving θ_clad = 72.1°.

markScheme.criterion: Finds θ_w = 65.0° and refracts into cladding to obtain 72.1° (D).

items.stem: Engineers evaluating bit-rate limits for a cryogenic laboratory optical feedthrough test a 750 m step-index waveguide (n_core = 1.57, n_clad = 1.46, n_ext = 1.00, ray shown at 24.7°). Take c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹. Determine the multipath dispersion delay Δt between extreme guided rays and axial rays.
items.workedSolution: Axial transit time t_min = n_core L / c = (1.57 × 750) / (3.00 × 10⁸) = 3.92 × 10⁻⁶ s. At the critical angle sin θ_c = n_clad / n_core, t_max = t_min / sin θ_c = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 4.22 × 10⁻⁶ s. Modal delay Δt = t_max − t_min = 2.96 × 10⁻⁷ s.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δt = (n_core L / c)(n_core / n_clad − 1) = 2.96 × 10⁻⁷ s (C).

items.stem: A concave diverging lens with focal length f = −0.1 m in an optical-bench virtual-image calibration rig forms an image of an object of height 0.045 m placed at object distance u = 0.18 m. Using 1/f = 1/u + 1/v, calculate the signed image distance v.
items.workedSolution: For a diverging lens, f = −0.1 m. Using 1/f = 1/u + 1/v gives 1/v = −1/0.1 − 1/0.18 = -15.56 m⁻¹, so v = -0.0643 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses negative f = −0.1 m in 1/v = 1/f − 1/u to obtain v = -0.0643 m (B).

items.stem: Engineers testing a structural vibration-isolation test sled on linear bearings measure a moving mass of 0.45 kg attached to an ideal horizontal spring of constant 120 N m⁻¹ oscillating with amplitude 0.035 m. Determine the period T of one complete cycle.
items.workedSolution: For an ideal mass-spring oscillator, T = 2π√(m / k) = 2π√(0.45 / 120) = 0.385 s.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 2π and calculates √(m / k) = 1 / ω.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the square root and evaluates 2π(m / k).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Swaps m/k and k/m inside the radical, computing 2π√(k / m) instead of 2π√(m / k).

items.stem: A simple pendulum of length 1.15 m and bob mass 0.25 kg in a skyscraper tuned-pendulum damper scale model executes small-angle oscillations of arc amplitude 0.115 m in a field where g = 9.8 m s⁻². Determine its period T.
items.workedSolution: For small angles, T = 2π√(L / g) = 2π√(1.15 / 9.8) = 2.15 s (independent of bob mass).

markScheme.criterion: Obtains 2.15 s using g = 9.8 m s⁻² (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Swaps L / g and g / L inside the square root, computing 2π√(g / L).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes the half-period π√(L / g) for a single swing from one extreme to the other rather than a complete cycle.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the square root and evaluates 2πL / g.

items.stem: A 0.6 kg brass bob on a 1.6 m suspension wire in a museum horology restoration pendulum rig oscillates with arc-length amplitude 0.4 m (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Calculate the maximum cord tension at the bottom of the swing.
items.workedSolution: With ω = √(g / L) = √(9.81 / 1.6), peak speed v_max = ω x₀ = 0.990 m s⁻¹. At the lowest point, T_cord = m(g + v_max² / L) = 6.25 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_max = ω x₀ and T_cord = mg + mv_max² / L = 6.25 N (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates only the net radial centripetal force mv_max² / L rather than the total cord tension.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Equates cord tension at the lowest point to static weight mg, ignoring the upward centripetal force mv_max² / L.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts the centripetal force mv_max² / L from mg instead of adding it at the bottom of the arc.

items.stem: A harmonic oscillator in a precision optical-chopper resonant blade moves with amplitude x₀ = 0.08 m and angular frequency ω = 16 rad s⁻¹. Calculate its speed when passing through displacement x = 0.064 m.
items.workedSolution: Using v = ω√(x₀² − x²) gives v = 16 × √(0.08² − 0.064²) = 0.768 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into v = ω√(x₀² − x²) to obtain 0.768 m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: The parabolic SHM energy graph shown corresponds to a magnetic-levitation harmonic test puck (mass 0.15 kg, angular frequency 25 rad s⁻¹, amplitude 0.1 m). Calculate the kinetic energy E_k at displacement x = 0.06 m.
items.workedSolution: Using E_k = ½mω²(x₀² − x²) gives E_k = 0.5 × 0.15 × 25² × (0.1² − 0.06²) = 0.300 J.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the potential energy ½mω²x² at x rather than the kinetic energy ½mω²(x₀² − x²).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Interpolates energy linearly as E_tot(1 − x / x₀) instead of quadratically as E_tot(1 − x² / x₀²).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes the total mechanical energy ½mω²x₀² instead of subtracting potential energy at x.

items.stem: Engineers designing a beam-turning prism on a submarine periscope window assembly send a ray in polycarbonate polymer (n₁ = 1.58, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) onto distilled water (n₂ = 1.33) at 66° to the normal. What is the angular deflection δ between the incident direction and the emerging reflected ray?
items.workedSolution: Since sin θ_c = 1.33 / 1.58 gives θ_c = 57.3° and θ₁ = 66° > θ_c, the beam undergoes total internal reflection with θ_r = 66°. The angular deviation from the original forward direction is δ = 180° − 2(66°) = 48.0°.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies TIR (θ₁ > θ_c = 57.3°) and computes δ = 180° − 2θ₁ = 48.0° (B).

items.stem: During alignment of an avionics fly-by-light data bus, monochromatic light from water (n_ext = 1.33) strikes the entry face of a 350 m step-index fiber (n_core = 1.58, n_clad = 1.49) at 15.6° to the central optic axis. Determine the angle of incidence θ_w at the cylindrical core–cladding boundary relative to its normal.
items.workedSolution: At the entry face, 1.33 sin 15.6° = 1.58 sin θ_axis ⇒ θ_axis = 13.1°. Since the core wall is parallel to the axis, its normal is perpendicular to the axis, giving θ_w = 90° − θ_axis = 76.9°.

items.stem: In a botanical loupe magnifier bench, a specimen of height 0.008 m is placed 0.1875 m in front of a convex magnifying lens of focal length 0.25 m. Calculate the upright virtual image height h_i.
items.workedSolution: From 1/v = 1/0.25 − 1/0.1875, v = -0.750 m. Linear magnification m = −v / u = 4.000, so upright image height h_i = m h_o = 0.0320 m.

items.stem: In a calibration run of a spacecraft thruster-valve return-spring test fixture, a 1.5 kg carriage oscillates horizontally with amplitude 0.035 m on a spring of stiffness 160 N m⁻¹. Determine the frequency f in hertz.
items.workedSolution: Natural frequency f = (1 / 2π)√(k / m) = (1 / 2π)√(160 / 1.5) = 1.64 Hz.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Reports angular frequency ω = √(k / m) in rad s⁻¹ without dividing by 2π.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Swaps k/m and m/k, computing (1 / 2π)√(m / k) instead of (1 / 2π)√(k / m).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes the period T = 2π√(m / k) instead of frequency f = 1 / T.

items.stem: A vertical helical spring of stiffness 40 N m⁻¹ in a precision gravimeter spring-mass test stage suspends a load of mass 0.3 kg that subsequently oscillates vertically with amplitude 0.018 m. Taking g = 9.8 m s⁻², what was the static extension Δx_eq of the spring at equilibrium before oscillation started?
items.workedSolution: At static equilibrium, upward spring tension balances weight: k Δx_eq = mg ⇒ Δx_eq = (0.3 × 9.8) / 40 = 0.0735 m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Hooke's law as k / (mg) instead of mg / k.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Adds the oscillation amplitude x₀ to mg / k, finding maximum total stretch rather than static equilibrium extension.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides mass m directly by spring constant k without multiplying by gravitational field strength g.

items.stem: A 0.15 kg pendulum bob suspended from a 1.9 m wire in a physics laboratory light-gate timing pendulum oscillates in SHM with arc amplitude 0.475 m (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). What is the maximum speed v_max of the bob?
items.workedSolution: Angular frequency ω = √(g / L) = √(9.81 / 1.9), so maximum speed v_max = ω x₀ = 1.08 m s⁻¹.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes ω² x₀ = (g / L) x₀ (maximum acceleration) instead of ω x₀ = √(g / L) x₀.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Treats the horizontal arc amplitude x₀ as a vertical free-fall drop height h in √(2gh).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts g / L inside √(g / L) when computing ω x₀.

items.stem: In a piezoelectric laser-mirror dithering stage, a component executes simple harmonic motion at frequency f = 5 Hz with amplitude x₀ = 0.03 m, as represented on the acceleration–displacement graph. Taking displacement to the right as positive, what is its signed acceleration a when x = 0.0135 m?
items.workedSolution: Angular frequency ω = 2πf = 2π(5) = 31.42 rad s⁻¹. By the defining SHM equation, a = −ω²x = −(31.42)²(0.0135) = -13.3 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ω = 2πf and obtains -13.3 m s⁻² (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes cyclic frequency f directly for angular frequency ω, computing −f²x instead of −(2πf)²x.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the restoring minus sign in a = −ω²x, giving acceleration in the same sign as displacement instead of toward equilibrium.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates −ωx instead of −ω²x, forgetting to square the angular frequency.

items.stem: In an ultrasonic wire-bonding horn tip, a 0.25 kg oscillator moves harmonically at ω = 18 rad s⁻¹ with amplitude x₀ = 0.12 m (sampled at 0.048 m). At what positive displacement x from equilibrium is its kinetic energy equal to its potential energy (E_k = E_p)?
items.workedSolution: Setting E_p = ½E_tot gives ½mω²x² = ½(½mω²x₀²), so x² = x₀² / 2 and x = x₀ / √2 = 0.12 / √2 = 0.0849 m.

markScheme.criterion: Solves x² = x₀² / 2 to obtain x = x₀ / √2 = 0.0849 m (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Assumes E_k = E_p occurs at half the amplitude (x₀ / 2, where E_p = ¼E_tot) instead of x₀ / √2.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Squares the ½ factor to obtain x₀ / 4 instead of taking the square root x₀ / √2.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes (√3 / 2)x₀ (where E_p = ¾E_tot) instead of x₀ / √2.

items.stem: A monochromatic beam with free-space wavelength 405 nm (vacuum speed 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) enters liquid ethanol (n₂ = 1.36) from polycarbonate polymer (n₁ = 1.58) at 34° to the interface normal in a photovoltaic encapsulant test coupon. Calculate the optical wavelength in liquid ethanol.
items.workedSolution: Wave frequency remains unchanged across the boundary, while phase speed decreases to v₂ = c / n₂. Hence λ₂ = λ₀ / n₂ = 405 / 1.36 = 298 nm.

markScheme.criterion: Uses λ₂ = λ₀ / n₂ = 405 / 1.36 to obtain 298 nm (B).

items.stem: On a deep-ocean optical hydrophone window, a narrow beam in dry air (n₀ = 1) hits a parallel-sided plate of dense flint glass (n₁ = 1.65, thickness 0.03 m) surrounded by dry air at 26° to the normal. By what distance along the exit face is the ray's exit point shifted from the normal through the entry point?
items.workedSolution: Inside the dense flint glass slab, sin θ₁ = (1 sin 26°) / 1.65, giving θ₁ = 15.4°. The transverse shift along the exit face is Δy = t₁ tan θ₁ = 0.03 × tan 15.41° = 0.00827 m.

items.stem: Engineers specifying a borehole geophysical telemetry line test a 350 m step-index optical fiber having n_core = 1.58 and n_clad = 1.49 under a 11.1° test beam from air (n_ext = 1.00). Calculate the minimum angle of incidence to the wall normal required for total internal reflection inside the core.
items.workedSolution: At the core–cladding boundary, sin θ_c = n_clad / n_core = 1.49 / 1.58 = 0.9430, giving θ_c = 70.6°.

items.stem: A 360 m multimode step-index cable in a fusion-chamber diagnostic optical relay has core index 1.52 and cladding index 1.46 in air (n_ext = 1.00, sample launch angle 12.5°, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹). Calculate the maximum guided transit time through the fiber.
items.workedSolution: Wave speed in the core is v = c / n_core, and the critical-angle ray travels path length L / sin θ_c = L (n_core / n_clad). Therefore t_max = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 1.90 × 10⁻⁶ s.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates t_max = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 1.90 × 10⁻⁶ s (A).

items.stem: In a museum conservation inspection magnifier, a thin converging lens of focal length 0.1 m is used as a simple magnifier so that an object of height 0.015 m forms an upright virtual image 0.0667 m in front of the lens (v = −0.0667 m in the real-is-positive convention). At what object distance u in front of the lens is the object held?
items.workedSolution: For a virtual image in the real-is-positive convention, v = -0.0667 m. Thus 1/u = 1/f − 1/v = 1/0.1 − (1/-0.06667) = 25.00 m⁻¹, giving u = 0.0400 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes negative v = -0.0667 m into 1/u = 1/f − 1/v to obtain u = 0.0400 m (C).

items.stem: A thin diverging lens of focal length f = −0.2 m in a clinical optometry phoropter test cell forms a virtual image of an upright object of height 0.05 m placed at u = 0.6 m. What is the linear magnification m = −v / u of the image?
items.workedSolution: With f = −0.2 m, 1/v = −1/0.2 − 1/0.6 gives v = -0.150 m. Therefore m = −v / u = −(-0.1500) / 0.6 = 0.250 (upright and diminished).

markScheme.criterion: Finds v = -0.150 m and m = −v / u = 0.250 (C).

items.stem: A 0.75 kg mass suspended vertically from a spring of stiffness 50 N m⁻¹ in an acoustic transducer moving-coil suspension rig is pulled down 0.018 m below equilibrium and released (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). What is the period T of the resulting vertical simple harmonic motion?
items.workedSolution: Gravity shifts the equilibrium position without altering effective stiffness k, so T = 2π√(m / k) = 2π√(0.75 / 50) = 0.770 s.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Swaps m/k and k/m inside the square root.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes the oscillation amplitude x₀ into a pendulum-style formula 2π√(x₀ / g) instead of 2π√(m / k).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Incorrectly adds weight mg to spring stiffness k, assuming gravity changes the vertical mass-spring period.

items.stem: To calibrate a lecture-hall rigid-ceiling wire pendulum where g = 9.8 m s⁻², a 0.18 kg pendulum bob oscillates at small arc amplitude 0.0936 m with period T = 1.77 s. Calculate the pendulum length L.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Divides gT² by 2π instead of 4π².

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Forgets to square T / (2π) when rearranging T = 2π√(L / g), computing gT / (2π).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the rearranged expression for L.

items.stem: In a vibrometer calibration shaker table, an oscillator undergoes SHM at 1.5 Hz with amplitude 0.1 m (passing through x = -0.075 m). Calculate the peak acceleration magnitude a_max = (2πf)² x₀.
items.workedSolution: With ω = 2π(1.5) = 9.425 rad s⁻¹, maximum acceleration magnitude a_max = ω² x₀ = 8.88 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ω = 2πf and obtains 8.88 m s⁻² (D).

items.stem: The velocity–displacement phase portrait shown represents a marine wave-tank oscillating piston paddle oscillating with ω = 20 rad s⁻¹ and x₀ = 0.12 m. Find the oscillator's speed at x = 0.0432 m.
items.workedSolution: Using v = ω√(x₀² − x²) gives v = 20 × √(0.12² − 0.0432²) = 2.24 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into v = ω√(x₀² − x²) to obtain 2.24 m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: In a submarine periscope window assembly, light of vacuum wavelength 589 nm (speed in vacuum c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) crosses a flat boundary from liquid ethanol (n₁ = 1.36) into optical diamond (n₂ = 2.42) with incident angle 26°. Determine the wave speed in optical diamond.
items.workedSolution: From the definition of refractive index n₂ = c / v₂, the wave speed in optical diamond is v₂ = (3.00 × 10⁸) / 2.42 = 1.24 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Computes v₂ = c / n₂ = 3.00 × 10⁸ / 2.42 = 1.24 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹ (B).

options.distractorRationale: Calculates the wave speed v₁ = c / n₁ in the first medium rather than v₂ in the second medium.

items.stem: Within a spectrophotometer cuvette wall, monochromatic light (vacuum speed 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) propagating in crystalline zircon (n₁ = 1.92) is incident at 58° to the normal on liquid ethanol (n₂ = 1.36). Determine the critical angle θ_c between these two media.
items.workedSolution: At the critical angle θ_c, sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1.36 / 1.92 = 0.7083, giving θ_c = arcsin(0.7083) = 45.1°.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1.36 / 1.92 to obtain θ_c = 45.1° (C).

items.stem: A 350 m step-index optical fiber used in a short-reach datacenter patch cord has core refractive index 1.49 and cladding refractive index 1.39. A laser ray in air (n_ext = 1.00) enters the center of the flat end-face at θ_in = 14° to the fiber axis. What angle of incidence θ_w does the refracted ray make with the normal to the core–cladding wall?
items.workedSolution: At the entry face, 1 sin 14° = 1.49 sin θ_axis ⇒ θ_axis = 9.34°. Since the core wall is parallel to the axis, its normal is perpendicular to the axis, giving θ_w = 90° − θ_axis = 80.7°.

items.stem: In a cryogenic laboratory optical feedthrough, a 750 m step-index waveguide with n_core = 1.57 and n_clad = 1.46 receives light from air of refractive index 1.00 (shown for a 22.2° ray). Determine the maximum external incidence angle θ_max to the axis that still achieves total internal reflection at the core wall.
items.workedSolution: At the grazing limit, sin θ_c = 1.46 / 1.57, so inside the core sin θ_axis,max = cos θ_c = √(1 − (n_clad / n_core)²). By Snell's law at the entry face, n_ext sin θ_max = √(n_core² − n_clad²) = 0.5773, giving θ_max = arcsin(0.5773) = 35.3°.

markScheme.criterion: Uses n_ext sin θ_max = √(n_core² − n_clad²) to obtain θ_max = 35.3° (C).

items.stem: A concave diverging lens with focal length f = −0.25 m in a pulsed-laser divergence compensator forms an image of an object of height 0.02 m placed at object distance u = 0.2 m. Using 1/f = 1/u + 1/v, calculate the signed image distance v.
items.workedSolution: For a diverging lens, f = −0.25 m. Using 1/f = 1/u + 1/v gives 1/v = −1/0.25 − 1/0.2 = -9.000 m⁻¹, so v = -0.111 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses negative f = −0.25 m in 1/v = 1/f − 1/u to obtain v = -0.111 m (B).

options.label: C

items.stem: In a robotics compliant-actuator test carriage of mass 0.12 kg and spring constant 120 N m⁻¹, the oscillator is displaced by an amplitude of 0.09 m from equilibrium and released. What is the period T of its simple harmonic motion?
items.workedSolution: For an ideal mass-spring oscillator, T = 2π√(m / k) = 2π√(0.12 / 120) = 0.199 s.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Omits the square root and evaluates 2π(m / k).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 2π and calculates √(m / k) = 1 / ω.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Swaps m/k and k/m inside the radical, computing 2π√(k / m) instead of 2π√(m / k).

items.stem: A simple pendulum of length 0.95 m and bob mass 0.18 kg in an evacuated bell-jar precision timing pendulum executes small-angle oscillations of arc amplitude 0.057 m in a field where g = 9.8 m s⁻². Determine its period T.
items.workedSolution: For small angles, T = 2π√(L / g) = 2π√(0.95 / 9.8) = 1.96 s (independent of bob mass).

markScheme.criterion: Obtains 1.96 s using g = 9.8 m s⁻² (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes the half-period π√(L / g) for a single swing from one extreme to the other rather than a complete cycle.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Swaps L / g and g / L inside the square root, computing 2π√(g / L).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Incorrectly includes the bob mass m inside the pendulum period equation.

items.stem: In a mine-shaft gravity-anomaly survey pendulum, a pendulum bob of mass 0.15 kg hangs on a light cord of length 1.3 m and swings in small-angle SHM with arc amplitude 0.325 m. Taking g = 9.81 m s⁻², what is the tension in the cord as the bob passes through its lowest equilibrium point?
items.workedSolution: With ω = √(g / L) = √(9.81 / 1.3), peak speed v_max = ω x₀ = 0.893 m s⁻¹. At the lowest point, T_cord = m(g + v_max² / L) = 1.56 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_max = ω x₀ and T_cord = mg + mv_max² / L = 1.56 N (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Equates cord tension at the lowest point to static weight mg, ignoring the upward centripetal force mv_max² / L.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts the centripetal force mv_max² / L from mg instead of adding it at the bottom of the arc.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates only the net radial centripetal force mv_max² / L rather than the total cord tension.

items.stem: A harmonic oscillator in a dynamic mechanical thermal-analyzer probe moves with amplitude x₀ = 0.1 m and angular frequency ω = 8 rad s⁻¹. Calculate its speed when passing through displacement x = 0.036 m.
items.workedSolution: Using v = ω√(x₀² − x²) gives v = 8 × √(0.1² − 0.036²) = 0.746 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into v = ω√(x₀² − x²) to obtain 0.746 m s⁻¹ (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses ωx instead of ω√(x₀² − x²), mistakenly assuming speed is directly proportional to displacement.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates ω(x₀ − x) linearly instead of taking √(x₀² − x²).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the maximum speed ωx₀ at equilibrium (x = 0) instead of the speed at x.

items.stem: In a scanning-probe interferometric calibration stage, an oscillating body of mass 0.4 kg executes simple harmonic motion with angular frequency ω = 10 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude x₀ = 0.14 m. What is its kinetic energy E_k when its displacement from equilibrium is x = 0.084 m?
items.workedSolution: Using E_k = ½mω²(x₀² − x²) gives E_k = 0.5 × 0.4 × 10² × (0.14² − 0.084²) = 0.251 J.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the potential energy ½mω²x² at x rather than the kinetic energy ½mω²(x₀² − x²).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Interpolates energy linearly as E_tot(1 − x / x₀) instead of quadratically as E_tot(1 − x² / x₀²).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes the total mechanical energy ½mω²x₀² instead of subtracting potential energy at x.

items.stem: In an ophthalmic lens-blank inspection jig, an optical beam propagating in optical diamond (n₁ = 2.42, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) meets a planar distilled water boundary (n₂ = 1.33) at an angle of incidence of 50° to the normal. Calculate the angular deviation of the beam produced at the interface.
items.workedSolution: Since sin θ_c = 1.33 / 2.42 gives θ_c = 33.3° and θ₁ = 50° > θ_c, the beam undergoes total internal reflection with θ_r = 50°. The angular deviation from the original forward direction is δ = 180° − 2(50°) = 80.0°.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies TIR (θ₁ > θ_c = 33.3°) and computes δ = 180° − 2θ₁ = 80.0° (B).

options.distractorRationale: Calculates the angle 2θ₁ between the reversed incident ray and the reflected ray rather than the forward deviation 180° − 2θ₁.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Gives the angle of reflection θ_r = θ₁ instead of the angular deflection from the original travel direction.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates only the single glancing angle 90° − θ₁ to the interface rather than twice the glancing angle 180° − 2θ₁.

items.stem: An immersion viewing window on a planetary lander atmospheric nephelometer consists of a uniform dense flint glass slab of refractive index 1.65 and thickness 0.065 m separating dry air (n₀ = 1) from liquid ethanol (n₂ = 1.36). A narrow beam enters from dry air at 28° to the normal. Calculate the emergent angle in liquid ethanol.
items.workedSolution: Across parallel planar boundaries, n₀ sin θ₀ = n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂. Thus sin θ₂ = (1 × sin 28°) / 1.36, giving θ₂ = 20.2°.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Snell invariant n₀ sin θ₀ = n₂ sin θ₂ to obtain θ₂ = 20.2° (A).

items.stem: Engineers evaluating bit-rate limits for an autonomous lidar reference delay spool test a 750 m step-index waveguide (n_core = 1.48, n_clad = 1.41, n_ext = 1.00, ray shown at 18.7°). Take c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹. Determine the multipath dispersion delay Δt between extreme guided rays and axial rays.
items.workedSolution: Axial transit time t_min = n_core L / c = (1.48 × 750) / (3.00 × 10⁸) = 3.70 × 10⁻⁶ s. At the critical angle sin θ_c = n_clad / n_core, t_max = t_min / sin θ_c = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 3.88 × 10⁻⁶ s. Modal delay Δt = t_max − t_min = 1.84 × 10⁻⁷ s.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δt = (n_core L / c)(n_core / n_clad − 1) = 1.84 × 10⁻⁷ s (B).

items.stem: A thin converging inspection lens of focal length 0.2 m in a retinal fundus imaging objective rig views an upright feature of height 0.018 m held at object distance u = 0.136 m (< f). What is the height h_i of the virtual upright image?
items.workedSolution: From 1/v = 1/0.2 − 1/0.136, v = -0.425 m. Linear magnification m = −v / u = 3.125, so upright image height h_i = m h_o = 0.0562 m.

items.stem: In an underwater dome-port virtual-image corrector, an upright test object of height 0.045 m stands 0.16 m in front of a thin diverging lens of focal length magnitude 0.2 m (f = −0.2 m in the real-is-positive convention). What is the signed image distance v?
items.workedSolution: For a diverging lens, f = −0.2 m. Using 1/f = 1/u + 1/v gives 1/v = −1/0.2 − 1/0.16 = -11.25 m⁻¹, so v = -0.0889 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses negative f = −0.2 m in 1/v = 1/f − 1/u to obtain v = -0.0889 m (C).

items.stem: A vertical helical spring of stiffness 32 N m⁻¹ in an orbital microgravity mass-measurement spring chair suspends a load of mass 0.9 kg that subsequently oscillates vertically with amplitude 0.018 m. Taking g = 9.81 m s⁻², what was the static extension Δx_eq of the spring at equilibrium before oscillation started?
items.workedSolution: At static equilibrium, upward spring tension balances weight: k Δx_eq = mg ⇒ Δx_eq = (0.9 × 9.81) / 32 = 0.276 m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Hooke's law as k / (mg) instead of mg / k.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Divides mass m directly by spring constant k without multiplying by gravitational field strength g.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Adds the oscillation amplitude x₀ to mg / k, finding maximum total stretch rather than static equilibrium extension.

items.stem: In an astronomical observatory sidereal regulator pendulum, a simple pendulum of length 0.55 m and bob mass 0.6 kg swings with small arc amplitude 0.154 m where g = 9.81 m s⁻². Calculate its speed at the equilibrium position.
items.workedSolution: Angular frequency ω = √(g / L) = √(9.81 / 0.55), so maximum speed v_max = ω x₀ = 0.650 m s⁻¹.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Treats the horizontal arc amplitude x₀ as a vertical free-fall drop height h in √(2gh).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes ω² x₀ = (g / L) x₀ (maximum acceleration) instead of ω x₀ = √(g / L) x₀.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts g / L inside √(g / L) when computing ω x₀.

items.stem: A vibrating element in a precision optical-chopper resonant blade executes simple harmonic motion of frequency 2.5 Hz and amplitude 0.06 m (sampled at x = 0.027 m). What is the magnitude a_max of its maximum acceleration?
items.workedSolution: With ω = 2π(2.5) = 15.71 rad s⁻¹, maximum acceleration magnitude a_max = ω² x₀ = 14.8 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ω = 2πf and obtains 14.8 m s⁻² (C).

options.distractorRationale: Calculates ω x₀ (maximum speed) instead of ω² x₀ (maximum acceleration).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes the acceleration magnitude at x rather than at maximum displacement x₀.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor (2π)² = 4π² and computes f² x₀.

items.stem: In a diesel injector needle-valve harmonic test rig, a 0.4 kg oscillator moves harmonically at ω = 18 rad s⁻¹ with amplitude x₀ = 0.14 m (sampled at 0.112 m). At what positive displacement x from equilibrium is its kinetic energy equal to its potential energy (E_k = E_p)?
items.workedSolution: Setting E_p = ½E_tot gives ½mω²x² = ½(½mω²x₀²), so x² = x₀² / 2 and x = x₀ / √2 = 0.14 / √2 = 0.0990 m.

markScheme.criterion: Solves x² = x₀² / 2 to obtain x = x₀ / √2 = 0.0990 m (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes (√3 / 2)x₀ (where E_p = ¾E_tot) instead of x₀ / √2.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Assumes E_k = E_p occurs at half the amplitude (x₀ / 2, where E_p = ¼E_tot) instead of x₀ / √2.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Squares the ½ factor to obtain x₀ / 4 instead of taking the square root x₀ / √2.

items.stem: A collimated optical ray of free-space wavelength 650 nm (c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) in synthetic sapphire (n₁ = 1.77) is incident at 42° to the normal on a smooth liquid ethanol surface (n₂ = 1.36) within a submarine periscope window assembly. Determine the angle of refraction θ₂.
items.workedSolution: By Snell's law, n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂, so sin θ₂ = (1.77 × sin 42°) / 1.36 = 0.8709. Taking the inverse sine gives θ₂ = 60.6°.

markScheme.criterion: Applies n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂ to obtain θ₂ = 60.6° (C).

items.stem: On a clinical corneal pachymetry test phantom, a narrow beam in dry air (n₀ = 1) hits a parallel-sided plate of crystalline zircon (n₁ = 1.92, thickness 0.085 m) surrounded by dry air at 38° to the normal. By what distance along the exit face is the ray's exit point shifted from the normal through the entry point?
items.workedSolution: Inside the crystalline zircon slab, sin θ₁ = (1 sin 38°) / 1.92, giving θ₁ = 18.7°. The transverse shift along the exit face is Δy = t₁ tan θ₁ = 0.085 × tan 18.70° = 0.0288 m.

items.stem: During alignment of an astronomical echelle-spectrograph feed, monochromatic light from air (n_ext = 1.00) strikes the entry face of a 40 m step-index fiber (n_core = 1.5, n_clad = 1.44) at 14.7° to the central optic axis. Determine the angle of incidence θ_w at the cylindrical core–cladding boundary relative to its normal.
items.workedSolution: At the entry face, 1 sin 14.7° = 1.5 sin θ_axis ⇒ θ_axis = 9.74°. Since the core wall is parallel to the axis, its normal is perpendicular to the axis, giving θ_w = 90° − θ_axis = 80.3°.

items.stem: In a subterranean pipeline temperature-sensing cable, light from air (n_ext = 1.00, illustrated at 13.5°) propagates along a 900 m step-index fiber with n_core = 1.6 and n_clad = 1.5. Taking c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, what is the transit time t_max of the slowest guided ray that meets the core–cladding wall at the critical angle?
items.workedSolution: Wave speed in the core is v = c / n_core, and the critical-angle ray travels path length L / sin θ_c = L (n_core / n_clad). Therefore t_max = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 5.12 × 10⁻⁶ s.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates t_max = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 5.12 × 10⁻⁶ s (A).

items.stem: In a heads-up display collimating negative element, an object of height 0.03 m is positioned 0.6 m from a concave lens of focal length −0.4 m. Calculate the signed linear magnification m = h_i / h_o = −v / u.
items.workedSolution: With f = −0.4 m, 1/v = −1/0.4 − 1/0.6 gives v = -0.240 m. Therefore m = −v / u = −(-0.2400) / 0.6 = 0.400 (upright and diminished).

markScheme.criterion: Finds v = -0.240 m and m = −v / u = 0.400 (C).

items.stem: A 0.64 kg test mass in a railway bogie secondary-suspension scale model executes horizontal simple harmonic motion of amplitude 0.11 m and period T = 1.34 s. Calculate the stiffness k of the spring.
items.workedSolution: Rearranging T = 2π√(m / k) gives k = 4π²m / T² = 4π²(0.64) / (1.34)² = 14.0 N m⁻¹.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts m / T² when rearranging the period equation.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Fails to square 2π / T when rearranging T = 2π√(m / k), computing 2πm / T instead of 4π²m / T².

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 4π² and computes m / T².

items.stem: On a museum horology restoration pendulum rig, a simple pendulum with a 0.18 kg bob swings through a small arc amplitude of 0.21 m with a measured period of 2.66 s. Taking g = 9.8 m s⁻², what is the effective length L of the pendulum?

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the rearranged expression for L.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Forgets to square T / (2π) when rearranging T = 2π√(L / g), computing gT / (2π).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides gT² by 2π instead of 4π².

items.stem: The acceleration–displacement line shown models a micro-electro-mechanical resonant beam oscillating harmonically at 4 Hz with amplitude 0.03 m. Using a = −ω²x, calculate the signed acceleration at displacement x = -0.0225 m.
items.workedSolution: Angular frequency ω = 2πf = 2π(4) = 25.13 rad s⁻¹. By the defining SHM equation, a = −ω²x = −(25.13)²(-0.0225) = 14.2 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ω = 2πf and obtains 14.2 m s⁻² (D).

options.distractorRationale: Substitutes cyclic frequency f directly for angular frequency ω, computing −f²x instead of −(2πf)²x.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates −ωx instead of −ω²x, forgetting to square the angular frequency.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the restoring minus sign in a = −ω²x, giving acceleration in the same sign as displacement instead of toward equilibrium.

items.stem: The velocity–displacement phase portrait shown represents an ultrasonic wire-bonding horn tip oscillating with ω = 40 rad s⁻¹ and x₀ = 0.12 m. Find the oscillator's speed at x = 0.072 m.
items.workedSolution: Using v = ω√(x₀² − x²) gives v = 40 × √(0.12² − 0.072²) = 3.84 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into v = ω√(x₀² − x²) to obtain 3.84 m s⁻¹ (C).

options.distractorRationale: Evaluates ω(x₀ − x) linearly instead of taking √(x₀² − x²).

options.label: B

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the maximum speed ωx₀ at equilibrium (x = 0) instead of the speed at x.

items.stem: A monochromatic beam with free-space wavelength 450 nm (vacuum speed 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) enters optical diamond (n₂ = 2.42) from dry air (n₁ = 1) at 22° to the interface normal in an ophthalmic lens-blank inspection jig. Calculate the optical wavelength in optical diamond.
items.workedSolution: Wave frequency remains unchanged across the boundary, while phase speed decreases to v₂ = c / n₂. Hence λ₂ = λ₀ / n₂ = 450 / 2.42 = 186 nm.

markScheme.criterion: Uses λ₂ = λ₀ / n₂ = 450 / 2.42 to obtain 186 nm (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies the vacuum wavelength λ₀ by n₂ instead of dividing λ₀ by n₂.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Assumes optical wavelength remains unchanged at λ₀ upon entering the second medium, confusing constant frequency with constant wavelength.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Incorrectly multiplies the medium wavelength by sin θ₁.

items.stem: A prism assembly in a semiconductor immersion-lithography stage places optical diamond of refractive index 2.42 in contact with liquid ethanol of refractive index 1.36 (take c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹). A test beam strikes the interface from inside optical diamond at 51° to the normal. Calculate the critical angle for total internal reflection at the boundary.
items.workedSolution: At the critical angle θ_c, sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1.36 / 2.42 = 0.5620, giving θ_c = arcsin(0.5620) = 34.2°.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1.36 / 2.42 to obtain θ_c = 34.2° (B).

items.stem: Engineers specifying a high-voltage substation optical isolator link test a 350 m step-index optical fiber having n_core = 1.5 and n_clad = 1.44 under a 12.3° test beam from water (n_ext = 1.33). Calculate the minimum angle of incidence to the wall normal required for total internal reflection inside the core.
items.workedSolution: At the core–cladding boundary, sin θ_c = n_clad / n_core = 1.44 / 1.5 = 0.9600, giving θ_c = 73.7°.

items.stem: A 60 m step-index optical fiber in a surgical laser-lithotripsy delivery fiber has core refractive index 1.55 and cladding refractive index 1.47, with its flat input face in air of refractive index 1.00 (currently aligned with a test ray at 15.9°). What is the maximum external launch angle θ_max to the fiber axis for which rays remain guided by total internal reflection?
items.workedSolution: At the grazing limit, sin θ_c = 1.47 / 1.55, so inside the core sin θ_axis,max = cos θ_c = √(1 − (n_clad / n_core)²). By Snell's law at the entry face, n_ext sin θ_max = √(n_core² − n_clad²) = 0.4915, giving θ_max = arcsin(0.4915) = 29.4°.

markScheme.criterion: Uses n_ext sin θ_max = √(n_core² − n_clad²) to obtain θ_max = 29.4° (C).

items.stem: In an optical-bench crosswire projection setup, a small specimen of height 0.018 m is held 0.1125 m in front of a thin converging magnifier lens of focal length 0.15 m. Using the real-is-positive sign convention (1/f = 1/u + 1/v), what is the signed image distance v?
items.workedSolution: Because u = 0.1125 m < f = 0.15 m, 1/v = 1/0.15 − 1/0.1125 = -2.222 m⁻¹, giving a signed virtual image distance v = -0.450 m.

markScheme.criterion: Computes 1/v = 1/0.15 − 1/0.1125 to obtain signed v = -0.450 m (A).

items.stem: In a precision gravimeter spring-mass test stage of mass 1.2 kg and spring constant 90 N m⁻¹, the oscillator is displaced by an amplitude of 0.035 m from equilibrium and released. What is the period T of its simple harmonic motion?
items.workedSolution: For an ideal mass-spring oscillator, T = 2π√(m / k) = 2π√(1.2 / 90) = 0.726 s.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Swaps m/k and k/m inside the radical, computing 2π√(k / m) instead of 2π√(m / k).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 2π and calculates √(m / k) = 1 / ω.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the square root and evaluates 2π(m / k).

items.stem: A vertical helical spring of stiffness 25 N m⁻¹ in a high-speed pantograph contact-spring test rig suspends a load of mass 0.9 kg that subsequently oscillates vertically with amplitude 0.042 m. Taking g = 9.81 m s⁻², what was the static extension Δx_eq of the spring at equilibrium before oscillation started?
items.workedSolution: At static equilibrium, upward spring tension balances weight: k Δx_eq = mg ⇒ Δx_eq = (0.9 × 9.81) / 25 = 0.353 m.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Adds the oscillation amplitude x₀ to mg / k, finding maximum total stretch rather than static equilibrium extension.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Hooke's law as k / (mg) instead of mg / k.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides mass m directly by spring constant k without multiplying by gravitational field strength g.

items.stem: A 0.25 kg brass bob on a 0.85 m suspension wire in a metrology gravimetry pendulum stand oscillates with arc-length amplitude 0.2125 m (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Calculate the maximum cord tension at the bottom of the swing.
items.workedSolution: With ω = √(g / L) = √(9.81 / 0.85), peak speed v_max = ω x₀ = 0.722 m s⁻¹. At the lowest point, T_cord = m(g + v_max² / L) = 2.61 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_max = ω x₀ and T_cord = mg + mv_max² / L = 2.61 N (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Equates cord tension at the lowest point to static weight mg, ignoring the upward centripetal force mv_max² / L.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts the centripetal force mv_max² / L from mg instead of adding it at the bottom of the arc.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates only the net radial centripetal force mv_max² / L rather than the total cord tension.

items.stem: In a marine wave-tank oscillating piston paddle, an oscillator undergoes SHM at 2 Hz with amplitude 0.06 m (passing through x = 0.021 m). Calculate the peak acceleration magnitude a_max = (2πf)² x₀.
items.workedSolution: With ω = 2π(2) = 12.57 rad s⁻¹, maximum acceleration magnitude a_max = ω² x₀ = 9.47 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ω = 2πf and obtains 9.47 m s⁻² (D).

items.stem: In an ultrasonic surgical transducer tip, an oscillating body of mass 0.15 kg executes simple harmonic motion with angular frequency ω = 18 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude x₀ = 0.08 m. What is its kinetic energy E_k when its displacement from equilibrium is x = 0.064 m?
items.workedSolution: Using E_k = ½mω²(x₀² − x²) gives E_k = 0.5 × 0.15 × 18² × (0.08² − 0.064²) = 0.0560 J.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Interpolates energy linearly as E_tot(1 − x / x₀) instead of quadratically as E_tot(1 − x² / x₀²).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the potential energy ½mω²x² at x rather than the kinetic energy ½mω²(x₀² − x²).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes the total mechanical energy ½mω²x₀² instead of subtracting potential energy at x.

items.stem: In a planetary lander atmospheric nephelometer, an optical beam propagating in optical diamond (n₁ = 2.42, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) meets a planar dry air boundary (n₂ = 1) at an angle of incidence of 33° to the normal. Calculate the angular deviation of the beam produced at the interface.
items.workedSolution: Since sin θ_c = 1 / 2.42 gives θ_c = 24.4° and θ₁ = 33° > θ_c, the beam undergoes total internal reflection with θ_r = 33°. The angular deviation from the original forward direction is δ = 180° − 2(33°) = 114°.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies TIR (θ₁ > θ_c = 24.4°) and computes δ = 180° − 2θ₁ = 114° (A).

items.stem: Within an undergraduate ray-box bench, monochromatic light enters a parallel-sided polycarbonate polymer window (n₁ = 1.58, thickness 0.045 m) from dry air (n₀ = 1) at 64° to the normal and exits into liquid ethanol (n₂ = 1.36). What is the angle of refraction in liquid ethanol?
items.workedSolution: Across parallel planar boundaries, n₀ sin θ₀ = n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂. Thus sin θ₂ = (1 × sin 64°) / 1.36, giving θ₂ = 41.4°.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Snell invariant n₀ sin θ₀ = n₂ sin θ₂ to obtain θ₂ = 41.4° (C).

items.stem: Engineers evaluating bit-rate limits for a flexible medical gastroscope bundle test a 1200 m step-index waveguide (n_core = 1.62, n_clad = 1.51, n_ext = 1.00, ray shown at 21.6°). Take c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹. Determine the multipath dispersion delay Δt between extreme guided rays and axial rays.
items.workedSolution: Axial transit time t_min = n_core L / c = (1.62 × 1200) / (3.00 × 10⁸) = 6.48 × 10⁻⁶ s. At the critical angle sin θ_c = n_clad / n_core, t_max = t_min / sin θ_c = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 6.95 × 10⁻⁶ s. Modal delay Δt = t_max − t_min = 4.72 × 10⁻⁷ s.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δt = (n_core L / c)(n_core / n_clad − 1) = 4.72 × 10⁻⁷ s (B).

items.stem: During optical testing on an architectural wide-field door viewer, a 0.036 m illuminated target sits 0.75 m from a thin diverging lens of focal length −0.3 m. Determine the signed image position v under the real-is-positive sign convention.
items.workedSolution: For a diverging lens, f = −0.3 m. Using 1/f = 1/u + 1/v gives 1/v = −1/0.3 − 1/0.75 = -4.667 m⁻¹, so v = -0.214 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses negative f = −0.3 m in 1/v = 1/f − 1/u to obtain v = -0.214 m (C).

items.stem: A vertical helical spring of stiffness 40 N m⁻¹ in a cryogenic cooler linear-compressor piston assembly suspends a load of mass 0.5 kg that subsequently oscillates vertically with amplitude 0.042 m. Taking g = 9.8 m s⁻², what was the static extension Δx_eq of the spring at equilibrium before oscillation started?
items.workedSolution: At static equilibrium, upward spring tension balances weight: k Δx_eq = mg ⇒ Δx_eq = (0.5 × 9.8) / 40 = 0.123 m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Adds the oscillation amplitude x₀ to mg / k, finding maximum total stretch rather than static equilibrium extension.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Hooke's law as k / (mg) instead of mg / k.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Divides mass m directly by spring constant k without multiplying by gravitational field strength g.

items.stem: In a coastal lighthouse clockwork escapement pendulum, a small dense bob of mass 0.35 kg hangs on a light inextensible cord of length 2.2 m and swings with small arc amplitude 0.22 m. Taking g = 9.8 m s⁻², what is the oscillation frequency f?

markScheme.criterion: Obtains 0.336 Hz using g = 9.8 m s⁻² (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts g / L inside the radical, computing (1 / 2π)√(L / g) instead of (1 / 2π)√(g / L).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Reports the angular frequency ω = √(g / L) without dividing by 2π.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the period T instead of the frequency f = 1 / T.

items.stem: The acceleration–displacement line shown models a dynamic mechanical thermal-analyzer probe oscillating harmonically at 2 Hz with amplitude 0.06 m. Using a = −ω²x, calculate the signed acceleration at displacement x = 0.045 m.
items.workedSolution: Angular frequency ω = 2πf = 2π(2) = 12.57 rad s⁻¹. By the defining SHM equation, a = −ω²x = −(12.57)²(0.045) = -7.11 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ω = 2πf and obtains -7.11 m s⁻² (C).

items.stem: The velocity–displacement phase portrait shown represents a scanning-probe interferometric calibration stage oscillating with ω = 24 rad s⁻¹ and x₀ = 0.04 m. Find the oscillator's speed at x = 0.02 m.
items.workedSolution: Using v = ω√(x₀² − x²) gives v = 24 × √(0.04² − 0.02²) = 0.831 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into v = ω√(x₀² − x²) to obtain 0.831 m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: During quality testing on a semiconductor immersion-lithography stage, monochromatic light in fused-silica glass (n₁ = 1.46) enters a transparent specimen at an incidence angle of 34° and is refracted to 54.7° relative to the boundary normal. Calculate the specimen's refractive index n₂.
items.workedSolution: Rearranging Snell's law n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂ gives n₂ = 1.46 × sin 34° / sin 54.7° = 1.00.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates n₂ = n₁ sin θ₁ / sin θ₂ = 1.00 (C).

items.stem: A parallel-sided optical window of dense flint glass (refractive index 1.65, thickness 0.03 m) immersed in distilled water (n₀ = 1.33) is illuminated at 38° to the normal in a bathymetric laser-ranging tank. Calculate the transverse shift t₁ tan θ₁ of the ray along the exit boundary.
items.workedSolution: Inside the dense flint glass slab, sin θ₁ = (1.33 sin 38°) / 1.65, giving θ₁ = 29.8°. The transverse shift along the exit face is Δy = t₁ tan θ₁ = 0.03 × tan 29.75° = 0.0171 m.

items.stem: In a cryogenic laboratory optical feedthrough, a straight step-index fiber of length 40 m has core index n_core = 1.55 and cladding index n_clad = 1.47. A test ray enters the flat end-face from air (n_ext = 1.00) at a steep angle θ_in = 40.4° to the fiber axis, exceeding the acceptance cone so light refracts into the cladding. What is the angle of refraction in the cladding measured from the core–cladding wall normal?
items.workedSolution: At entry, sin θ_axis = (1 sin 40.4°) / 1.55 ⇒ θ_axis = 24.7°. The angle to the wall normal is θ_w = 90° − θ_axis = 65.3° (< θ_c = 71.5°). Refracting into the cladding: sin θ_clad = (1.55 sin θ_w) / 1.47, giving θ_clad = 73.3°.

markScheme.criterion: Finds θ_w = 65.3° and refracts into cladding to obtain 73.3° (A).

items.stem: In a structural-health bridge sensor lead, light from air (n_ext = 1.00, illustrated at 22.7°) propagates along a 500 m step-index fiber with n_core = 1.49 and n_clad = 1.39. Taking c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, what is the transit time t_max of the slowest guided ray that meets the core–cladding wall at the critical angle?
items.workedSolution: Wave speed in the core is v = c / n_core, and the critical-angle ray travels path length L / sin θ_c = L (n_core / n_clad). Therefore t_max = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 2.66 × 10⁻⁶ s.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates t_max = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 2.66 × 10⁻⁶ s (B).

items.stem: In a high-power excimer beam-shaping negative lens, an object of height 0.045 m is positioned 0.25 m from a concave lens of focal length −0.1 m. Calculate the signed linear magnification m = h_i / h_o = −v / u.
items.workedSolution: With f = −0.1 m, 1/v = −1/0.1 − 1/0.25 gives v = -0.0714 m. Therefore m = −v / u = −(-0.07143) / 0.25 = 0.286 (upright and diminished).

markScheme.criterion: Finds v = -0.0714 m and m = −v / u = 0.286 (B).

options.distractorRationale: Assigns a negative magnification as if a diverging lens formed an inverted real image of a real object.

options.label: C

items.stem: During stiffness testing on a cleanroom nanopositioning flexure stage, a 0.64 kg mass oscillates horizontally with amplitude 0.025 m and a measured period of 0.672 s. What is the spring constant k?
items.workedSolution: Rearranging T = 2π√(m / k) gives k = 4π²m / T² = 4π²(0.64) / (0.672)² = 56.0 N m⁻¹.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 4π² and computes m / T².

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Fails to square 2π / T when rearranging T = 2π√(m / k), computing 2πm / T instead of 4π²m / T².

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts m / T² when rearranging the period equation.

items.stem: To calibrate a mine-shaft gravity-anomaly survey pendulum where g = 9.8 m s⁻², a 0.45 kg pendulum bob oscillates at small arc amplitude 0.021 m with period T = 1.19 s. Calculate the pendulum length L.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Divides gT² by 2π instead of 4π².

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Forgets to square T / (2π) when rearranging T = 2π√(L / g), computing gT / (2π).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the rearranged expression for L.

items.stem: Engineers timing a skyscraper tuned-pendulum damper scale model use a 0.6 kg bob on a 1.3 m light cord swinging with arc amplitude 0.364 m (g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Calculate the period T.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Omits the square root on L / g.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the half-period π√(L / g) instead of the full period 2π√(L / g).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts L / g inside the square root.

items.stem: In a diesel injector needle-valve harmonic test rig, a stage oscillates in simple harmonic motion with angular frequency ω = 24 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude x₀ = 0.15 m, tracing the velocity–displacement ellipse shown. What is the speed v of the stage when its displacement from equilibrium is x = 0.054 m?
items.workedSolution: Using v = ω√(x₀² − x²) gives v = 24 × √(0.15² − 0.054²) = 3.36 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into v = ω√(x₀² − x²) to obtain 3.36 m s⁻¹ (C).

options.distractorRationale: Uses ωx instead of ω√(x₀² − x²), mistakenly assuming speed is directly proportional to displacement.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates ω(x₀ − x) linearly instead of taking √(x₀² − x²).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the maximum speed ωx₀ at equilibrium (x = 0) instead of the speed at x.

items.stem: A 0.25 kg resonator in an atomic-force microscope cantilever tip executes simple harmonic motion of amplitude 0.1 m and angular frequency ω = 18 rad s⁻¹ (probed at x = 0.05 m). At what cyclic frequency f_E does its kinetic energy oscillate with time?
items.workedSolution: Mechanical frequency f = ω / (2π) = 18 / (2π) = 2.865 Hz. Because kinetic energy reaches a maximum twice per mechanical period, f_E = 2f = ω / π = 5.73 Hz.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates 2ω in rad s⁻¹ without dividing by 2π to convert to hertz.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Halves the mechanical frequency instead of doubling it.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Gives the mechanical displacement frequency f = ω / (2π) instead of recognizing that E_k ∝ cos²(ωt) oscillates at 2f.

items.stem: A prism assembly in an industrial sugar-brix inline refractometer places crystalline zircon of refractive index 1.92 in contact with distilled water of refractive index 1.33 (take c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹). A test beam strikes the interface from inside crystalline zircon at 52° to the normal. Calculate the critical angle for total internal reflection at the boundary.
items.workedSolution: At the critical angle θ_c, sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1.33 / 1.92 = 0.6927, giving θ_c = arcsin(0.6927) = 43.8°.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1.33 / 1.92 to obtain θ_c = 43.8° (C).

items.stem: Engineers aligning a precision Abbe refractometer cell pass a narrow beam in dry air (n₀ = 1) through a flat optical crown glass window (n₁ = 1.52, thickness 0.06 m) at 38° to the normal into dry air. Determine the perpendicular lateral displacement of the transmitted beam.
items.workedSolution: By Snell's law, sin θ₁ = (1 sin 38°) / 1.52 ⇒ θ₁ = 23.9°. The perpendicular lateral displacement of the emergent ray is d = t₁ sin(θ₀ − θ₁) / cos θ₁ = 0.0160 m.

items.stem: In a transoceanic telecommunications link, a 60 m step-index waveguide with n_core = 1.58 and n_clad = 1.49 receives light from air of refractive index 1.00 (shown for a 14.3° ray). Determine the maximum external incidence angle θ_max to the axis that still achieves total internal reflection at the core wall.
items.workedSolution: At the grazing limit, sin θ_c = 1.49 / 1.58, so inside the core sin θ_axis,max = cos θ_c = √(1 − (n_clad / n_core)²). By Snell's law at the entry face, n_ext sin θ_max = √(n_core² − n_clad²) = 0.5256, giving θ_max = arcsin(0.5256) = 31.7°.

markScheme.criterion: Uses n_ext sin θ_max = √(n_core² − n_clad²) to obtain θ_max = 31.7° (C).

items.stem: Within a precision machine-vision inspection camera, an upright scale mark of height 0.018 m sits 0.07 m from a thin convex lens of focal length 0.2 m. Applying 1/f = 1/u + 1/v in the real-is-positive convention, determine the signed image position v.
items.workedSolution: Because u = 0.07 m < f = 0.2 m, 1/v = 1/0.2 − 1/0.07 = -9.286 m⁻¹, giving a signed virtual image distance v = -0.108 m.

markScheme.criterion: Computes 1/v = 1/0.2 − 1/0.07 to obtain signed v = -0.108 m (B).

options.distractorRationale: Adds 1/f + 1/u instead of evaluating 1/v = 1/f − 1/u.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Forgets that v < 0 for a virtual image in the real-is-positive sign convention, reporting +|v| as if a real image formed behind the lens.

options.label: D

items.stem: An experimental setup consisting of an orbital microgravity mass-measurement spring chair has oscillating mass 0.16 kg, spring stiffness 18 N m⁻¹, and horizontal amplitude 0.075 m. Calculate the oscillation period T.
items.workedSolution: For an ideal mass-spring oscillator, T = 2π√(m / k) = 2π√(0.16 / 18) = 0.592 s.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Swaps m/k and k/m inside the radical, computing 2π√(k / m) instead of 2π√(m / k).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 2π and calculates √(m / k) = 1 / ω.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the square root and evaluates 2π(m / k).

items.stem: A vertical helical spring of stiffness 100 N m⁻¹ in a frictionless air-track glider coupled to a calibrated coil spring suspends a load of mass 1.2 kg that subsequently oscillates vertically with amplitude 0.055 m. Taking g = 9.8 m s⁻², what was the static extension Δx_eq of the spring at equilibrium before oscillation started?
items.workedSolution: At static equilibrium, upward spring tension balances weight: k Δx_eq = mg ⇒ Δx_eq = (1.2 × 9.8) / 100 = 0.118 m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Divides mass m directly by spring constant k without multiplying by gravitational field strength g.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Adds the oscillation amplitude x₀ to mg / k, finding maximum total stretch rather than static equilibrium extension.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Hooke's law as k / (mg) instead of mg / k.

items.stem: A 0.5 kg brass bob on a 1.6 m suspension wire in a geophysical field-survey simple pendulum oscillates with arc-length amplitude 0.448 m (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Calculate the maximum cord tension at the bottom of the swing.
items.workedSolution: With ω = √(g / L) = √(9.81 / 1.6), peak speed v_max = ω x₀ = 1.11 m s⁻¹. At the lowest point, T_cord = m(g + v_max² / L) = 5.29 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_max = ω x₀ and T_cord = mg + mv_max² / L = 5.29 N (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates only the net radial centripetal force mv_max² / L rather than the total cord tension.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts the centripetal force mv_max² / L from mg instead of adding it at the bottom of the arc.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Equates cord tension at the lowest point to static weight mg, ignoring the upward centripetal force mv_max² / L.

items.stem: In an ultrasonic wire-bonding horn tip, a component executes simple harmonic motion at frequency f = 6 Hz with amplitude x₀ = 0.02 m, as represented on the acceleration–displacement graph. Taking displacement to the right as positive, what is its signed acceleration a when x = 0.007 m?
items.workedSolution: Angular frequency ω = 2πf = 2π(6) = 37.70 rad s⁻¹. By the defining SHM equation, a = −ω²x = −(37.70)²(0.007) = -9.95 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ω = 2πf and obtains -9.95 m s⁻² (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates −ωx instead of −ω²x, forgetting to square the angular frequency.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes cyclic frequency f directly for angular frequency ω, computing −f²x instead of −(2πf)²x.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the restoring minus sign in a = −ω²x, giving acceleration in the same sign as displacement instead of toward equilibrium.

items.stem: In a studio loudspeaker voice-coil cone, an oscillating body of mass 0.5 kg executes simple harmonic motion with angular frequency ω = 12 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude x₀ = 0.12 m. What is its kinetic energy E_k when its displacement from equilibrium is x = 0.096 m?
items.workedSolution: Using E_k = ½mω²(x₀² − x²) gives E_k = 0.5 × 0.5 × 12² × (0.12² − 0.096²) = 0.187 J.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the potential energy ½mω²x² at x rather than the kinetic energy ½mω²(x₀² − x²).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Interpolates energy linearly as E_tot(1 − x / x₀) instead of quadratically as E_tot(1 − x² / x₀²).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes the total mechanical energy ½mω²x₀² instead of subtracting potential energy at x.

items.stem: A monochromatic beam with free-space wavelength 650 nm (vacuum speed 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) enters optical diamond (n₂ = 2.42) from distilled water (n₁ = 1.33) at 52° to the interface normal in a semiconductor immersion-lithography stage. Calculate the optical wavelength in optical diamond.
items.workedSolution: Wave frequency remains unchanged across the boundary, while phase speed decreases to v₂ = c / n₂. Hence λ₂ = λ₀ / n₂ = 650 / 2.42 = 269 nm.

markScheme.criterion: Uses λ₂ = λ₀ / n₂ = 650 / 2.42 to obtain 269 nm (D).
