items.stem: Within an immersion-microscopy optical stage, monochromatic light enters a parallel-sided polycarbonate polymer window (n₁ = 1.58, thickness 0.055 m) from dry air (n₀ = 1) at 34° to the normal and exits into fused-silica glass (n₂ = 1.46). What is the angle of refraction in fused-silica glass?
items.workedSolution: Across parallel planar boundaries, n₀ sin θ₀ = n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂. Thus sin θ₂ = (1 × sin 34°) / 1.46, giving θ₂ = 22.5°.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Snell invariant n₀ sin θ₀ = n₂ sin θ₂ to obtain θ₂ = 22.5° (C).

items.stem: A 80 m step-index waveguide in a fusion-chamber diagnostic optical relay is fabricated with a core of refractive index 1.58 surrounded by cladding of refractive index 1.49, with light launched from air (n_ext = 1.00) at 18.7° to the axis. What is the critical angle θ_c at the core–cladding interface?
items.workedSolution: At the core–cladding boundary, sin θ_c = n_clad / n_core = 1.49 / 1.58 = 0.9430, giving θ_c = 70.6°.

options.distractorRationale: Finds the complement 90° − θ_c measured to the fiber axis rather than the critical angle measured to the wall normal.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes arcsin(1 / n_core) as if the bare core were surrounded by air instead of cladding of index n_clad.

items.stem: Engineers evaluating bit-rate limits for an avionics fly-by-light data bus test a 240 m step-index waveguide (n_core = 1.57, n_clad = 1.46, n_ext = 1.00, ray shown at 17.6°). Take c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹. Determine the multipath dispersion delay Δt between extreme guided rays and axial rays.
items.workedSolution: Axial transit time t_min = n_core L / c = (1.57 × 240) / (3.00 × 10⁸) = 1.26 × 10⁻⁶ s. At the critical angle sin θ_c = n_clad / n_core, t_max = t_min / sin θ_c = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 1.35 × 10⁻⁶ s. Modal delay Δt = t_max − t_min = 9.46 × 10⁻⁸ s.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δt = (n_core L / c)(n_core / n_clad − 1) = 9.46 × 10⁻⁸ s (C).

items.stem: A thin converging inspection lens of focal length 0.1 m in a cinema slide-projector lens mount views an upright feature of height 0.012 m held at object distance u = 0.04 m (< f). What is the height h_i of the virtual upright image?
items.workedSolution: From 1/v = 1/0.1 − 1/0.04, v = -0.0667 m. Linear magnification m = −v / u = 1.667, so upright image height h_i = m h_o = 0.0200 m.

items.stem: A thin diverging lens of focal length f = −0.15 m in an underwater dome-port virtual-image corrector forms a virtual image of an upright object of height 0.036 m placed at u = 0.09 m. What is the linear magnification m = −v / u of the image?
items.workedSolution: With f = −0.15 m, 1/v = −1/0.15 − 1/0.09 gives v = -0.0563 m. Therefore m = −v / u = −(-0.05625) / 0.09 = 0.625 (upright and diminished).

markScheme.criterion: Finds v = -0.0563 m and m = −v / u = 0.625 (A).

items.stem: A vertical helical spring of stiffness 100 N m⁻¹ in a silicon MEMS accelerometer proof-mass flexure test model suspends a load of mass 0.6 kg that subsequently oscillates vertically with amplitude 0.042 m. Taking g = 9.81 m s⁻², what was the static extension Δx_eq of the spring at equilibrium before oscillation started?
items.workedSolution: At static equilibrium, upward spring tension balances weight: k Δx_eq = mg ⇒ Δx_eq = (0.6 × 9.81) / 100 = 0.0589 m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Hooke's law as k / (mg) instead of mg / k.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Adds the oscillation amplitude x₀ to mg / k, finding maximum total stretch rather than static equilibrium extension.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides mass m directly by spring constant k without multiplying by gravitational field strength g.

items.stem: In a long-case regulator clock calibration rig, a small dense bob of mass 0.45 kg hangs on a light inextensible cord of length 1.15 m and swings with small arc amplitude 0.115 m. Taking g = 9.8 m s⁻², what is the oscillation frequency f?

markScheme.criterion: Obtains 0.465 Hz using g = 9.8 m s⁻² (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the period T instead of the frequency f = 1 / T.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Reports the angular frequency ω = √(g / L) without dividing by 2π.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts g / L inside the radical, computing (1 / 2π)√(L / g) instead of (1 / 2π)√(g / L).

items.stem: In a studio loudspeaker voice-coil cone, a component executes simple harmonic motion at frequency f = 2 Hz with amplitude x₀ = 0.02 m, as represented on the acceleration–displacement graph. Taking displacement to the right as positive, what is its signed acceleration a when x = -0.012 m?
items.workedSolution: Angular frequency ω = 2πf = 2π(2) = 12.57 rad s⁻¹. By the defining SHM equation, a = −ω²x = −(12.57)²(-0.012) = 1.89 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ω = 2πf and obtains 1.89 m s⁻² (A).

items.stem: The velocity–displacement phase portrait shown represents an ultrasonic surgical transducer tip oscillating with ω = 30 rad s⁻¹ and x₀ = 0.1 m. Find the oscillator's speed at x = 0.028 m.
items.workedSolution: Using v = ω√(x₀² − x²) gives v = 30 × √(0.1² − 0.028²) = 2.88 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into v = ω√(x₀² − x²) to obtain 2.88 m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: In a clinical corneal pachymetry test phantom, light of vacuum wavelength 650 nm (speed in vacuum c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) crosses a flat boundary from optical diamond (n₁ = 2.42) into liquid ethanol (n₂ = 1.36) with incident angle 18°. Determine the wave speed in liquid ethanol.
items.workedSolution: From the definition of refractive index n₂ = c / v₂, the wave speed in liquid ethanol is v₂ = (3.00 × 10⁸) / 1.36 = 2.21 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Computes v₂ = c / n₂ = 3.00 × 10⁸ / 1.36 = 2.21 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: On a bathymetric laser-ranging tank, the critical angle for total internal reflection of monochromatic light passing from a transparent crystal into dry air (n₂ = 1) is measured to be 43.2° to the normal. What is the refractive index n₁ of the crystal?
items.workedSolution: At the critical angle, n₁ sin θ_c = n₂ sin 90° = n₂, so n₁ = 1 / sin 43.2° = 1.46.

markScheme.criterion: Computes n₁ = n₂ / sin θ_c = 1 / sin 43.2° = 1.46 (D).

items.stem: A 350 m step-index optical fiber used in a surgical laser-lithotripsy delivery fiber has core refractive index 1.58 and cladding refractive index 1.49. A laser ray in water (n_ext = 1.33) enters the center of the flat end-face at θ_in = 15.6° to the fiber axis. What angle of incidence θ_w does the refracted ray make with the normal to the core–cladding wall?
items.workedSolution: At the entry face, 1.33 sin 15.6° = 1.58 sin θ_axis ⇒ θ_axis = 13.1°. Since the core wall is parallel to the axis, its normal is perpendicular to the axis, giving θ_w = 90° − θ_axis = 76.9°.

items.stem: A monochromatic ray in water of refractive index 1.33 is coupled at 15° to the axis into a straight 450 m optical fiber (n_core = 1.49, n_clad = 1.39) during a structural-health bridge sensor lead. Calculate the total ray path length inside the 450 m fiber.
items.workedSolution: Inside the core, sin θ_axis = (1.33 sin 15°) / 1.49 ⇒ θ_axis = 13.4°. The total zig-zag geometric path length is L_ray = L / cos θ_axis = 450 / cos 13.36° = 463 m.

markScheme.criterion: Finds θ_axis = 13.4° and computes L / cos θ_axis = 463 m (C).

items.stem: An observer using a laboratory autocollimator test rail adjusts the position of a 0.022 m scale mark in front of a thin convex lens of focal length 0.12 m until its virtual image lies at the near point 0.180 m on the object side of the lens (v = −0.180 m). Calculate the object distance u.
items.workedSolution: For a virtual image in the real-is-positive convention, v = -0.180 m. Thus 1/u = 1/f − 1/v = 1/0.12 − (1/-0.1800) = 13.89 m⁻¹, giving u = 0.0720 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes negative v = -0.180 m into 1/u = 1/f − 1/v to obtain u = 0.0720 m (B).

options.distractorRationale: Subtracts focal length directly from |v| instead of adding reciprocals 1/f + 1/|v|.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Forgets v < 0 for a virtual image and substitutes v = +|v| into 1/u = 1/f − 1/v instead of v = −|v|.

options.label: D

items.stem: A 1.5 kg test mass in a high-speed pantograph contact-spring test rig executes horizontal simple harmonic motion of amplitude 0.06 m and period T = 2.06 s. Calculate the stiffness k of the spring.
items.workedSolution: Rearranging T = 2π√(m / k) gives k = 4π²m / T² = 4π²(1.5) / (2.06)² = 14.0 N m⁻¹.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 4π² and computes m / T².

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Fails to square 2π / T when rearranging T = 2π√(m / k), computing 2πm / T instead of 4π²m / T².

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts m / T² when rearranging the period equation.

items.stem: On a metrology gravimetry pendulum stand, a simple pendulum with a 0.45 kg bob swings through a small arc amplitude of 0.14 m with a measured period of 2.66 s. Taking g = 9.8 m s⁻², what is the effective length L of the pendulum?

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Divides gT² by 2π instead of 4π².

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Forgets to square T / (2π) when rearranging T = 2π√(L / g), computing gT / (2π).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the rearranged expression for L.

items.stem: Engineers timing an evacuated bell-jar precision timing pendulum use a 0.15 kg bob on a 1.3 m light cord swinging with arc amplitude 0.364 m (g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Calculate the period T.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Omits the square root on L / g.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the half-period π√(L / g) instead of the full period 2π√(L / g).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts L / g inside the square root.

items.stem: Engineers monitoring a quartz crystal tuning-fork tine measure simple harmonic motion of amplitude 0.06 m and angular frequency 25 rad s⁻¹. Determine the speed |v| = ω√(x₀² − x²) at displacement x = 0.0216 m.
items.workedSolution: Using v = ω√(x₀² − x²) gives v = 25 × √(0.06² − 0.0216²) = 1.40 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into v = ω√(x₀² − x²) to obtain 1.40 m s⁻¹ (B).

options.distractorRationale: Uses ωx instead of ω√(x₀² − x²), mistakenly assuming speed is directly proportional to displacement.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the maximum speed ωx₀ at equilibrium (x = 0) instead of the speed at x.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates ω(x₀ − x) linearly instead of taking √(x₀² − x²).

items.stem: A 0.25 kg resonator in a vibrometer calibration shaker table executes simple harmonic motion of amplitude 0.04 m and angular frequency ω = 12 rad s⁻¹ (probed at x = 0.016 m). At what cyclic frequency f_E does its kinetic energy oscillate with time?
items.workedSolution: Mechanical frequency f = ω / (2π) = 12 / (2π) = 1.910 Hz. Because kinetic energy reaches a maximum twice per mechanical period, f_E = 2f = ω / π = 3.82 Hz.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Halves the mechanical frequency instead of doubling it.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Gives the mechanical displacement frequency f = ω / (2π) instead of recognizing that E_k ∝ cos²(ωt) oscillates at 2f.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates 2ω in rad s⁻¹ without dividing by 2π to convert to hertz.

items.stem: In a precision Abbe refractometer cell, a light ray inside synthetic sapphire (n₁ = 1.77, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) approaches a planar interface with distilled water (n₂ = 1.33) at an incident angle of 61° to the normal. What is the critical angle θ_c at this synthetic sapphire–distilled water boundary?
items.workedSolution: At the critical angle θ_c, sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1.33 / 1.77 = 0.7514, giving θ_c = arcsin(0.7514) = 48.7°.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1.33 / 1.77 to obtain θ_c = 48.7° (D).

items.stem: In a microfluidic refractive-index sensor, a collimated laser ray in distilled water (n₀ = 1.33) strikes a uniform parallel-sided crystalline zircon block (n₁ = 1.92) of thickness 0.04 m at 44° to the normal and emerges back into distilled water. What is the perpendicular lateral displacement between the emergent ray and the undeviated incident ray line?
items.workedSolution: By Snell's law, sin θ₁ = (1.33 sin 44°) / 1.92 ⇒ θ₁ = 28.8°. The perpendicular lateral displacement of the emergent ray is d = t₁ sin(θ₀ − θ₁) / cos θ₁ = 0.0120 m.

items.stem: In an industrial laser-welding delivery cable, a 60 m step-index waveguide with n_core = 1.54 and n_clad = 1.45 receives light from air of refractive index 1.00 (shown for a 22.5° ray). Determine the maximum external incidence angle θ_max to the axis that still achieves total internal reflection at the core wall.
items.workedSolution: At the grazing limit, sin θ_c = 1.45 / 1.54, so inside the core sin θ_axis,max = cos θ_c = √(1 − (n_clad / n_core)²). By Snell's law at the entry face, n_ext sin θ_max = √(n_core² − n_clad²) = 0.5187, giving θ_max = arcsin(0.5187) = 31.2°.

markScheme.criterion: Uses n_ext sin θ_max = √(n_core² − n_clad²) to obtain θ_max = 31.2° (D).

options.distractorRationale: Confuses the core–cladding critical angle θ_c with the external acceptance half-angle θ_max.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Gives the maximum internal angle 90° − θ_c inside the core without refracting across the entry face into the external medium.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses (n_core − n_clad) instead of √(n_core² − n_clad²) when finding sin θ_max.

items.stem: Engineers evaluating bit-rate limits for a short-reach datacenter patch cord test a 1800 m step-index waveguide (n_core = 1.52, n_clad = 1.46, n_ext = 1.00, ray shown at 17.5°). Take c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹. Determine the multipath dispersion delay Δt between extreme guided rays and axial rays.
items.workedSolution: Axial transit time t_min = n_core L / c = (1.52 × 1800) / (3.00 × 10⁸) = 9.12 × 10⁻⁶ s. At the critical angle sin θ_c = n_clad / n_core, t_max = t_min / sin θ_c = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 9.49 × 10⁻⁶ s. Modal delay Δt = t_max − t_min = 3.75 × 10⁻⁷ s.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δt = (n_core L / c)(n_core / n_clad − 1) = 3.75 × 10⁻⁷ s (B).

options.distractorRationale: Calculates the total transit time t_max of the slowest critical-angle ray without subtracting the axial transit time t_axial.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies t_axial by (1 − n_clad / n_core) instead of (n_core / n_clad − 1), inverting sin θ_c.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses the vacuum speed c instead of the core wave speed c / n_core when computing transit times.

items.stem: Within a metrology profile-projector optical train, an upright scale mark of height 0.008 m sits 0.08 m from a thin convex lens of focal length 0.1 m. Applying 1/f = 1/u + 1/v in the real-is-positive convention, determine the signed image position v.
items.workedSolution: Because u = 0.08 m < f = 0.1 m, 1/v = 1/0.1 − 1/0.08 = -2.500 m⁻¹, giving a signed virtual image distance v = -0.400 m.

markScheme.criterion: Computes 1/v = 1/0.1 − 1/0.08 to obtain signed v = -0.400 m (D).

options.distractorRationale: Forgets that v < 0 for a virtual image in the real-is-positive sign convention, reporting +|v| as if a real image formed behind the lens.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Adds 1/f + 1/u instead of evaluating 1/v = 1/f − 1/u.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes a negative focal length −f as if the magnifier were a diverging lens.

items.stem: During optical testing on a wide-angle security peephole assembly, a 0.02 m illuminated target sits 0.32 m from a thin diverging lens of focal length −0.4 m. Determine the signed image position v under the real-is-positive sign convention.
items.workedSolution: For a diverging lens, f = −0.4 m. Using 1/f = 1/u + 1/v gives 1/v = −1/0.4 − 1/0.32 = -5.625 m⁻¹, so v = -0.178 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses negative f = −0.4 m in 1/v = 1/f − 1/u to obtain v = -0.178 m (B).

options.distractorRationale: Computes the correct magnitude |v| but omits the negative sign required for a virtual image in the real-is-positive convention.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Forgets that a diverging lens has negative focal length f < 0, substituting +|f| into 1/v = 1/f − 1/u.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Stops at 1/v = −1/|f| − 1/u in m⁻¹ without taking the reciprocal to find v in metres.

items.stem: In a structural vibration-isolation test sled on linear bearings, a 0.3 kg mass hangs from a vertical spring of constant 100 N m⁻¹ and executes vertical SHM of amplitude 0.042 m (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Calculate the static equilibrium extension Δx_eq from the spring's unstretched length.
items.workedSolution: At static equilibrium, upward spring tension balances weight: k Δx_eq = mg ⇒ Δx_eq = (0.3 × 9.81) / 100 = 0.0294 m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Hooke's law as k / (mg) instead of mg / k.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Adds the oscillation amplitude x₀ to mg / k, finding maximum total stretch rather than static equilibrium extension.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides mass m directly by spring constant k without multiplying by gravitational field strength g.

items.stem: During timing measurements on a Foucault-style brass sphere suspension apparatus, a pendulum bob of mass 0.45 kg suspended from a light cord of length 1.15 m oscillates with small arc amplitude 0.115 m. Taking g = 9.8 m s⁻², what is the period T of one full oscillation?
items.workedSolution: For small angles, T = 2π√(L / g) = 2π√(1.15 / 9.8) = 2.15 s (independent of bob mass).

markScheme.criterion: Obtains 2.15 s using g = 9.8 m s⁻² (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes the half-period π√(L / g) for a single swing from one extreme to the other rather than a complete cycle.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Incorrectly includes the bob mass m inside the pendulum period equation.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Swaps L / g and g / L inside the square root, computing 2π√(g / L).

items.stem: In a diesel injector needle-valve harmonic test rig, an oscillator undergoes SHM at 3 Hz with amplitude 0.06 m (passing through x = 0.027 m). Calculate the peak acceleration magnitude a_max = (2πf)² x₀.
items.workedSolution: With ω = 2π(3) = 18.85 rad s⁻¹, maximum acceleration magnitude a_max = ω² x₀ = 21.3 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ω = 2πf and obtains 21.3 m s⁻² (C).

options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor (2π)² = 4π² and computes f² x₀.

options.label: B

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates ω x₀ (maximum speed) instead of ω² x₀ (maximum acceleration).

items.stem: In a tall-building tuned mass damper block, an oscillating body of mass 0.6 kg executes simple harmonic motion with angular frequency ω = 30 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude x₀ = 0.06 m. What is its kinetic energy E_k when its displacement from equilibrium is x = 0.024 m?
items.workedSolution: Using E_k = ½mω²(x₀² − x²) gives E_k = 0.5 × 0.6 × 30² × (0.06² − 0.024²) = 0.816 J.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Interpolates energy linearly as E_tot(1 − x / x₀) instead of quadratically as E_tot(1 − x² / x₀²).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the potential energy ½mω²x² at x rather than the kinetic energy ½mω²(x₀² − x²).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes the total mechanical energy ½mω²x₀² instead of subtracting potential energy at x.

items.stem: In a precision Abbe refractometer cell, a narrow monochromatic beam of free-space wavelength 589 nm (vacuum speed c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) travels through fused-silica glass (n₁ = 1.46) and strikes a flat boundary with synthetic sapphire (n₂ = 1.77) at 60° to the normal. What is the angle of refraction in the synthetic sapphire?
items.workedSolution: By Snell's law, n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂, so sin θ₂ = (1.46 × sin 60°) / 1.77 = 0.7143. Taking the inverse sine gives θ₂ = 45.6°.

markScheme.criterion: Applies n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂ to obtain θ₂ = 45.6° (B).

options.distractorRationale: Measures the incident angle from the boundary surface (90° − θ₁) rather than from the normal when applying Snell's law.

items.stem: In a photovoltaic encapsulant test coupon, a laser ray in dry air (n₀ = 1) strikes a flat parallel plate of dense flint glass (n₁ = 1.65, thickness 0.055 m) at 34° to the normal. The opposite face of the plate is in direct contact with liquid ethanol (n₂ = 1.36). At what emergent angle to the normal does the ray travel in liquid ethanol?
items.workedSolution: Across parallel planar boundaries, n₀ sin θ₀ = n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂. Thus sin θ₂ = (1 × sin 34°) / 1.36, giving θ₂ = 24.3°.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Snell invariant n₀ sin θ₀ = n₂ sin θ₂ to obtain θ₂ = 24.3° (A).

items.stem: A 350 m step-index optical fiber used in a subterranean pipeline temperature-sensing cable has core refractive index 1.54 and cladding refractive index 1.45. A laser ray in air (n_ext = 1.00) enters the center of the flat end-face at θ_in = 13.4° to the fiber axis. What angle of incidence θ_w does the refracted ray make with the normal to the core–cladding wall?
items.workedSolution: At the entry face, 1 sin 13.4° = 1.54 sin θ_axis ⇒ θ_axis = 8.66°. Since the core wall is parallel to the axis, its normal is perpendicular to the axis, giving θ_w = 90° − θ_axis = 81.3°.

items.stem: A multimode step-index fiber of length 240 m in a tethered deep-sea ROV umbilical waveguide has n_core = 1.55 and n_clad = 1.47 in air (n_ext = 1.00, illustrated with a 11.8° launch ray). Taking c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹ and neglecting material dispersion, what is the maximum multipath (modal) pulse broadening Δt between the fastest axial ray and the slowest guided ray?
items.workedSolution: Axial transit time t_min = n_core L / c = (1.55 × 240) / (3.00 × 10⁸) = 1.24 × 10⁻⁶ s. At the critical angle sin θ_c = n_clad / n_core, t_max = t_min / sin θ_c = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 1.31 × 10⁻⁶ s. Modal delay Δt = t_max − t_min = 6.75 × 10⁻⁸ s.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δt = (n_core L / c)(n_core / n_clad − 1) = 6.75 × 10⁻⁸ s (C).

items.stem: During optical testing on an optical-bench virtual-image calibration rig, a 0.036 m illuminated target sits 0.14 m from a thin diverging lens of focal length −0.1 m. Determine the signed image position v under the real-is-positive sign convention.
items.workedSolution: For a diverging lens, f = −0.1 m. Using 1/f = 1/u + 1/v gives 1/v = −1/0.1 − 1/0.14 = -17.14 m⁻¹, so v = -0.0583 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses negative f = −0.1 m in 1/v = 1/f − 1/u to obtain v = -0.0583 m (B).

items.stem: A test rig using an earthquake shake-table Tuned spring sled has mass 0.8 kg, horizontal spring constant 120 N m⁻¹, and oscillation amplitude 0.11 m. What is the natural frequency f of the oscillation?
items.workedSolution: Natural frequency f = (1 / 2π)√(k / m) = (1 / 2π)√(120 / 0.8) = 1.95 Hz.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Swaps k/m and m/k, computing (1 / 2π)√(m / k) instead of (1 / 2π)√(k / m).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes the period T = 2π√(m / k) instead of frequency f = 1 / T.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Reports angular frequency ω = √(k / m) in rad s⁻¹ without dividing by 2π.

items.stem: On a coastal lighthouse clockwork escapement pendulum, a simple pendulum with a 0.12 kg bob swings through a small arc amplitude of 0.105 m with a measured period of 2.66 s. Taking g = 9.8 m s⁻², what is the effective length L of the pendulum?

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Divides gT² by 2π instead of 4π².

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Forgets to square T / (2π) when rearranging T = 2π√(L / g), computing gT / (2π).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the rearranged expression for L.

items.stem: In a museum horology restoration pendulum rig, a simple pendulum of length 1.05 m and bob mass 0.15 kg swings with small arc amplitude 0.231 m where g = 9.81 m s⁻². Calculate its speed at the equilibrium position.
items.workedSolution: Angular frequency ω = √(g / L) = √(9.81 / 1.05), so maximum speed v_max = ω x₀ = 0.706 m s⁻¹.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes ω² x₀ = (g / L) x₀ (maximum acceleration) instead of ω x₀ = √(g / L) x₀.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Treats the horizontal arc amplitude x₀ as a vertical free-fall drop height h in √(2gh).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts g / L inside √(g / L) when computing ω x₀.

items.stem: Engineers monitoring a studio loudspeaker voice-coil cone measure simple harmonic motion of amplitude 0.04 m and angular frequency 30 rad s⁻¹. Determine the speed |v| = ω√(x₀² − x²) at displacement x = 0.024 m.
items.workedSolution: Using v = ω√(x₀² − x²) gives v = 30 × √(0.04² − 0.024²) = 0.960 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into v = ω√(x₀² − x²) to obtain 0.960 m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: During a bathymetric laser-ranging tank, a laser emits light of vacuum wavelength 650 nm (c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) that passes from dense flint glass (n₁ = 1.65) into liquid ethanol (n₂ = 1.36) at an angle of incidence of 26° to the normal. What is the wavelength of this light inside liquid ethanol?
items.workedSolution: Wave frequency remains unchanged across the boundary, while phase speed decreases to v₂ = c / n₂. Hence λ₂ = λ₀ / n₂ = 650 / 1.36 = 478 nm.

markScheme.criterion: Uses λ₂ = λ₀ / n₂ = 650 / 1.36 to obtain 478 nm (C).

items.stem: A refractometer cell in a subsea ROV camera viewport test immerses a polished dielectric slab in distilled water (n₂ = 1.33), recording a critical angle of 33.3° relative to the boundary normal. Determine the refractive index n₁ of the dielectric slab.
items.workedSolution: At the critical angle, n₁ sin θ_c = n₂ sin 90° = n₂, so n₁ = 1.33 / sin 33.3° = 2.42.

markScheme.criterion: Computes n₁ = n₂ / sin θ_c = 1.33 / sin 33.3° = 2.42 (D).

items.workedSolution: At the core–cladding boundary, sin θ_c = n_clad / n_core = 1.39 / 1.49 = 0.9329, giving θ_c = 68.9°.

items.stem: A monochromatic ray in water of refractive index 1.33 is coupled at 9.9° to the axis into a straight 60 m optical fiber (n_core = 1.5, n_clad = 1.44) during a borehole geophysical telemetry line. Calculate the total ray path length inside the 60 m fiber.
items.workedSolution: Inside the core, sin θ_axis = (1.33 sin 9.9°) / 1.5 ⇒ θ_axis = 8.77°. The total zig-zag geometric path length is L_ray = L / cos θ_axis = 60 / cos 8.769° = 60.7 m.

markScheme.criterion: Finds θ_axis = 8.77° and computes L / cos θ_axis = 60.7 m (B).

items.stem: In a botanical loupe magnifier bench, a thin converging lens of focal length 0.24 m is used as a simple magnifier so that an object of height 0.012 m forms an upright virtual image 0.960 m in front of the lens (v = −0.960 m in the real-is-positive convention). At what object distance u in front of the lens is the object held?
items.workedSolution: For a virtual image in the real-is-positive convention, v = -0.960 m. Thus 1/u = 1/f − 1/v = 1/0.24 − (1/-0.9600) = 5.208 m⁻¹, giving u = 0.192 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes negative v = -0.960 m into 1/u = 1/f − 1/v to obtain u = 0.192 m (A).

items.stem: A 0.64 kg test mass in a frictionless air-track glider coupled to a calibrated coil spring executes horizontal simple harmonic motion of amplitude 0.025 m and period T = 1.34 s. Calculate the stiffness k of the spring.
items.workedSolution: Rearranging T = 2π√(m / k) gives k = 4π²m / T² = 4π²(0.64) / (1.34)² = 14.0 N m⁻¹.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts m / T² when rearranging the period equation.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Fails to square 2π / T when rearranging T = 2π√(m / k), computing 2πm / T instead of 4π²m / T².

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 4π² and computes m / T².

items.stem: A 0.6 kg mass suspended vertically from a spring of stiffness 25 N m⁻¹ in an inertial seismometer calibration trolley is pulled down 0.024 m below equilibrium and released (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). What is the period T of the resulting vertical simple harmonic motion?
items.workedSolution: Gravity shifts the equilibrium position without altering effective stiffness k, so T = 2π√(m / k) = 2π√(0.6 / 25) = 0.973 s.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Swaps m/k and k/m inside the square root.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Incorrectly adds weight mg to spring stiffness k, assuming gravity changes the vertical mass-spring period.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes the oscillation amplitude x₀ into a pendulum-style formula 2π√(x₀ / g) instead of 2π√(m / k).

items.stem: Engineers timing a physics laboratory light-gate timing pendulum use a 0.15 kg bob on a 2.4 m light cord swinging with arc amplitude 0.6 m (g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Calculate the period T.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 2π and evaluates √(L / g) = 1 / ω.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the half-period π√(L / g) instead of the full period 2π√(L / g).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts L / g inside the square root.

items.stem: In an ultrasonic surgical transducer tip, an oscillator undergoes SHM at 8 Hz with amplitude 0.05 m (passing through x = -0.0225 m). Calculate the peak acceleration magnitude a_max = (2πf)² x₀.
items.workedSolution: With ω = 2π(8) = 50.27 rad s⁻¹, maximum acceleration magnitude a_max = ω² x₀ = 126 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ω = 2πf and obtains 126 m s⁻² (D).

items.stem: In a micro-electro-mechanical resonant beam, a 1.2 kg mass undergoes SHM with ω = 20 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude 0.04 m (with a sensor at x = 0.024 m). Calculate the frequency f_E at which the kinetic energy completes full cycles.
items.workedSolution: Mechanical frequency f = ω / (2π) = 20 / (2π) = 3.183 Hz. Because kinetic energy reaches a maximum twice per mechanical period, f_E = 2f = ω / π = 6.37 Hz.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Halves the mechanical frequency instead of doubling it.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Gives the mechanical displacement frequency f = ω / (2π) instead of recognizing that E_k ∝ cos²(ωt) oscillates at 2f.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates 2ω in rad s⁻¹ without dividing by 2π to convert to hertz.

items.stem: Within a precision Abbe refractometer cell, a beam of vacuum wavelength 670 nm (c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) strikes a planar liquid ethanol–crystalline zircon interface (n₁ = 1.36, n₂ = 1.92) at 42° to the normal. At what speed does the refracted wave propagate in crystalline zircon?
items.workedSolution: From the definition of refractive index n₂ = c / v₂, the wave speed in crystalline zircon is v₂ = (3.00 × 10⁸) / 1.92 = 1.56 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Computes v₂ = c / n₂ = 3.00 × 10⁸ / 1.92 = 1.56 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹ (A).

items.stem: A parallel-faced optical crown glass plate of thickness 0.06 m and refractive index 1.52 sits in dry air (n₀ = 1) on a submarine periscope window assembly. A monochromatic beam enters at 44° to the normal. Calculate the perpendicular lateral shift d of the emerging parallel beam.
items.workedSolution: By Snell's law, sin θ₁ = (1 sin 44°) / 1.52 ⇒ θ₁ = 27.2°. The perpendicular lateral displacement of the emergent ray is d = t₁ sin(θ₀ − θ₁) / cos θ₁ = 0.0195 m.

items.stem: A 60 m step-index optical fiber in a short-reach datacenter patch cord has core refractive index 1.52 and cladding refractive index 1.46, with its flat input face in air of refractive index 1.00 (currently aligned with a test ray at 15.8°). What is the maximum external launch angle θ_max to the fiber axis for which rays remain guided by total internal reflection?
items.workedSolution: At the grazing limit, sin θ_c = 1.46 / 1.52, so inside the core sin θ_axis,max = cos θ_c = √(1 − (n_clad / n_core)²). By Snell's law at the entry face, n_ext sin θ_max = √(n_core² − n_clad²) = 0.4228, giving θ_max = arcsin(0.4228) = 25.0°.

markScheme.criterion: Uses n_ext sin θ_max = √(n_core² − n_clad²) to obtain θ_max = 25.0° (D).

items.stem: Engineers evaluating bit-rate limits for a high-voltage substation optical isolator link test a 360 m step-index waveguide (n_core = 1.6, n_clad = 1.5, n_ext = 1.00, ray shown at 20.3°). Take c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹. Determine the multipath dispersion delay Δt between extreme guided rays and axial rays.
items.workedSolution: Axial transit time t_min = n_core L / c = (1.6 × 360) / (3.00 × 10⁸) = 1.92 × 10⁻⁶ s. At the critical angle sin θ_c = n_clad / n_core, t_max = t_min / sin θ_c = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 2.05 × 10⁻⁶ s. Modal delay Δt = t_max − t_min = 1.28 × 10⁻⁷ s.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δt = (n_core L / c)(n_core / n_clad − 1) = 1.28 × 10⁻⁷ s (B).

items.stem: Within a museum conservation inspection magnifier, an upright scale mark of height 0.018 m sits 0.048 m from a thin convex lens of focal length 0.08 m. Applying 1/f = 1/u + 1/v in the real-is-positive convention, determine the signed image position v.
items.workedSolution: Because u = 0.048 m < f = 0.08 m, 1/v = 1/0.08 − 1/0.048 = -8.333 m⁻¹, giving a signed virtual image distance v = -0.120 m.

markScheme.criterion: Computes 1/v = 1/0.08 − 1/0.048 to obtain signed v = -0.120 m (A).

items.stem: During optical testing on a clinical optometry phoropter test cell, a 0.05 m illuminated target sits 0.6 m from a thin diverging lens of focal length −0.2 m. Determine the signed image position v under the real-is-positive sign convention.
items.workedSolution: For a diverging lens, f = −0.2 m. Using 1/f = 1/u + 1/v gives 1/v = −1/0.2 − 1/0.6 = -6.667 m⁻¹, so v = -0.150 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses negative f = −0.2 m in 1/v = 1/f − 1/u to obtain v = -0.150 m (C).

options.distractorRationale: Forgets that a diverging lens has negative focal length f < 0, substituting +|f| into 1/v = 1/f − 1/u.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes the correct magnitude |v| but omits the negative sign required for a virtual image in the real-is-positive convention.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Stops at 1/v = −1/|f| − 1/u in m⁻¹ without taking the reciprocal to find v in metres.

items.stem: In a robotics compliant-actuator test carriage, a 0.4 kg mass hangs from a vertical spring of constant 25 N m⁻¹ and executes vertical SHM of amplitude 0.055 m (take g = 9.8 m s⁻²). Calculate the static equilibrium extension Δx_eq from the spring's unstretched length.
items.workedSolution: At static equilibrium, upward spring tension balances weight: k Δx_eq = mg ⇒ Δx_eq = (0.4 × 9.8) / 25 = 0.157 m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Hooke's law as k / (mg) instead of mg / k.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Adds the oscillation amplitude x₀ to mg / k, finding maximum total stretch rather than static equilibrium extension.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides mass m directly by spring constant k without multiplying by gravitational field strength g.

items.stem: A simple pendulum of length 1.15 m and bob mass 0.18 kg in a lecture-hall rigid-ceiling wire pendulum executes small-angle oscillations of arc amplitude 0.115 m in a field where g = 9.8 m s⁻². Determine its period T.
items.workedSolution: For small angles, T = 2π√(L / g) = 2π√(1.15 / 9.8) = 2.15 s (independent of bob mass).

markScheme.criterion: Obtains 2.15 s using g = 9.8 m s⁻² (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes the half-period π√(L / g) for a single swing from one extreme to the other rather than a complete cycle.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Incorrectly includes the bob mass m inside the pendulum period equation.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Swaps L / g and g / L inside the square root, computing 2π√(g / L).

items.stem: During calibration of a quartz crystal tuning-fork tine vibrating at f = 4 Hz and amplitude 0.1 m, a laser sensor records an instantaneous displacement x = 0.075 m. Determine the signed SHM acceleration a at that instant.
items.workedSolution: Angular frequency ω = 2πf = 2π(4) = 25.13 rad s⁻¹. By the defining SHM equation, a = −ω²x = −(25.13)²(0.075) = -47.4 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ω = 2πf and obtains -47.4 m s⁻² (D).

options.distractorRationale: Omits the restoring minus sign in a = −ω²x, giving acceleration in the same sign as displacement instead of toward equilibrium.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes cyclic frequency f directly for angular frequency ω, computing −f²x instead of −(2πf)²x.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates −ωx instead of −ω²x, forgetting to square the angular frequency.

items.stem: A harmonic oscillator in a vibrometer calibration shaker table moves with amplitude x₀ = 0.05 m and angular frequency ω = 15 rad s⁻¹. Calculate its speed when passing through displacement x = 0.03 m.
items.workedSolution: Using v = ω√(x₀² − x²) gives v = 15 × √(0.05² − 0.03²) = 0.600 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into v = ω√(x₀² − x²) to obtain 0.600 m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: To identify an unknown transparent solid on a microfluidic refractive-index sensor, a beam in distilled water (n₁ = 1.33) is directed onto its flat surface at 30° to the normal. The refracted beam inside the sample travels at 15.9° to the normal. What is the refractive index n₂ of the sample?
items.workedSolution: Rearranging Snell's law n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂ gives n₂ = 1.33 × sin 30° / sin 15.9° = 2.42.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates n₂ = n₁ sin θ₁ / sin θ₂ = 2.42 (C).

items.stem: Engineers designing a beam-turning prism on a photovoltaic encapsulant test coupon send a ray in optical diamond (n₁ = 2.42, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) onto liquid ethanol (n₂ = 1.36) at 43° to the normal. What is the angular deflection δ between the incident direction and the emerging reflected ray?
items.workedSolution: Since sin θ_c = 1.36 / 2.42 gives θ_c = 34.2° and θ₁ = 43° > θ_c, the beam undergoes total internal reflection with θ_r = 43°. The angular deviation from the original forward direction is δ = 180° − 2(43°) = 94.0°.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies TIR (θ₁ > θ_c = 34.2°) and computes δ = 180° − 2θ₁ = 94.0° (D).

items.stem: An over-angled ray in water (n_ext = 1.33) is launched at 26.4° to the central axis into a 350 m step-index waveguide (n_core = 1.5, n_clad = 1.44) during a structural-health bridge sensor lead. At what angle to the cylindrical wall normal does the leaked ray refract into the cladding?
items.workedSolution: At entry, sin θ_axis = (1.33 sin 26.4°) / 1.5 ⇒ θ_axis = 23.2°. The angle to the wall normal is θ_w = 90° − θ_axis = 66.8° (< θ_c = 73.7°). Refracting into the cladding: sin θ_clad = (1.5 sin θ_w) / 1.44, giving θ_clad = 73.2°.

markScheme.criterion: Finds θ_w = 66.8° and refracts into cladding to obtain 73.2° (D).

items.stem: A multimode step-index fiber of length 500 m in a railway trackside acoustic-sensing fiber has n_core = 1.58 and n_clad = 1.49 in air (n_ext = 1.00, illustrated with a 22.2° launch ray). Taking c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹ and neglecting material dispersion, what is the maximum multipath (modal) pulse broadening Δt between the fastest axial ray and the slowest guided ray?
items.workedSolution: Axial transit time t_min = n_core L / c = (1.58 × 500) / (3.00 × 10⁸) = 2.63 × 10⁻⁶ s. At the critical angle sin θ_c = n_clad / n_core, t_max = t_min / sin θ_c = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 2.79 × 10⁻⁶ s. Modal delay Δt = t_max − t_min = 1.59 × 10⁻⁷ s.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δt = (n_core L / c)(n_core / n_clad − 1) = 1.59 × 10⁻⁷ s (B).

items.stem: A concave diverging lens with focal length f = −0.12 m in a pulsed-laser divergence compensator forms an image of an object of height 0.05 m placed at object distance u = 0.072 m. Using 1/f = 1/u + 1/v, calculate the signed image distance v.
items.workedSolution: For a diverging lens, f = −0.12 m. Using 1/f = 1/u + 1/v gives 1/v = −1/0.12 − 1/0.072 = -22.22 m⁻¹, so v = -0.0450 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses negative f = −0.12 m in 1/v = 1/f − 1/u to obtain v = -0.0450 m (B).

items.stem: In a calibration run of a precision marine-chronometer balance-mass rig, a 1.2 kg carriage oscillates horizontally with amplitude 0.025 m on a spring of stiffness 32 N m⁻¹. Determine the frequency f in hertz.
items.workedSolution: Natural frequency f = (1 / 2π)√(k / m) = (1 / 2π)√(32 / 1.2) = 0.822 Hz.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes the period T = 2π√(m / k) instead of frequency f = 1 / T.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Swaps k/m and m/k, computing (1 / 2π)√(m / k) instead of (1 / 2π)√(k / m).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Reports angular frequency ω = √(k / m) in rad s⁻¹ without dividing by 2π.

items.stem: In an evacuated bell-jar precision timing pendulum, a small dense bob of mass 0.25 kg hangs on a light inextensible cord of length 0.49 m and swings with small arc amplitude 0.0294 m. Taking g = 9.8 m s⁻², what is the oscillation frequency f?

markScheme.criterion: Obtains 0.712 Hz using g = 9.8 m s⁻² (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Reports the angular frequency ω = √(g / L) without dividing by 2π.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the period T instead of the frequency f = 1 / T.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts g / L inside the radical, computing (1 / 2π)√(L / g) instead of (1 / 2π)√(g / L).

items.stem: A 0.15 kg pendulum bob suspended from a 0.72 m wire in a mine-shaft gravity-anomaly survey pendulum oscillates in SHM with arc amplitude 0.18 m (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). What is the maximum speed v_max of the bob?
items.workedSolution: Angular frequency ω = √(g / L) = √(9.81 / 0.72), so maximum speed v_max = ω x₀ = 0.664 m s⁻¹.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts g / L inside √(g / L) when computing ω x₀.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Treats the horizontal arc amplitude x₀ as a vertical free-fall drop height h in √(2gh).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes ω² x₀ = (g / L) x₀ (maximum acceleration) instead of ω x₀ = √(g / L) x₀.

items.stem: In a tall-building tuned mass damper block, a stage oscillates in simple harmonic motion with angular frequency ω = 40 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude x₀ = 0.06 m, tracing the velocity–displacement ellipse shown. What is the speed v of the stage when its displacement from equilibrium is x = 0.0216 m?
items.workedSolution: Using v = ω√(x₀² − x²) gives v = 40 × √(0.06² − 0.0216²) = 2.24 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into v = ω√(x₀² − x²) to obtain 2.24 m s⁻¹ (B).

options.distractorRationale: Calculates the maximum speed ωx₀ at equilibrium (x = 0) instead of the speed at x.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates ω(x₀ − x) linearly instead of taking √(x₀² − x²).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses ωx instead of ω√(x₀² − x²), mistakenly assuming speed is directly proportional to displacement.

items.stem: In a dynamic mechanical thermal-analyzer probe, a 1.2 kg oscillator moves harmonically at ω = 30 rad s⁻¹ with amplitude x₀ = 0.06 m (sampled at 0.048 m). At what positive displacement x from equilibrium is its kinetic energy equal to its potential energy (E_k = E_p)?
items.workedSolution: Setting E_p = ½E_tot gives ½mω²x² = ½(½mω²x₀²), so x² = x₀² / 2 and x = x₀ / √2 = 0.06 / √2 = 0.0424 m.

markScheme.criterion: Solves x² = x₀² / 2 to obtain x = x₀ / √2 = 0.0424 m (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Squares the ½ factor to obtain x₀ / 4 instead of taking the square root x₀ / √2.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Assumes E_k = E_p occurs at half the amplitude (x₀ / 2, where E_p = ¼E_tot) instead of x₀ / √2.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes (√3 / 2)x₀ (where E_p = ¾E_tot) instead of x₀ / √2.

items.stem: In a planetary lander atmospheric nephelometer, a light ray inside dense flint glass (n₁ = 1.65, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) approaches a planar interface with fused-silica glass (n₂ = 1.46) at an incident angle of 68° to the normal. What is the critical angle θ_c at this dense flint glass–fused-silica glass boundary?
items.workedSolution: At the critical angle θ_c, sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1.46 / 1.65 = 0.8848, giving θ_c = arcsin(0.8848) = 62.2°.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1.46 / 1.65 to obtain θ_c = 62.2° (A).

items.stem: A parallel-sided optical window of optical crown glass (refractive index 1.52, thickness 0.085 m) immersed in dry air (n₀ = 1) is illuminated at 38° to the normal in a spectrophotometer cuvette wall. Calculate the transverse shift t₁ tan θ₁ of the ray along the exit boundary.
items.workedSolution: Inside the optical crown glass slab, sin θ₁ = (1 sin 38°) / 1.52, giving θ₁ = 23.9°. The transverse shift along the exit face is Δy = t₁ tan θ₁ = 0.085 × tan 23.89° = 0.0377 m.

items.stem: A monochromatic ray in water of refractive index 1.33 is coupled at 8.9° to the axis into a straight 60 m optical fiber (n_core = 1.48, n_clad = 1.41) during an astronomical echelle-spectrograph feed. Calculate the total ray path length inside the 60 m fiber.
items.workedSolution: Inside the core, sin θ_axis = (1.33 sin 8.9°) / 1.48 ⇒ θ_axis = 7.99°. The total zig-zag geometric path length is L_ray = L / cos θ_axis = 60 / cos 7.992° = 60.6 m.

markScheme.criterion: Finds θ_axis = 7.99° and computes L / cos θ_axis = 60.6 m (B).

items.stem: A 2400 m multimode step-index cable in a cryogenic laboratory optical feedthrough has core index 1.62 and cladding index 1.51 in air (n_ext = 1.00, sample launch angle 14.4°, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹). Calculate the maximum guided transit time through the fiber.
items.workedSolution: Wave speed in the core is v = c / n_core, and the critical-angle ray travels path length L / sin θ_c = L (n_core / n_clad). Therefore t_max = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 1.39 × 10⁻⁵ s.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates t_max = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 1.39 × 10⁻⁵ s (D).

items.stem: In a retinal fundus imaging objective rig, a thin converging lens of focal length 0.25 m is used as a simple magnifier so that an object of height 0.008 m forms an upright virtual image 0.750 m in front of the lens (v = −0.750 m in the real-is-positive convention). At what object distance u in front of the lens is the object held?
items.workedSolution: For a virtual image in the real-is-positive convention, v = -0.750 m. Thus 1/u = 1/f − 1/v = 1/0.25 − (1/-0.7500) = 5.333 m⁻¹, giving u = 0.188 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes negative v = -0.750 m into 1/u = 1/f − 1/v to obtain u = 0.188 m (A).

items.stem: A 1.2 kg test mass in a structural vibration-isolation test sled on linear bearings executes horizontal simple harmonic motion of amplitude 0.025 m and period T = 1.40 s. Calculate the stiffness k of the spring.
items.workedSolution: Rearranging T = 2π√(m / k) gives k = 4π²m / T² = 4π²(1.2) / (1.40)² = 24.0 N m⁻¹.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts m / T² when rearranging the period equation.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 4π² and computes m / T².

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Fails to square 2π / T when rearranging T = 2π√(m / k), computing 2πm / T instead of 4π²m / T².

items.stem: A vertical helical spring of stiffness 100 N m⁻¹ in a cryogenic cooler linear-compressor piston assembly suspends a load of mass 0.2 kg that subsequently oscillates vertically with amplitude 0.055 m. Taking g = 9.81 m s⁻², what was the static extension Δx_eq of the spring at equilibrium before oscillation started?
items.workedSolution: At static equilibrium, upward spring tension balances weight: k Δx_eq = mg ⇒ Δx_eq = (0.2 × 9.81) / 100 = 0.0196 m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Divides mass m directly by spring constant k without multiplying by gravitational field strength g.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Adds the oscillation amplitude x₀ to mg / k, finding maximum total stretch rather than static equilibrium extension.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Hooke's law as k / (mg) instead of mg / k.

items.stem: Engineers timing an astronomical observatory sidereal regulator pendulum use a 0.6 kg bob on a 1.3 m light cord swinging with arc amplitude 0.325 m (g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Calculate the period T.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Omits the square root on L / g.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the half-period π√(L / g) instead of the full period 2π√(L / g).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts L / g inside the square root.

items.stem: In a studio loudspeaker voice-coil cone, a component executes simple harmonic motion at frequency f = 6 Hz with amplitude x₀ = 0.03 m, as represented on the acceleration–displacement graph. Taking displacement to the right as positive, what is its signed acceleration a when x = -0.0105 m?
items.workedSolution: Angular frequency ω = 2πf = 2π(6) = 37.70 rad s⁻¹. By the defining SHM equation, a = −ω²x = −(37.70)²(-0.0105) = 14.9 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ω = 2πf and obtains 14.9 m s⁻² (C).

items.stem: In a magnetic-levitation harmonic test puck, a 0.25 kg mass undergoes SHM with ω = 18 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude 0.06 m (with a sensor at x = 0.015 m). Calculate the frequency f_E at which the kinetic energy completes full cycles.
items.workedSolution: Mechanical frequency f = ω / (2π) = 18 / (2π) = 2.865 Hz. Because kinetic energy reaches a maximum twice per mechanical period, f_E = 2f = ω / π = 5.73 Hz.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates 2ω in rad s⁻¹ without dividing by 2π to convert to hertz.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Gives the mechanical displacement frequency f = ω / (2π) instead of recognizing that E_k ∝ cos²(ωt) oscillates at 2f.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Halves the mechanical frequency instead of doubling it.

items.stem: A beam-steering prism assembly on a subsea ROV camera viewport test guides light (c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) inside dense flint glass (n₁ = 1.65) toward a planar interface with fused-silica glass (n₂ = 1.46) at an incidence angle of 79° measured from the normal.
items.workedSolution: (a) sin θ_c = 1.46 / 1.65, so θ_c = 62.2°. (b) Because n₁ > n₂ and θ₁ > θ_c, total internal reflection occurs at the interface. (c) Wave speed v₁ = 3.00 × 10⁸ / 1.65 = 1.82 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, and angular deviation δ = 180° − 2(79°) = 22.0°.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1.46 / 1.65.
States total internal reflection because the ray is in the higher-index medium with incident angle greater than the critical angle.

parts.expectedAnswer: Total internal reflection occurs because light travels in the medium of higher refractive index and the incident angle exceeds the critical angle.
workingSteps: Compare incident angle with critical angle in the optically denser medium to confirm total internal reflection.

parts.prompt: Calculate the angular deviation of the reflected ray from the incident ray's original forward direction, and find the wave speed in the first medium.
workingSteps: Wave speed in dense flint glass: v₁ = c / n₁ = 1.82 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹.
Angular deviation under total internal reflection: δ = 180° − 2(79°) = 22.0°.

items.stem: Engineers characterizing a borehole geophysical telemetry line couple a laser beam from air of refractive index 1.00 at 12° to the axis into a straight 750 m step-index waveguide (core index 1.48, cladding index 1.41).
items.workedSolution: (a) θ_c = arcsin(1.41 / 1.48) = 72.3°. (b) Using n_ext sin θ_max = √(n_core² − n_clad²) gives θ_max = 26.7°. (c) For θ_in = 12°, θ_axis = 8.08° and L_ray = 750 / cos θ_axis = 758 m.

markScheme.criterion: Applies 1 sin θ_max = n_core sin(90° − θ_c).
Finds θ_axis = 8.08° and evaluates L / cos θ_axis.

items.stem: An experimental arrangement of a frictionless air-track glider coupled to a calibrated coil spring comprises a block of mass m = 1.5 kg attached to an ideal horizontal spring of stiffness k = 72 N m⁻¹. The block oscillates in simple harmonic motion with amplitude x₀ = 0.09 m.

Divides F_max by m (or multiplies ω² by x₀).

items.stem: In a lecture-hall rigid-ceiling wire pendulum, a pendulum bob of mass m = 0.8 kg suspended on a light cord of length L = 1.3 m oscillates in small-angle simple harmonic motion with arc amplitude x₀ = 0.325 m. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) T = 2π√(1.3 / 9.81) = 2.29 s. (b) v_max = √(9.81 / 1.3) × 0.325 = 0.893 m s⁻¹. (c) Lowest-point cord tension = m(g + v_max² / L) = 8.34 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies v_max = ω x₀ = (2π / T) x₀.
Uses T_cord = mg + mv_max² / L at the bottom of the arc.

parts.prompt: Calculate the period T of the pendulum.
Calculate the maximum speed v_max of the bob as it passes through equilibrium.
Determine the tension in the suspension cord as the bob passes through its lowest point.

items.stem: In a micro-electro-mechanical resonant beam, a mass m = 0.6 kg oscillates in undamped simple harmonic motion with angular frequency ω = 10 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude x₀ = 0.08 m. The parabolic energy–displacement curves are analyzed at displacement x = 0.02 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes m = 0.6 kg, ω = 10 rad s⁻¹, and x₀ = 0.08 m into E_tot = ½mω²x₀².
Applies E_k = ½mω²(x₀² − x²) or E_tot − ½mω²x².
Sets E_p = ½E_tot to obtain x = x₀ / √2.

parts.prompt: Calculate the total mechanical energy E_tot of the oscillating mass.
Calculate the kinetic energy E_k of the mass when its displacement is x = 0.02 m.
workingSteps: E_k = E_tot − E_p = ½mω²(x₀² − x²) = 0.180 J.

parts.prompt: Determine the positive displacement x from equilibrium at which kinetic energy equals potential energy.

items.stem: In a submarine periscope window assembly, a narrow monochromatic beam in dry air (refractive index n₀ = 1) strikes a parallel-sided block of optical crown glass (refractive index n₁ = 1.52, thickness 0.075 m) at an angle of incidence of 44° to the normal and emerges back into dry air on the far side.
items.workedSolution: (a) Snells invariant n₀ sin θ₀ = 1 sin 44° = 0.695 (emergent angle = 44°). (b) Inside the slab, θ₁ = arcsin(0.6947 / 1.52) = 27.2°, so Δy = 0.075 tan θ₁ = 0.0385 m. (c) Perpendicular lateral displacement d = t₁ sin(θ₀ − θ₁) / cos θ₁ = 0.0244 m.

markScheme.criterion: Finds θ₁ = 27.2° and applies Δy = t₁ tan θ₁.
Applies d = t₁ sin(θ₀ − θ₁) / cos θ₁ or (t₁ tan θ₀ − Δy) cos θ₀.

parts.prompt: State the emergent angle of refraction in dry air and calculate the optical Snell invariant n₀ sin θ₀.
workingSteps: Because both outer media have refractive index 1 and the faces are parallel, the emergent angle equals 44°.
Snell invariant = n₀ sin θ₀ = 1 × sin 44° = 0.695.

parts.prompt: Calculate the transverse offset Δy = t₁ tan θ₁ of the ray between the entry normal and exit normal along the slab face.
Hence calculate the perpendicular lateral displacement d between the emergent ray and the original incident ray line.
workingSteps: d = (t₁ tan θ₀ − Δy) cos θ₀ = t₁ sin(θ₀ − θ₁) / cos θ₁ = 0.0244 m.

items.stem: A 360 m multimode step-index optical fiber in a high-voltage substation optical isolator link has a core of refractive index n_core = 1.49 and cladding of refractive index n_clad = 1.39 in air (n_ext = 1.00, shown with a guided ray launched at 16.2°). Take the speed of light in vacuum to be c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) t_axial = n_core L / c = (1.49 × 360) / 3.00 × 10⁸ = 1.79 × 10⁻⁶ s. (b) Longest guided ray has path L / sin θ_c = L n_core / n_clad, giving t_max = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 1.92 × 10⁻⁶ s. (c) Modal pulse delay Δt = t_max − t_axial = 1.29 × 10⁻⁷ s.

markScheme.criterion: Uses t_axial = n_core L / c with n_core = 1.49 and L = 360 m.
Applies L_max = L (n_core / n_clad) to find t_max = t_axial (n_core / n_clad).

items.stem: Engineers testing a subsea ROV camera viewport test direct a narrow beam of vacuum wavelength 405 nm (c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) through crystalline zircon (n₁ = 1.92) onto a smooth optical crown glass surface (n₂ = 1.52) at an incidence angle of 30° to the boundary normal.
items.workedSolution: (a) Inside optical crown glass, v₂ = c / n₂ = 1.97 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹ and λ₂ = λ₀ / n₂ = 405 / 1.52 = 266 nm. (b) By Snell's law, sin θ₂ = (1.92 sin 30°) / 1.52, giving θ₂ = 39.2°. (c) Angular deviation δ = |θ₂ − θ₁| = 9.17°.

items.stem: A 200 m step-index waveguide deployed in a structural-health bridge sensor lead comprises a glass core (n_core = 1.55) surrounded by lower-index cladding (n_clad = 1.47). Monochromatic light enters from air (n_ext = 1.00) at an angle of 15° to the fiber axis.

items.stem: A simple pendulum rig in a seismic base-isolation pendulum test frame carries a 0.4 kg sphere on a 0.4 m wire, swinging with small-angle arc amplitude 0.08 m where g = 9.81 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) T = 2π√(0.4 / 9.81) = 1.27 s. (b) v_max = √(9.81 / 0.4) × 0.08 = 0.396 m s⁻¹. (c) Lowest-point cord tension = m(g + v_max² / L) = 4.08 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies v_max = ω x₀ = (2π / T) x₀.
Uses T_cord = mg + mv_max² / L at the bottom of the arc.

items.stem: A beam-steering prism assembly on a gemstone goniometer calibration rig guides light (c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) inside polycarbonate polymer (n₁ = 1.58) toward a planar interface with dry air (n₂ = 1) at an incidence angle of 56° measured from the normal.
items.workedSolution: (a) sin θ_c = 1 / 1.58, so θ_c = 39.3°. (b) Because n₁ > n₂ and θ₁ > θ_c, total internal reflection occurs at the interface. (c) Wave speed v₁ = 3.00 × 10⁸ / 1.58 = 1.90 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, and angular deviation δ = 180° − 2(56°) = 68.0°.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1 / 1.58.
States total internal reflection because the ray is in the higher-index medium with incident angle greater than the critical angle.

items.stem: In a semiconductor wafer-alignment imaging head, an upright object of height h_o = 0.018 m is held at a distance u = 0.2 m in front of a thin converging magnifying lens of focal length f = 0.25 m. Use the real-is-positive sign convention (1/f = 1/u + 1/v, m = −v/u).
items.workedSolution: (a) 1/v = 1/0.25 − 1/0.2 ⇒ v = -1.00 m (virtual, since v < 0). (b) m = −v / u = 5.00. (c) Upright virtual image height h_i = m h_o = 0.0900 m.

items.stem: In a railway bogie secondary-suspension scale model, a load of mass m = 0.75 kg hangs at rest from a vertical spring of spring constant k = 25 N m⁻¹. It is then pulled vertically downward by x₀ = 0.024 m from equilibrium and released. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Δx_eq = mg / k = (0.75 × 9.81) / 25 = 0.294 m. (b) T = 2π√(0.75 / 25) = 1.09 s. (c) Maximum net SHM acceleration a_max = (k / m) x₀ = 0.800 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Uses mg = k Δx_eq with g = 9.81 m s⁻².
Evaluates a_max = ω² x₀ = (k / m) x₀.

parts.prompt: Calculate the static extension Δx_eq of the spring when the mass hangs at rest in equilibrium.
Calculate the period T of the vertical simple harmonic oscillations.
Determine the magnitude of the maximum net acceleration a_max of the mass during the oscillation.

items.stem: The acceleration–displacement phase graph for a studio loudspeaker voice-coil cone corresponds to simple harmonic motion of frequency 6 Hz and amplitude 0.05 m, with a measurement taken at displacement x = 0.0175 m.
items.workedSolution: (a) ω = 2π(6) = 37.7 rad s⁻¹. (b) At x = 0.0175 m, a = −ω²x = -24.9 m s⁻². (c) Maximum acceleration magnitude a_max = ω² x₀ = 71.1 m s⁻².

items.stem: In a gemstone goniometer calibration rig, a collimated laser beam of vacuum wavelength 515 nm (speed of light in vacuum c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) travels in distilled water of refractive index n₁ = 1.33 and strikes a flat boundary with fused-silica glass of refractive index n₂ = 1.46 at an angle of incidence of 18° to the normal.
items.workedSolution: (a) Inside fused-silica glass, v₂ = c / n₂ = 2.05 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹ and λ₂ = λ₀ / n₂ = 515 / 1.46 = 353 nm. (b) By Snell's law, sin θ₂ = (1.33 sin 18°) / 1.46, giving θ₂ = 16.3°. (c) Angular deviation δ = |θ₂ − θ₁| = 1.65°.

markScheme.criterion: Obtains λ₂ = 353 nm (with v₂ = 2.05 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹).
Substitutes n₁ = 1.33, θ₁ = 18°, and n₂ = 1.46 into n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂.

items.stem: A precision optical compensator in an ophthalmic lens-blank inspection jig uses a flat, parallel-sided crystalline zircon plate of thickness 0.05 m and refractive index 1.92 surrounded by dry air (n₀ = 1). An incident ray meets the entry face at 44° to the normal.
items.workedSolution: (a) Snells invariant n₀ sin θ₀ = 1 sin 44° = 0.695 (emergent angle = 44°). (b) Inside the slab, θ₁ = arcsin(0.6947 / 1.92) = 21.2°, so Δy = 0.05 tan θ₁ = 0.0194 m. (c) Perpendicular lateral displacement d = t₁ sin(θ₀ − θ₁) / cos θ₁ = 0.0208 m.

markScheme.criterion: Finds θ₁ = 21.2° and applies Δy = t₁ tan θ₁.
Applies d = t₁ sin(θ₀ − θ₁) / cos θ₁ or (t₁ tan θ₀ − Δy) cos θ₀.

parts.prompt: State the emergent angle of refraction in dry air and calculate the optical Snell invariant n₀ sin θ₀.
workingSteps: Because both outer media have refractive index 1 and the faces are parallel, the emergent angle equals 44°.
Snell invariant = n₀ sin θ₀ = 1 × sin 44° = 0.695.

parts.prompt: Calculate the transverse offset Δy = t₁ tan θ₁ of the ray between the entry normal and exit normal along the slab face.
Hence calculate the perpendicular lateral displacement d between the emergent ray and the original incident ray line.
workingSteps: d = (t₁ tan θ₀ − Δy) cos θ₀ = t₁ sin(θ₀ − θ₁) / cos θ₁ = 0.0208 m.

items.stem: During pulse-broadening tests for a wind-turbine blade strain-monitoring waveguide, engineers transmit narrow laser pulses from air (n_ext = 1.00, sample launch angle 9.9°) along a 360 m step-index fiber of core index 1.5 and cladding index 1.44. Take c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) t_axial = n_core L / c = (1.5 × 360) / 3.00 × 10⁸ = 1.80 × 10⁻⁶ s. (b) Longest guided ray has path L / sin θ_c = L n_core / n_clad, giving t_max = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 1.88 × 10⁻⁶ s. (c) Modal pulse delay Δt = t_max − t_axial = 7.50 × 10⁻⁸ s.

markScheme.criterion: Uses t_axial = n_core L / c with n_core = 1.5 and L = 360 m.
Applies L_max = L (n_core / n_clad) to find t_max = t_axial (n_core / n_clad).

items.stem: Optometry apparatus in a compact viewfinder negative-lens element positions an illuminated test letter of height 0.045 m at u = 0.9 m in front of a thin concave lens of focal length f = −0.3 m. Apply the real-is-positive sign convention throughout.
items.workedSolution: (a) Optical power P = 1 / (−0.3) = -3.33 D. (b) 1/v = −1/0.3 − 1/0.9 ⇒ v = -0.225 m. (c) Axial separation between object and virtual image on the same side = u − |v| = 0.675 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes f = −0.3 m and u = 0.9 m into 1/v = 1/f − 1/u.
Subtracts |v| from u because virtual image and object are on the same side of the lens.

items.stem: A beam-steering prism assembly on an interferometric metrology window guides light (c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) inside crystalline zircon (n₁ = 1.92) toward a planar interface with fused-silica glass (n₂ = 1.46) at an incidence angle of 58° measured from the normal.
items.workedSolution: (a) sin θ_c = 1.46 / 1.92, so θ_c = 49.5°. (b) Because n₁ > n₂ and θ₁ > θ_c, total internal reflection occurs at the interface. (c) Wave speed v₁ = 3.00 × 10⁸ / 1.92 = 1.56 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, and angular deviation δ = 180° − 2(58°) = 64.0°.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1.46 / 1.92.
States total internal reflection because the ray is in the higher-index medium with incident angle greater than the critical angle.

items.workedSolution: (a) θ_c = arcsin(1.45 / 1.54) = 70.3°. (b) Using n_ext sin θ_max = √(n_core² − n_clad²) gives θ_max = 23.0°. (c) For θ_in = 12.4°, θ_axis = 10.7° and L_ray = 60 / cos θ_axis = 61.1 m.

markScheme.criterion: Applies 1.33 sin θ_max = n_core sin(90° − θ_c).

items.stem: In a semiconductor immersion-lithography stage, a narrow monochromatic beam in dry air (refractive index n₀ = 1) strikes a parallel-sided block of dense flint glass (refractive index n₁ = 1.65, thickness 0.05 m) at an angle of incidence of 56° to the normal and emerges back into dry air on the far side.
items.workedSolution: (a) Snells invariant n₀ sin θ₀ = 1 sin 56° = 0.829 (emergent angle = 56°). (b) Inside the slab, θ₁ = arcsin(0.8290 / 1.65) = 30.2°, so Δy = 0.05 tan θ₁ = 0.0291 m. (c) Perpendicular lateral displacement d = t₁ sin(θ₀ − θ₁) / cos θ₁ = 0.0252 m.

markScheme.criterion: Finds θ₁ = 30.2° and applies Δy = t₁ tan θ₁.
Applies d = t₁ sin(θ₀ − θ₁) / cos θ₁ or (t₁ tan θ₀ − Δy) cos θ₀.

parts.prompt: Calculate the transverse offset Δy = t₁ tan θ₁ of the ray between the entry normal and exit normal along the slab face.
Hence calculate the perpendicular lateral displacement d between the emergent ray and the original incident ray line.
workingSteps: d = (t₁ tan θ₀ − Δy) cos θ₀ = t₁ sin(θ₀ − θ₁) / cos θ₁ = 0.0252 m.

items.stem: A 2400 m multimode step-index optical fiber in a surgical laser-lithotripsy delivery fiber has a core of refractive index n_core = 1.55 and cladding of refractive index n_clad = 1.47 in air (n_ext = 1.00, shown with a guided ray launched at 17.7°). Take the speed of light in vacuum to be c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) t_axial = n_core L / c = (1.55 × 2400) / 3.00 × 10⁸ = 1.24 × 10⁻⁵ s. (b) Longest guided ray has path L / sin θ_c = L n_core / n_clad, giving t_max = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 1.31 × 10⁻⁵ s. (c) Modal pulse delay Δt = t_max − t_axial = 6.75 × 10⁻⁷ s.

markScheme.criterion: Uses t_axial = n_core L / c with n_core = 1.55 and L = 2400 m.
Applies L_max = L (n_core / n_clad) to find t_max = t_axial (n_core / n_clad).

items.stem: During close inspection on an aerial reconnaissance camera test collimator, a thin convex lens of focal length 0.25 m is positioned 0.15 m from a fine detail of height 0.015 m. Adopt the real-is-positive sign convention throughout.
items.workedSolution: (a) 1/v = 1/0.25 − 1/0.15 ⇒ v = -0.375 m (virtual, since v < 0). (b) m = −v / u = 2.50. (c) Upright virtual image height h_i = m h_o = 0.0375 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes u = 0.15 m and f = 0.25 m into 1/v = 1/f − 1/u.
Multiplies magnification m by object height h_o.

items.stem: In a cleanroom nanopositioning flexure stage, a load of mass m = 1.2 kg hangs at rest from a vertical spring of spring constant k = 25 N m⁻¹. It is then pulled vertically downward by x₀ = 0.024 m from equilibrium and released. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Δx_eq = mg / k = (1.2 × 9.8) / 25 = 0.470 m. (b) T = 2π√(1.2 / 25) = 1.38 s. (c) Maximum net SHM acceleration a_max = (k / m) x₀ = 0.500 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Uses mg = k Δx_eq with g = 9.8 m s⁻².
Evaluates a_max = ω² x₀ = (k / m) x₀.

parts.prompt: Calculate the static extension Δx_eq of the spring when the mass hangs at rest in equilibrium.
Calculate the period T of the vertical simple harmonic oscillations.
Determine the magnitude of the maximum net acceleration a_max of the mass during the oscillation.

items.stem: In a tall-building tuned mass damper block, a component oscillates in simple harmonic motion at frequency f = 6 Hz with amplitude x₀ = 0.02 m. Its instantaneous state is examined when the displacement from equilibrium is x = 0.012 m.
items.workedSolution: (a) ω = 2π(6) = 37.7 rad s⁻¹. (b) At x = 0.012 m, a = −ω²x = -17.1 m s⁻². (c) Maximum acceleration magnitude a_max = ω² x₀ = 28.4 m s⁻².

items.stem: Engineers testing a spectrophotometer cuvette wall direct a narrow beam of vacuum wavelength 488 nm (c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) through distilled water (n₁ = 1.33) onto a smooth synthetic sapphire surface (n₂ = 1.77) at an incidence angle of 26° to the boundary normal.
items.workedSolution: (a) Inside synthetic sapphire, v₂ = c / n₂ = 1.69 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹ and λ₂ = λ₀ / n₂ = 488 / 1.77 = 276 nm. (b) By Snell's law, sin θ₂ = (1.33 sin 26°) / 1.77, giving θ₂ = 19.2°. (c) Angular deviation δ = |θ₂ − θ₁| = 6.77°.

markScheme.criterion: Obtains λ₂ = 276 nm (with v₂ = 1.69 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹).
Substitutes n₁ = 1.33, θ₁ = 26°, and n₂ = 1.77 into n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂.

items.stem: In a tethered deep-sea ROV umbilical waveguide, a straight 120 m step-index optical fiber has a core of refractive index n_core = 1.54 and a cladding of refractive index n_clad = 1.45. A narrow laser beam in air (n_ext = 1.00) strikes the flat entry face at θ_in = 15.9° to the central axis.
items.workedSolution: (a) sin θ_c = 1.45 / 1.54 ⇒ θ_c = 70.3°. (b) By Snell's law at the end-face, sin θ_axis = (1 sin 15.9°) / 1.54, so θ_axis = 10.2°. (c) Wall incident angle θ_w = 90° − θ_axis = 79.8°, which exceeds θ_c so the ray is guided by TIR.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts θ_axis from 90° to obtain θ_w.

items.stem: In a deep-ocean optical hydrophone window, a narrow monochromatic beam (speed of light in vacuum c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) travels inside synthetic sapphire of refractive index n₁ = 1.77 and strikes a flat boundary with fused-silica glass of refractive index n₂ = 1.46 at an angle of incidence of 68° to the normal.
items.workedSolution: (a) sin θ_c = 1.46 / 1.77, so θ_c = 55.6°. (b) Because n₁ > n₂ and θ₁ > θ_c, total internal reflection occurs at the interface. (c) Wave speed v₁ = 3.00 × 10⁸ / 1.77 = 1.69 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, and angular deviation δ = 180° − 2(68°) = 44.0°.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1.46 / 1.77.
States total internal reflection because the ray is in the higher-index medium with incident angle greater than the critical angle.

items.stem: A vertical suspension stage in a precision watch hairspring linear test bench supports a 0.2 kg mass on an ideal coil spring of stiffness 40 N m⁻¹, oscillating vertically with amplitude 0.024 m about its equilibrium position (take g = 9.8 m s⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) Δx_eq = mg / k = (0.2 × 9.8) / 40 = 0.0490 m. (b) T = 2π√(0.2 / 40) = 0.444 s. (c) Maximum net SHM acceleration a_max = (k / m) x₀ = 4.80 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Uses mg = k Δx_eq with g = 9.8 m s⁻².
Evaluates a_max = ω² x₀ = (k / m) x₀.

Calculate the period T of the vertical simple harmonic oscillations.

items.stem: In a long-case regulator clock calibration rig, a pendulum bob of mass m = 0.4 kg suspended on a light cord of length L = 1.3 m oscillates in small-angle simple harmonic motion with arc amplitude x₀ = 0.364 m. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) T = 2π√(1.3 / 9.81) = 2.29 s. (b) v_max = √(9.81 / 1.3) × 0.364 = 1.000 m s⁻¹. (c) Lowest-point cord tension = m(g + v_max² / L) = 4.23 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies v_max = ω x₀ = (2π / T) x₀.
Uses T_cord = mg + mv_max² / L at the bottom of the arc.

Calculate the maximum speed v_max of the bob as it passes through equilibrium.
Determine the tension in the suspension cord as the bob passes through its lowest point.

items.stem: In a violins bridge laser-Doppler vibration target, a mass m = 0.5 kg oscillates in undamped simple harmonic motion with angular frequency ω = 20 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude x₀ = 0.1 m. The parabolic energy–displacement curves are analyzed at displacement x = 0.08 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes m = 0.5 kg, ω = 20 rad s⁻¹, and x₀ = 0.1 m into E_tot = ½mω²x₀².
Applies E_k = ½mω²(x₀² − x²) or E_tot − ½mω²x².
Sets E_p = ½E_tot to obtain x = x₀ / √2.

parts.prompt: Calculate the total mechanical energy E_tot of the oscillating mass.
Calculate the kinetic energy E_k of the mass when its displacement is x = 0.08 m.
workingSteps: E_k = E_tot − E_p = ½mω²(x₀² − x²) = 0.360 J.

parts.prompt: Determine the positive displacement x from equilibrium at which kinetic energy equals potential energy.

items.stem: In an industrial sugar-brix inline refractometer, a narrow monochromatic beam in dry air (refractive index n₀ = 1) strikes a parallel-sided block of polycarbonate polymer (refractive index n₁ = 1.58, thickness 0.03 m) at an angle of incidence of 50° to the normal and emerges back into dry air on the far side.
items.workedSolution: (a) Snells invariant n₀ sin θ₀ = 1 sin 50° = 0.766 (emergent angle = 50°). (b) Inside the slab, θ₁ = arcsin(0.7660 / 1.58) = 29.0°, so Δy = 0.03 tan θ₁ = 0.0166 m. (c) Perpendicular lateral displacement d = t₁ sin(θ₀ − θ₁) / cos θ₁ = 0.0123 m.

markScheme.criterion: Finds θ₁ = 29.0° and applies Δy = t₁ tan θ₁.
Applies d = t₁ sin(θ₀ − θ₁) / cos θ₁ or (t₁ tan θ₀ − Δy) cos θ₀.

parts.prompt: State the emergent angle of refraction in dry air and calculate the optical Snell invariant n₀ sin θ₀.
workingSteps: Because both outer media have refractive index 1 and the faces are parallel, the emergent angle equals 50°.
Snell invariant = n₀ sin θ₀ = 1 × sin 50° = 0.766.

parts.prompt: Calculate the transverse offset Δy = t₁ tan θ₁ of the ray between the entry normal and exit normal along the slab face.
Hence calculate the perpendicular lateral displacement d between the emergent ray and the original incident ray line.
workingSteps: d = (t₁ tan θ₀ − Δy) cos θ₀ = t₁ sin(θ₀ − θ₁) / cos θ₁ = 0.0123 m.

items.stem: A 240 m multimode step-index optical fiber in a transoceanic telecommunications link has a core of refractive index n_core = 1.58 and cladding of refractive index n_clad = 1.49 in air (n_ext = 1.00, shown with a guided ray launched at 15.9°). Take the speed of light in vacuum to be c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) t_axial = n_core L / c = (1.58 × 240) / 3.00 × 10⁸ = 1.26 × 10⁻⁶ s. (b) Longest guided ray has path L / sin θ_c = L n_core / n_clad, giving t_max = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 1.34 × 10⁻⁶ s. (c) Modal pulse delay Δt = t_max − t_axial = 7.63 × 10⁻⁸ s.

markScheme.criterion: Uses t_axial = n_core L / c with n_core = 1.58 and L = 240 m.
Applies L_max = L (n_core / n_clad) to find t_max = t_axial (n_core / n_clad).

items.stem: In an ophthalmic lens-blank inspection jig, a collimated laser beam of vacuum wavelength 633 nm (speed of light in vacuum c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) travels in distilled water of refractive index n₁ = 1.33 and strikes a flat boundary with dense flint glass of refractive index n₂ = 1.65 at an angle of incidence of 26° to the normal.
items.workedSolution: (a) Inside dense flint glass, v₂ = c / n₂ = 1.82 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹ and λ₂ = λ₀ / n₂ = 633 / 1.65 = 384 nm. (b) By Snell's law, sin θ₂ = (1.33 sin 26°) / 1.65, giving θ₂ = 20.7°. (c) Angular deviation δ = |θ₂ − θ₁| = 5.31°.

markScheme.criterion: Obtains λ₂ = 384 nm (with v₂ = 1.82 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹).
Substitutes n₁ = 1.33, θ₁ = 26°, and n₂ = 1.65 into n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts θ_axis from 90° to obtain θ_w.

items.stem: An experimental arrangement of an acoustic transducer moving-coil suspension rig comprises a block of mass m = 0.36 kg attached to an ideal horizontal spring of stiffness k = 72 N m⁻¹. The block oscillates in simple harmonic motion with amplitude x₀ = 0.025 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes m = 0.36 kg and k = 72 N m⁻¹ into T = 2π√(m / k).
Applies Hooke's law F_max = k x₀ = 72 × 0.025.
Divides F_max by m (or multiplies ω² by x₀).

items.stem: In a Foucault-style brass sphere suspension apparatus, a pendulum bob of mass m = 0.25 kg suspended on a light cord of length L = 1.6 m oscillates in small-angle simple harmonic motion with arc amplitude x₀ = 0.32 m. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) T = 2π√(1.6 / 9.81) = 2.54 s. (b) v_max = √(9.81 / 1.6) × 0.32 = 0.792 m s⁻¹. (c) Lowest-point cord tension = m(g + v_max² / L) = 2.55 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies v_max = ω x₀ = (2π / T) x₀.
Uses T_cord = mg + mv_max² / L at the bottom of the arc.

parts.prompt: Calculate the period T of the pendulum.
Calculate the maximum speed v_max of the bob as it passes through equilibrium.
Determine the tension in the suspension cord as the bob passes through its lowest point.

items.stem: In a quartz crystal tuning-fork tine, a mass m = 1.2 kg oscillates in undamped simple harmonic motion with angular frequency ω = 25 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude x₀ = 0.1 m. The parabolic energy–displacement curves are analyzed at displacement x = 0.05 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes m = 1.2 kg, ω = 25 rad s⁻¹, and x₀ = 0.1 m into E_tot = ½mω²x₀².
Applies E_k = ½mω²(x₀² − x²) or E_tot − ½mω²x².
Sets E_p = ½E_tot to obtain x = x₀ / √2.

parts.prompt: Calculate the total mechanical energy E_tot of the oscillating mass.
Calculate the kinetic energy E_k of the mass when its displacement is x = 0.05 m.
workingSteps: E_k = E_tot − E_p = ½mω²(x₀² − x²) = 2.81 J.

parts.prompt: Determine the positive displacement x from equilibrium at which kinetic energy equals potential energy.

items.stem: A beam-steering prism assembly on a clinical corneal pachymetry test phantom guides light (c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) inside optical diamond (n₁ = 2.42) toward a planar interface with fused-silica glass (n₂ = 1.46) at an incidence angle of 46° measured from the normal.
items.workedSolution: (a) sin θ_c = 1.46 / 2.42, so θ_c = 37.1°. (b) Because n₁ > n₂ and θ₁ > θ_c, total internal reflection occurs at the interface. (c) Wave speed v₁ = 3.00 × 10⁸ / 2.42 = 1.24 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, and angular deviation δ = 180° − 2(46°) = 88.0°.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1.46 / 2.42.
States total internal reflection because the ray is in the higher-index medium with incident angle greater than the critical angle.

parts.expectedAnswer: Total internal reflection occurs because light travels in the medium of higher refractive index and the incident angle exceeds the critical angle.

parts.prompt: Calculate the angular deviation of the reflected ray from the incident ray's original forward direction, and find the wave speed in the first medium.
workingSteps: Wave speed in optical diamond: v₁ = c / n₁ = 1.24 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Engineers characterizing a subterranean pipeline temperature-sensing cable couple a laser beam from water of refractive index 1.33 at 17.8° to the axis into a straight 60 m step-index waveguide (core index 1.6, cladding index 1.5).
items.workedSolution: (a) θ_c = arcsin(1.5 / 1.6) = 69.6°. (b) Using n_ext sin θ_max = √(n_core² − n_clad²) gives θ_max = 24.7°. (c) For θ_in = 17.8°, θ_axis = 14.7° and L_ray = 60 / cos θ_axis = 62.0 m.

markScheme.criterion: Applies 1.33 sin θ_max = n_core sin(90° − θ_c).
Finds θ_axis = 14.7° and evaluates L / cos θ_axis.

items.stem: In a forensic macro-photography stage, an upright object of height h_o = 0.008 m is held at a distance u = 0.0525 m in front of a thin converging magnifying lens of focal length f = 0.15 m. Use the real-is-positive sign convention (1/f = 1/u + 1/v, m = −v/u).

items.stem: In an earthquake shake-table Tuned spring sled, a load of mass m = 0.6 kg hangs at rest from a vertical spring of spring constant k = 25 N m⁻¹. It is then pulled vertically downward by x₀ = 0.024 m from equilibrium and released. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Δx_eq = mg / k = (0.6 × 9.81) / 25 = 0.235 m. (b) T = 2π√(0.6 / 25) = 0.973 s. (c) Maximum net SHM acceleration a_max = (k / m) x₀ = 1.00 m s⁻².

Evaluates a_max = ω² x₀ = (k / m) x₀.

items.workedSolution: (a) ω = 2π(12) = 75.4 rad s⁻¹. (b) At x = -0.03 m, a = −ω²x = 171 m s⁻². (c) Maximum acceleration magnitude a_max = ω² x₀ = 227 m s⁻².
