items.stem: Engineers testing a deep-ocean optical hydrophone window direct a narrow beam of vacuum wavelength 670 nm (c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) through optical crown glass (n₁ = 1.52) onto a smooth synthetic sapphire surface (n₂ = 1.77) at an incidence angle of 38° to the boundary normal.
items.workedSolution: (a) Inside synthetic sapphire, v₂ = c / n₂ = 1.69 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹ and λ₂ = λ₀ / n₂ = 670 / 1.77 = 379 nm. (b) By Snell's law, sin θ₂ = (1.52 sin 38°) / 1.77, giving θ₂ = 31.9°. (c) Angular deviation δ = |θ₂ − θ₁| = 6.08°.

items.stem: A 80 m step-index waveguide deployed in a wind-turbine blade strain-monitoring waveguide comprises a glass core (n_core = 1.55) surrounded by lower-index cladding (n_clad = 1.47). Monochromatic light enters from air (n_ext = 1.00) at an angle of 15° to the fiber axis.
items.workedSolution: (a) sin θ_c = 1.47 / 1.55 ⇒ θ_c = 71.5°. (b) By Snell's law at the end-face, sin θ_axis = (1 sin 15°) / 1.55, so θ_axis = 9.61°. (c) Wall incident angle θ_w = 90° − θ_axis = 80.4°, which exceeds θ_c so the ray is guided by TIR.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts θ_axis from 90° to obtain θ_w.

items.stem: A 2400 m multimode step-index optical fiber in an industrial laser-welding delivery cable has a core of refractive index n_core = 1.54 and cladding of refractive index n_clad = 1.45 in air (n_ext = 1.00, shown with a guided ray launched at 12.5°). Take the speed of light in vacuum to be c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) t_axial = n_core L / c = (1.54 × 2400) / 3.00 × 10⁸ = 1.23 × 10⁻⁵ s. (b) Longest guided ray has path L / sin θ_c = L n_core / n_clad, giving t_max = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 1.31 × 10⁻⁵ s. (c) Modal pulse delay Δt = t_max − t_axial = 7.65 × 10⁻⁷ s.

markScheme.criterion: Uses t_axial = n_core L / c with n_core = 1.54 and L = 2400 m.
Applies L_max = L (n_core / n_clad) to find t_max = t_axial (n_core / n_clad).

items.workedSolution: (a) Optical power P = 1 / (−0.15) = -6.67 D. (b) 1/v = −1/0.15 − 1/0.375 ⇒ v = -0.107 m. (c) Axial separation between object and virtual image on the same side = u − |v| = 0.268 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes f = −0.15 m and u = 0.375 m into 1/v = 1/f − 1/u.

items.stem: A beam-steering prism assembly on an undergraduate ray-box bench guides light (c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) inside polycarbonate polymer (n₁ = 1.58) toward a planar interface with liquid ethanol (n₂ = 1.36) at an incidence angle of 72° measured from the normal.
items.workedSolution: (a) sin θ_c = 1.36 / 1.58, so θ_c = 59.4°. (b) Because n₁ > n₂ and θ₁ > θ_c, total internal reflection occurs at the interface. (c) Wave speed v₁ = 3.00 × 10⁸ / 1.58 = 1.90 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, and angular deviation δ = 180° − 2(72°) = 36.0°.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1.36 / 1.58.
States total internal reflection because the ray is in the higher-index medium with incident angle greater than the critical angle.

Finds θ_axis = 11.8° and evaluates L / cos θ_axis.

Divides F_max by m (or multiplies ω² by x₀).

items.stem: A simple pendulum rig in a lecture-hall rigid-ceiling wire pendulum carries a 0.8 kg sphere on a 1.05 m wire, swinging with small-angle arc amplitude 0.2625 m where g = 9.81 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Applies v_max = ω x₀ = (2π / T) x₀.
Uses T_cord = mg + mv_max² / L at the bottom of the arc.

parts.prompt: Calculate the period T of the pendulum.
Calculate the maximum speed v_max of the bob as it passes through equilibrium.

items.stem: A 1.2 kg harmonic oscillator in a piezoelectric laser-mirror dithering stage vibrates with angular frequency 20 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude 0.06 m. Consider its mechanical energy distribution when passing through displacement x = 0.048 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes m = 1.2 kg, ω = 20 rad s⁻¹, and x₀ = 0.06 m into E_tot = ½mω²x₀².
Applies E_k = ½mω²(x₀² − x²) or E_tot − ½mω²x².
Sets E_p = ½E_tot to obtain x = x₀ / √2.

parts.prompt: Calculate the total mechanical energy E_tot of the oscillating mass.
Calculate the kinetic energy E_k of the mass when its displacement is x = 0.048 m.
workingSteps: E_k = E_tot − E_p = ½mω²(x₀² − x²) = 0.311 J.

parts.prompt: Determine the positive displacement x from equilibrium at which kinetic energy equals potential energy.

items.stem: In a subsea ROV camera viewport test, a narrow monochromatic beam in dry air (refractive index n₀ = 1) strikes a parallel-sided block of dense flint glass (refractive index n₁ = 1.65, thickness 0.085 m) at an angle of incidence of 32° to the normal and emerges back into dry air on the far side.
items.workedSolution: (a) Snells invariant n₀ sin θ₀ = 1 sin 32° = 0.530 (emergent angle = 32°). (b) Inside the slab, θ₁ = arcsin(0.5299 / 1.65) = 18.7°, so Δy = 0.085 tan θ₁ = 0.0288 m. (c) Perpendicular lateral displacement d = t₁ sin(θ₀ − θ₁) / cos θ₁ = 0.0206 m.

markScheme.criterion: Finds θ₁ = 18.7° and applies Δy = t₁ tan θ₁.
Applies d = t₁ sin(θ₀ − θ₁) / cos θ₁ or (t₁ tan θ₀ − Δy) cos θ₀.

parts.prompt: State the emergent angle of refraction in dry air and calculate the optical Snell invariant n₀ sin θ₀.
workingSteps: Because both outer media have refractive index 1 and the faces are parallel, the emergent angle equals 32°.
Snell invariant = n₀ sin θ₀ = 1 × sin 32° = 0.530.

parts.prompt: Calculate the transverse offset Δy = t₁ tan θ₁ of the ray between the entry normal and exit normal along the slab face.
Hence calculate the perpendicular lateral displacement d between the emergent ray and the original incident ray line.
workingSteps: d = (t₁ tan θ₀ − Δy) cos θ₀ = t₁ sin(θ₀ − θ₁) / cos θ₁ = 0.0206 m.

items.stem: During pulse-broadening tests for a borehole geophysical telemetry line, engineers transmit narrow laser pulses from air (n_ext = 1.00, sample launch angle 14.9°) along a 360 m step-index fiber of core index 1.5 and cladding index 1.44. Take c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) t_axial = n_core L / c = (1.5 × 360) / 3.00 × 10⁸ = 1.80 × 10⁻⁶ s. (b) Longest guided ray has path L / sin θ_c = L n_core / n_clad, giving t_max = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 1.88 × 10⁻⁶ s. (c) Modal pulse delay Δt = t_max − t_axial = 7.50 × 10⁻⁸ s.

markScheme.criterion: Uses t_axial = n_core L / c with n_core = 1.5 and L = 360 m.
Applies L_max = L (n_core / n_clad) to find t_max = t_axial (n_core / n_clad).

items.stem: A vertical suspension stage in a precision marine-chronometer balance-mass rig supports a 0.5 kg mass on an ideal coil spring of stiffness 100 N m⁻¹, oscillating vertically with amplitude 0.018 m about its equilibrium position (take g = 9.8 m s⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) Δx_eq = mg / k = (0.5 × 9.8) / 100 = 0.0490 m. (b) T = 2π√(0.5 / 100) = 0.444 s. (c) Maximum net SHM acceleration a_max = (k / m) x₀ = 3.60 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Uses mg = k Δx_eq with g = 9.8 m s⁻².
Evaluates a_max = ω² x₀ = (k / m) x₀.

items.workedSolution: (a) Inside crystalline zircon, v₂ = c / n₂ = 1.56 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹ and λ₂ = λ₀ / n₂ = 450 / 1.92 = 234 nm. (b) By Snell's law, sin θ₂ = (1.52 sin 52°) / 1.92, giving θ₂ = 38.6°. (c) Angular deviation δ = |θ₂ − θ₁| = 13.4°.

items.stem: In a spacecraft thruster-valve return-spring test fixture, a load of mass m = 0.4 kg hangs at rest from a vertical spring of spring constant k = 64 N m⁻¹. It is then pulled vertically downward by x₀ = 0.018 m from equilibrium and released. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Δx_eq = mg / k = (0.4 × 9.8) / 64 = 0.0613 m. (b) T = 2π√(0.4 / 64) = 0.497 s. (c) Maximum net SHM acceleration a_max = (k / m) x₀ = 2.88 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Uses mg = k Δx_eq with g = 9.8 m s⁻².
Evaluates a_max = ω² x₀ = (k / m) x₀.

parts.prompt: Calculate the static extension Δx_eq of the spring when the mass hangs at rest in equilibrium.
Calculate the period T of the vertical simple harmonic oscillations.
Determine the magnitude of the maximum net acceleration a_max of the mass during the oscillation.

items.stem: In a violins bridge laser-Doppler vibration target, a component oscillates in simple harmonic motion at frequency f = 2.5 Hz with amplitude x₀ = 0.1 m. Its instantaneous state is examined when the displacement from equilibrium is x = 0.035 m.
items.workedSolution: (a) ω = 2π(2.5) = 15.7 rad s⁻¹. (b) At x = 0.035 m, a = −ω²x = -8.64 m s⁻². (c) Maximum acceleration magnitude a_max = ω² x₀ = 24.7 m s⁻².

items.stem: In a precision optical-chopper resonant blade, a mass m = 0.25 kg oscillates in undamped simple harmonic motion with angular frequency ω = 15 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude x₀ = 0.04 m. The parabolic energy–displacement curves are analyzed at displacement x = 0.016 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes m = 0.25 kg, ω = 15 rad s⁻¹, and x₀ = 0.04 m into E_tot = ½mω²x₀².
Applies E_k = ½mω²(x₀² − x²) or E_tot − ½mω²x².
Sets E_p = ½E_tot to obtain x = x₀ / √2.

parts.prompt: Calculate the total mechanical energy E_tot of the oscillating mass.
Calculate the kinetic energy E_k of the mass when its displacement is x = 0.016 m.
workingSteps: E_k = E_tot − E_p = ½mω²(x₀² − x²) = 0.0378 J.

parts.prompt: Determine the positive displacement x from equilibrium at which kinetic energy equals potential energy.

items.stem: A precision optical compensator in a gemstone goniometer calibration rig uses a flat, parallel-sided synthetic sapphire plate of thickness 0.06 m and refractive index 1.77 surrounded by dry air (n₀ = 1). An incident ray meets the entry face at 62° to the normal.
items.workedSolution: (a) Snells invariant n₀ sin θ₀ = 1 sin 62° = 0.883 (emergent angle = 62°). (b) Inside the slab, θ₁ = arcsin(0.8829 / 1.77) = 29.9°, so Δy = 0.06 tan θ₁ = 0.0345 m. (c) Perpendicular lateral displacement d = t₁ sin(θ₀ − θ₁) / cos θ₁ = 0.0368 m.

markScheme.criterion: Finds θ₁ = 29.9° and applies Δy = t₁ tan θ₁.
Applies d = t₁ sin(θ₀ − θ₁) / cos θ₁ or (t₁ tan θ₀ − Δy) cos θ₀.

parts.prompt: State the emergent angle of refraction in dry air and calculate the optical Snell invariant n₀ sin θ₀.
workingSteps: Because both outer media have refractive index 1 and the faces are parallel, the emergent angle equals 62°.
Snell invariant = n₀ sin θ₀ = 1 × sin 62° = 0.883.

parts.prompt: Calculate the transverse offset Δy = t₁ tan θ₁ of the ray between the entry normal and exit normal along the slab face.
Hence calculate the perpendicular lateral displacement d between the emergent ray and the original incident ray line.
workingSteps: d = (t₁ tan θ₀ − Δy) cos θ₀ = t₁ sin(θ₀ − θ₁) / cos θ₁ = 0.0368 m.

items.stem: A 360 m multimode step-index optical fiber in an astronomical echelle-spectrograph feed has a core of refractive index n_core = 1.48 and cladding of refractive index n_clad = 1.41 in air (n_ext = 1.00, shown with a guided ray launched at 13.4°). Take the speed of light in vacuum to be c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) t_axial = n_core L / c = (1.48 × 360) / 3.00 × 10⁸ = 1.78 × 10⁻⁶ s. (b) Longest guided ray has path L / sin θ_c = L n_core / n_clad, giving t_max = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 1.86 × 10⁻⁶ s. (c) Modal pulse delay Δt = t_max − t_axial = 8.82 × 10⁻⁸ s.

markScheme.criterion: Uses t_axial = n_core L / c with n_core = 1.48 and L = 360 m.
Applies L_max = L (n_core / n_clad) to find t_max = t_axial (n_core / n_clad).

items.stem: A beam-steering prism assembly on a microfluidic refractive-index sensor guides light (c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) inside crystalline zircon (n₁ = 1.92) toward a planar interface with dry air (n₂ = 1) at an incidence angle of 44° measured from the normal.
items.workedSolution: (a) sin θ_c = 1 / 1.92, so θ_c = 31.4°. (b) Because n₁ > n₂ and θ₁ > θ_c, total internal reflection occurs at the interface. (c) Wave speed v₁ = 3.00 × 10⁸ / 1.92 = 1.56 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, and angular deviation δ = 180° − 2(44°) = 92.0°.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1 / 1.92.
States total internal reflection because the ray is in the higher-index medium with incident angle greater than the critical angle.

parts.expectedAnswer: Total internal reflection occurs because light travels in the medium of higher refractive index and the incident angle exceeds the critical angle.

parts.prompt: Calculate the angular deviation of the reflected ray from the incident ray's original forward direction, and find the wave speed in the first medium.
workingSteps: Wave speed in crystalline zircon: v₁ = c / n₁ = 1.56 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹.
Angular deviation under total internal reflection: δ = 180° − 2(44°) = 92.0°.

items.stem: In a flexible medical gastroscope bundle, a straight 120 m step-index optical fiber has a core of refractive index n_core = 1.5 and a cladding of refractive index n_clad = 1.44. A narrow laser beam in air (n_ext = 1.00) strikes the flat entry face at θ_in = 14.7° to the central axis.
items.workedSolution: (a) sin θ_c = 1.44 / 1.5 ⇒ θ_c = 73.7°. (b) By Snell's law at the end-face, sin θ_axis = (1 sin 14.7°) / 1.5, so θ_axis = 9.74°. (c) Wall incident angle θ_w = 90° − θ_axis = 80.3°, which exceeds θ_c so the ray is guided by TIR.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts θ_axis from 90° to obtain θ_w.

items.stem: In a coastal lighthouse clockwork escapement pendulum, a pendulum bob of mass m = 0.25 kg suspended on a light cord of length L = 1.9 m oscillates in small-angle simple harmonic motion with arc amplitude x₀ = 0.418 m. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) T = 2π√(1.9 / 9.81) = 2.77 s. (b) v_max = √(9.81 / 1.9) × 0.418 = 0.950 m s⁻¹. (c) Lowest-point cord tension = m(g + v_max² / L) = 2.57 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies v_max = ω x₀ = (2π / T) x₀.

items.stem: In a marine wave-tank oscillating piston paddle, a mass m = 0.6 kg oscillates in undamped simple harmonic motion with angular frequency ω = 12 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude x₀ = 0.04 m. The parabolic energy–displacement curves are analyzed at displacement x = 0.032 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes m = 0.6 kg, ω = 12 rad s⁻¹, and x₀ = 0.04 m into E_tot = ½mω²x₀².
Applies E_k = ½mω²(x₀² − x²) or E_tot − ½mω²x².
Sets E_p = ½E_tot to obtain x = x₀ / √2.

parts.prompt: Calculate the total mechanical energy E_tot of the oscillating mass.
Calculate the kinetic energy E_k of the mass when its displacement is x = 0.032 m.
workingSteps: E_k = E_tot − E_p = ½mω²(x₀² − x²) = 0.0249 J.

parts.prompt: Determine the positive displacement x from equilibrium at which kinetic energy equals potential energy.

items.stem: A precision optical compensator in an interferometric metrology window uses a flat, parallel-sided crystalline zircon plate of thickness 0.06 m and refractive index 1.92 surrounded by distilled water (n₀ = 1.33). An incident ray meets the entry face at 32° to the normal.
items.workedSolution: (a) Snells invariant n₀ sin θ₀ = 1.33 sin 32° = 0.705 (emergent angle = 32°). (b) Inside the slab, θ₁ = arcsin(0.7048 / 1.92) = 21.5°, so Δy = 0.06 tan θ₁ = 0.0237 m. (c) Perpendicular lateral displacement d = t₁ sin(θ₀ − θ₁) / cos θ₁ = 0.0117 m.

markScheme.criterion: Finds θ₁ = 21.5° and applies Δy = t₁ tan θ₁.
Applies d = t₁ sin(θ₀ − θ₁) / cos θ₁ or (t₁ tan θ₀ − Δy) cos θ₀.

parts.prompt: State the emergent angle of refraction in distilled water and calculate the optical Snell invariant n₀ sin θ₀.
workingSteps: Because both outer media have refractive index 1.33 and the faces are parallel, the emergent angle equals 32°.
Snell invariant = n₀ sin θ₀ = 1.33 × sin 32° = 0.705.

parts.prompt: Calculate the transverse offset Δy = t₁ tan θ₁ of the ray between the entry normal and exit normal along the slab face.
Hence calculate the perpendicular lateral displacement d between the emergent ray and the original incident ray line.
workingSteps: d = (t₁ tan θ₀ − Δy) cos θ₀ = t₁ sin(θ₀ − θ₁) / cos θ₁ = 0.0117 m.

items.stem: Engineers characterizing a tethered deep-sea ROV umbilical waveguide couple a laser beam from air of refractive index 1.00 at 21.2° to the axis into a straight 150 m step-index waveguide (core index 1.55, cladding index 1.47).
items.workedSolution: (a) θ_c = arcsin(1.47 / 1.55) = 71.5°. (b) Using n_ext sin θ_max = √(n_core² − n_clad²) gives θ_max = 29.4°. (c) For θ_in = 21.2°, θ_axis = 13.5° and L_ray = 150 / cos θ_axis = 154 m.

markScheme.criterion: Applies 1 sin θ_max = n_core sin(90° − θ_c).
Finds θ_axis = 13.5° and evaluates L / cos θ_axis.

items.stem: A vertical suspension stage in a university mechanics oscillation sled supports a 0.75 kg mass on an ideal coil spring of stiffness 80 N m⁻¹, oscillating vertically with amplitude 0.055 m about its equilibrium position (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) Δx_eq = mg / k = (0.75 × 9.81) / 80 = 0.0920 m. (b) T = 2π√(0.75 / 80) = 0.608 s. (c) Maximum net SHM acceleration a_max = (k / m) x₀ = 5.87 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Uses mg = k Δx_eq with g = 9.81 m s⁻².
Evaluates a_max = ω² x₀ = (k / m) x₀.

items.stem: In an atomic-force microscope cantilever tip, a component oscillates in simple harmonic motion at frequency f = 3 Hz with amplitude x₀ = 0.1 m. Its instantaneous state is examined when the displacement from equilibrium is x = 0.06 m.
items.workedSolution: (a) ω = 2π(3) = 18.8 rad s⁻¹. (b) At x = 0.06 m, a = −ω²x = -21.3 m s⁻². (c) Maximum acceleration magnitude a_max = ω² x₀ = 35.5 m s⁻².

items.stem: In an immersion-microscopy optical stage, a collimated laser beam of vacuum wavelength 650 nm (speed of light in vacuum c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) travels in dense flint glass of refractive index n₁ = 1.65 and strikes a flat boundary with fused-silica glass of refractive index n₂ = 1.46 at an angle of incidence of 48° to the normal.
items.workedSolution: (a) Inside fused-silica glass, v₂ = c / n₂ = 2.05 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹ and λ₂ = λ₀ / n₂ = 650 / 1.46 = 445 nm. (b) By Snell's law, sin θ₂ = (1.65 sin 48°) / 1.46, giving θ₂ = 57.1°. (c) Angular deviation δ = |θ₂ − θ₁| = 9.12°.

markScheme.criterion: Obtains λ₂ = 445 nm (with v₂ = 2.05 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹).
Substitutes n₁ = 1.65, θ₁ = 48°, and n₂ = 1.46 into n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂.

A narrow laser beam in air (n_ext = 1.00) strikes the flat entry face at θ_in = 8.8° to the central axis.

items.stem: In an underwater dome-port virtual-image corrector, an upright object of height h_o = 0.02 m is placed at a distance u = 0.24 m in front of a thin diverging lens whose focal length is f = −0.4 m under the real-is-positive sign convention.
items.workedSolution: (a) Optical power P = 1 / (−0.4) = -2.50 D. (b) 1/v = −1/0.4 − 1/0.24 ⇒ v = -0.150 m. (c) Axial separation between object and virtual image on the same side = u − |v| = 0.0900 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes f = −0.4 m and u = 0.24 m into 1/v = 1/f − 1/u.
Subtracts |v| from u because virtual image and object are on the same side of the lens.

items.stem: A simple pendulum in a metrology gravimetry pendulum stand consists of a 0.25 kg sphere on a 0.62 m wire oscillating in small-angle simple harmonic motion with arc amplitude 0.0744 m (take g = 9.8 m s⁻²).

parts.prompt: Calculate the period T of the small-angle oscillations.
Calculate the angular frequency ω of the pendulum.
Determine the maximum magnitude of the bob's restoring acceleration a_max.

items.stem: In a precision optical-chopper resonant blade, a resonant element executes simple harmonic motion with angular frequency ω = 40 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude x₀ = 0.1 m, as depicted by its velocity–displacement phase ellipse. Measurements are taken when the displacement is x = 0.05 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses T = 2π / ω with ω = 40 rad s⁻¹.
Substitutes x₀ = 0.1 m and x = 0.05 m into v = ω√(x₀² − x²).

items.stem: During alignment of a transoceanic telecommunications link, monochromatic light from air (n_ext = 1.00) strikes the entry face of a 350 m step-index fiber (n_core = 1.52, n_clad = 1.46) at 8.8° to the central optic axis. Determine the angle of incidence θ_w at the cylindrical core–cladding boundary relative to its normal.
items.workedSolution: At the entry face, 1 sin 8.8° = 1.52 sin θ_axis ⇒ θ_axis = 5.78°. Since the core wall is parallel to the axis, its normal is perpendicular to the axis, giving θ_w = 90° − θ_axis = 84.2°.

items.stem: Engineers evaluating bit-rate limits for an astronomical echelle-spectrograph feed test a 900 m step-index waveguide (n_core = 1.62, n_clad = 1.51, n_ext = 1.00, ray shown at 14.4°). Take c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹. Determine the multipath dispersion delay Δt between extreme guided rays and axial rays.
items.workedSolution: Axial transit time t_min = n_core L / c = (1.62 × 900) / (3.00 × 10⁸) = 4.86 × 10⁻⁶ s. At the critical angle sin θ_c = n_clad / n_core, t_max = t_min / sin θ_c = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 5.21 × 10⁻⁶ s. Modal delay Δt = t_max − t_min = 3.54 × 10⁻⁷ s.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δt = (n_core L / c)(n_core / n_clad − 1) = 3.54 × 10⁻⁷ s (C).

items.stem: During optical testing on a myopia-corrective ophthalmic spectacle trial, a 0.036 m illuminated target sits 0.08 m from a thin diverging lens of focal length −0.1 m. Determine the signed image position v under the real-is-positive sign convention.
items.workedSolution: For a diverging lens, f = −0.1 m. Using 1/f = 1/u + 1/v gives 1/v = −1/0.1 − 1/0.08 = -22.50 m⁻¹, so v = -0.0444 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses negative f = −0.1 m in 1/v = 1/f − 1/u to obtain v = -0.0444 m (B).

options.distractorRationale: Computes the correct magnitude |v| but omits the negative sign required for a virtual image in the real-is-positive convention.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Forgets that a diverging lens has negative focal length f < 0, substituting +|f| into 1/v = 1/f − 1/u.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Stops at 1/v = −1/|f| − 1/u in m⁻¹ without taking the reciprocal to find v in metres.

items.stem: A vertical helical spring of stiffness 20 N m⁻¹ in an inertial seismometer calibration trolley suspends a load of mass 0.75 kg that subsequently oscillates vertically with amplitude 0.018 m. Taking g = 9.8 m s⁻², what was the static extension Δx_eq of the spring at equilibrium before oscillation started?
items.workedSolution: At static equilibrium, upward spring tension balances weight: k Δx_eq = mg ⇒ Δx_eq = (0.75 × 9.8) / 20 = 0.368 m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Hooke's law as k / (mg) instead of mg / k.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Adds the oscillation amplitude x₀ to mg / k, finding maximum total stretch rather than static equilibrium extension.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides mass m directly by spring constant k without multiplying by gravitational field strength g.

items.stem: In an ultrasonic surgical transducer tip, a component executes simple harmonic motion at frequency f = 4 Hz with amplitude x₀ = 0.08 m, as represented on the acceleration–displacement graph. Taking displacement to the right as positive, what is its signed acceleration a when x = 0.028 m?
items.workedSolution: Angular frequency ω = 2πf = 2π(4) = 25.13 rad s⁻¹. By the defining SHM equation, a = −ω²x = −(25.13)²(0.028) = -17.7 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ω = 2πf and obtains -17.7 m s⁻² (B).

items.stem: Engineers monitoring a piezoelectric laser-mirror dithering stage measure simple harmonic motion of amplitude 0.12 m and angular frequency 12 rad s⁻¹. Determine the speed |v| = ω√(x₀² − x²) at displacement x = 0.0432 m.
items.workedSolution: Using v = ω√(x₀² − x²) gives v = 12 × √(0.12² − 0.0432²) = 1.34 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into v = ω√(x₀² − x²) to obtain 1.34 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: A collimated ray inside optical diamond (n₁ = 2.42, vacuum light speed c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) strikes a flat interface with fused-silica glass (n₂ = 1.46) at 50° to the normal during a microfluidic refractive-index sensor. Through what angle is the ray deviated from its original forward path at this boundary?
items.workedSolution: Since sin θ_c = 1.46 / 2.42 gives θ_c = 37.1° and θ₁ = 50° > θ_c, the beam undergoes total internal reflection with θ_r = 50°. The angular deviation from the original forward direction is δ = 180° − 2(50°) = 80.0°.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies TIR (θ₁ > θ_c = 37.1°) and computes δ = 180° − 2θ₁ = 80.0° (B).

items.stem: A test rig using a silicon MEMS accelerometer proof-mass flexure test model has mass 0.8 kg, horizontal spring constant 14 N m⁻¹, and oscillation amplitude 0.025 m. What is the natural frequency f of the oscillation?
items.workedSolution: Natural frequency f = (1 / 2π)√(k / m) = (1 / 2π)√(14 / 0.8) = 0.666 Hz.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Reports angular frequency ω = √(k / m) in rad s⁻¹ without dividing by 2π.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes the period T = 2π√(m / k) instead of frequency f = 1 / T.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Swaps k/m and m/k, computing (1 / 2π)√(m / k) instead of (1 / 2π)√(k / m).

items.stem: In a robotics compliant-actuator test carriage, a 0.3 kg mass hangs from a vertical spring of constant 100 N m⁻¹ and executes vertical SHM of amplitude 0.018 m (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Calculate the static equilibrium extension Δx_eq from the spring's unstretched length.
items.workedSolution: At static equilibrium, upward spring tension balances weight: k Δx_eq = mg ⇒ Δx_eq = (0.3 × 9.81) / 100 = 0.0294 m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Hooke's law as k / (mg) instead of mg / k.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Adds the oscillation amplitude x₀ to mg / k, finding maximum total stretch rather than static equilibrium extension.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides mass m directly by spring constant k without multiplying by gravitational field strength g.

items.stem: A 0.8 kg pendulum bob suspended from a 1.9 m wire in an evacuated bell-jar precision timing pendulum oscillates in SHM with arc amplitude 0.532 m (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). What is the maximum speed v_max of the bob?
items.workedSolution: Angular frequency ω = √(g / L) = √(9.81 / 1.9), so maximum speed v_max = ω x₀ = 1.21 m s⁻¹.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Treats the horizontal arc amplitude x₀ as a vertical free-fall drop height h in √(2gh).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes ω² x₀ = (g / L) x₀ (maximum acceleration) instead of ω x₀ = √(g / L) x₀.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts g / L inside √(g / L) when computing ω x₀.

items.stem: The velocity–displacement phase portrait shown represents a vibrometer calibration shaker table oscillating with ω = 40 rad s⁻¹ and x₀ = 0.15 m. Find the oscillator's speed at x = 0.054 m.
items.workedSolution: Using v = ω√(x₀² − x²) gives v = 40 × √(0.15² − 0.054²) = 5.60 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into v = ω√(x₀² − x²) to obtain 5.60 m s⁻¹ (B).

options.distractorRationale: Calculates the maximum speed ωx₀ at equilibrium (x = 0) instead of the speed at x.

options.label: C

items.stem: In a marine wave-tank oscillating piston paddle, a 0.25 kg oscillator moves harmonically at ω = 18 rad s⁻¹ with amplitude x₀ = 0.04 m (sampled at 0.02 m). At what positive displacement x from equilibrium is its kinetic energy equal to its potential energy (E_k = E_p)?
items.workedSolution: Setting E_p = ½E_tot gives ½mω²x² = ½(½mω²x₀²), so x² = x₀² / 2 and x = x₀ / √2 = 0.04 / √2 = 0.0283 m.

markScheme.criterion: Solves x² = x₀² / 2 to obtain x = x₀ / √2 = 0.0283 m (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Squares the ½ factor to obtain x₀ / 4 instead of taking the square root x₀ / √2.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes (√3 / 2)x₀ (where E_p = ¾E_tot) instead of x₀ / √2.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Assumes E_k = E_p occurs at half the amplitude (x₀ / 2, where E_p = ¼E_tot) instead of x₀ / √2.

items.stem: A refractometer cell in a photovoltaic encapsulant test coupon immerses a polished dielectric slab in fused-silica glass (n₂ = 1.46), recording a critical angle of 49.5° relative to the boundary normal. Determine the refractive index n₁ of the dielectric slab.
items.workedSolution: At the critical angle, n₁ sin θ_c = n₂ sin 90° = n₂, so n₁ = 1.46 / sin 49.5° = 1.92.

markScheme.criterion: Computes n₁ = n₂ / sin θ_c = 1.46 / sin 49.5° = 1.92 (B).

items.stem: In a tethered deep-sea ROV umbilical waveguide, a guided ray from water of refractive index 1.33 enters a straight 450 m step-index fiber (n_core = 1.58, n_clad = 1.49) at launch angle θ_in = 14.7° to the axis. Neglecting end losses, what total geometric path length does this zig-zagging ray travel through the core?
items.workedSolution: Inside the core, sin θ_axis = (1.33 sin 14.7°) / 1.58 ⇒ θ_axis = 12.3°. The total zig-zag geometric path length is L_ray = L / cos θ_axis = 450 / cos 12.33° = 461 m.

markScheme.criterion: Finds θ_axis = 12.3° and computes L / cos θ_axis = 461 m (B).

items.stem: A 900 m multimode step-index cable in a railway trackside acoustic-sensing fiber has core index 1.54 and cladding index 1.45 in air (n_ext = 1.00, sample launch angle 18.7°, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹). Calculate the maximum guided transit time through the fiber.
items.workedSolution: Wave speed in the core is v = c / n_core, and the critical-angle ray travels path length L / sin θ_c = L (n_core / n_clad). Therefore t_max = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 4.91 × 10⁻⁶ s.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates t_max = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 4.91 × 10⁻⁶ s (A).

items.stem: An observer using a metrology profile-projector optical train adjusts the position of a 0.015 m scale mark in front of a thin convex lens of focal length 0.24 m until its virtual image lies at the near point 0.360 m on the object side of the lens (v = −0.360 m). Calculate the object distance u.
items.workedSolution: For a virtual image in the real-is-positive convention, v = -0.360 m. Thus 1/u = 1/f − 1/v = 1/0.24 − (1/-0.3600) = 6.944 m⁻¹, giving u = 0.144 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes negative v = -0.360 m into 1/u = 1/f − 1/v to obtain u = 0.144 m (A).

items.stem: In a wide-angle security peephole assembly, an object of height 0.045 m is positioned 0.168 m from a concave lens of focal length −0.12 m. Calculate the signed linear magnification m = h_i / h_o = −v / u.
items.workedSolution: With f = −0.12 m, 1/v = −1/0.12 − 1/0.168 gives v = -0.0700 m. Therefore m = −v / u = −(-0.07000) / 0.168 = 0.417 (upright and diminished).

markScheme.criterion: Finds v = -0.0700 m and m = −v / u = 0.417 (A).

items.stem: Engineers testing a university mechanics oscillation sled hang a 0.9 kg mass from a vertical coil spring (k = 32 N m⁻¹) and excite vertical oscillations of amplitude 0.032 m in a gravitational field g = 9.8 m s⁻². Determine the period T of oscillation.
items.workedSolution: Gravity shifts the equilibrium position without altering effective stiffness k, so T = 2π√(m / k) = 2π√(0.9 / 32) = 1.05 s.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Swaps m/k and k/m inside the square root.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Incorrectly adds weight mg to spring stiffness k, assuming gravity changes the vertical mass-spring period.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes the oscillation amplitude x₀ into a pendulum-style formula 2π√(x₀ / g) instead of 2π√(m / k).

items.stem: During calibration of an atomic-force microscope cantilever tip vibrating at f = 1.5 Hz and amplitude 0.04 m, a laser sensor records an instantaneous displacement x = -0.03 m. Determine the signed SHM acceleration a at that instant.
items.workedSolution: Angular frequency ω = 2πf = 2π(1.5) = 9.425 rad s⁻¹. By the defining SHM equation, a = −ω²x = −(9.425)²(-0.03) = 2.66 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ω = 2πf and obtains 2.66 m s⁻² (A).

items.stem: In a dynamic mechanical thermal-analyzer probe, a 0.15 kg mass undergoes SHM with ω = 18 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude 0.04 m (with a sensor at x = 0.024 m). Calculate the frequency f_E at which the kinetic energy completes full cycles.
items.workedSolution: Mechanical frequency f = ω / (2π) = 18 / (2π) = 2.865 Hz. Because kinetic energy reaches a maximum twice per mechanical period, f_E = 2f = ω / π = 5.73 Hz.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Halves the mechanical frequency instead of doubling it.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Gives the mechanical displacement frequency f = ω / (2π) instead of recognizing that E_k ∝ cos²(ωt) oscillates at 2f.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates 2ω in rad s⁻¹ without dividing by 2π to convert to hertz.

items.stem: In an industrial laser-welding delivery cable, a straight step-index fiber of length 200 m has core index n_core = 1.58 and cladding index n_clad = 1.49. A test ray enters the flat end-face from air (n_ext = 1.00) at a steep angle θ_in = 45.7° to the fiber axis, exceeding the acceptance cone so light refracts into the cladding. What is the angle of refraction in the cladding measured from the core–cladding wall normal?
items.workedSolution: At entry, sin θ_axis = (1 sin 45.7°) / 1.58 ⇒ θ_axis = 26.9°. The angle to the wall normal is θ_w = 90° − θ_axis = 63.1° (< θ_c = 70.6°). Refracting into the cladding: sin θ_clad = (1.58 sin θ_w) / 1.49, giving θ_clad = 71.0°.

markScheme.criterion: Finds θ_w = 63.1° and refracts into cladding to obtain 71.0° (A).

items.stem: A multimode step-index fiber of length 150 m in a cryogenic laboratory optical feedthrough has n_core = 1.57 and n_clad = 1.46 in air (n_ext = 1.00, illustrated with a 24.7° launch ray). Taking c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹ and neglecting material dispersion, what is the maximum multipath (modal) pulse broadening Δt between the fastest axial ray and the slowest guided ray?
items.workedSolution: Axial transit time t_min = n_core L / c = (1.57 × 150) / (3.00 × 10⁸) = 7.85 × 10⁻⁷ s. At the critical angle sin θ_c = n_clad / n_core, t_max = t_min / sin θ_c = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 8.44 × 10⁻⁷ s. Modal delay Δt = t_max − t_min = 5.91 × 10⁻⁸ s.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δt = (n_core L / c)(n_core / n_clad − 1) = 5.91 × 10⁻⁸ s (A).

items.stem: In an optical-bench virtual-image calibration rig, an upright test object of height 0.02 m stands 0.18 m in front of a thin diverging lens of focal length magnitude 0.1 m (f = −0.1 m in the real-is-positive convention). What is the signed image distance v?
items.workedSolution: For a diverging lens, f = −0.1 m. Using 1/f = 1/u + 1/v gives 1/v = −1/0.1 − 1/0.18 = -15.56 m⁻¹, so v = -0.0643 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses negative f = −0.1 m in 1/v = 1/f − 1/u to obtain v = -0.0643 m (B).

items.stem: An experimental setup consisting of a structural vibration-isolation test sled on linear bearings has oscillating mass 1.2 kg, spring stiffness 56 N m⁻¹, and horizontal amplitude 0.035 m. Calculate the oscillation period T.
items.workedSolution: For an ideal mass-spring oscillator, T = 2π√(m / k) = 2π√(1.2 / 56) = 0.920 s.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Swaps m/k and k/m inside the radical, computing 2π√(k / m) instead of 2π√(m / k).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 2π and calculates √(m / k) = 1 / ω.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the square root and evaluates 2π(m / k).

items.stem: A 0.15 kg brass bob on a 0.85 m suspension wire in a museum horology restoration pendulum rig oscillates with arc-length amplitude 0.238 m (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Calculate the maximum cord tension at the bottom of the swing.
items.workedSolution: With ω = √(g / L) = √(9.81 / 0.85), peak speed v_max = ω x₀ = 0.809 m s⁻¹. At the lowest point, T_cord = m(g + v_max² / L) = 1.59 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_max = ω x₀ and T_cord = mg + mv_max² / L = 1.59 N (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Equates cord tension at the lowest point to static weight mg, ignoring the upward centripetal force mv_max² / L.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts the centripetal force mv_max² / L from mg instead of adding it at the bottom of the arc.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates only the net radial centripetal force mv_max² / L rather than the total cord tension.

items.stem: Engineers monitoring a precision optical-chopper resonant blade measure simple harmonic motion of amplitude 0.08 m and angular frequency 20 rad s⁻¹. Determine the speed |v| = ω√(x₀² − x²) at displacement x = 0.064 m.
items.workedSolution: Using v = ω√(x₀² − x²) gives v = 20 × √(0.08² − 0.064²) = 0.960 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into v = ω√(x₀² − x²) to obtain 0.960 m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: A 0.5 kg harmonic proof mass in a magnetic-levitation harmonic test puck vibrates at ω = 25 rad s⁻¹ with amplitude 0.06 m. Determine its kinetic energy at the instant x = 0.036 m.
items.workedSolution: Using E_k = ½mω²(x₀² − x²) gives E_k = 0.5 × 0.5 × 25² × (0.06² − 0.036²) = 0.360 J.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the potential energy ½mω²x² at x rather than the kinetic energy ½mω²(x₀² − x²).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Interpolates energy linearly as E_tot(1 − x / x₀) instead of quadratically as E_tot(1 − x² / x₀²).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes the total mechanical energy ½mω²x₀² instead of subtracting potential energy at x.

items.stem: Engineers designing a beam-turning prism on a submarine periscope window assembly send a ray in synthetic sapphire (n₁ = 1.77, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) onto fused-silica glass (n₂ = 1.46) at 72° to the normal. What is the angular deflection δ between the incident direction and the emerging reflected ray?
items.workedSolution: Since sin θ_c = 1.46 / 1.77 gives θ_c = 55.6° and θ₁ = 72° > θ_c, the beam undergoes total internal reflection with θ_r = 72°. The angular deviation from the original forward direction is δ = 180° − 2(72°) = 36.0°.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies TIR (θ₁ > θ_c = 55.6°) and computes δ = 180° − 2θ₁ = 36.0° (C).

items.stem: During alignment of an avionics fly-by-light data bus, monochromatic light from water (n_ext = 1.33) strikes the entry face of a 200 m step-index fiber (n_core = 1.6, n_clad = 1.5) at 16.6° to the central optic axis. Determine the angle of incidence θ_w at the cylindrical core–cladding boundary relative to its normal.
items.workedSolution: At the entry face, 1.33 sin 16.6° = 1.6 sin θ_axis ⇒ θ_axis = 13.7°. Since the core wall is parallel to the axis, its normal is perpendicular to the axis, giving θ_w = 90° − θ_axis = 76.3°.

items.stem: A thin converging inspection lens of focal length 0.25 m in a botanical loupe magnifier bench views an upright feature of height 0.018 m held at object distance u = 0.1875 m (< f). What is the height h_i of the virtual upright image?
items.workedSolution: From 1/v = 1/0.25 − 1/0.1875, v = -0.750 m. Linear magnification m = −v / u = 4.000, so upright image height h_i = m h_o = 0.0720 m.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses the diverging-lens formula f / (f + u) for magnification, obtaining a diminished height smaller than h_o.

options.label: C

items.stem: A test rig using a spacecraft thruster-valve return-spring test fixture has mass 0.8 kg, horizontal spring constant 160 N m⁻¹, and oscillation amplitude 0.035 m. What is the natural frequency f of the oscillation?
items.workedSolution: Natural frequency f = (1 / 2π)√(k / m) = (1 / 2π)√(160 / 0.8) = 2.25 Hz.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Swaps k/m and m/k, computing (1 / 2π)√(m / k) instead of (1 / 2π)√(k / m).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes the period T = 2π√(m / k) instead of frequency f = 1 / T.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Reports angular frequency ω = √(k / m) in rad s⁻¹ without dividing by 2π.

items.stem: A vertical helical spring of stiffness 100 N m⁻¹ in a precision gravimeter spring-mass test stage suspends a load of mass 0.6 kg that subsequently oscillates vertically with amplitude 0.024 m. Taking g = 9.8 m s⁻², what was the static extension Δx_eq of the spring at equilibrium before oscillation started?
items.workedSolution: At static equilibrium, upward spring tension balances weight: k Δx_eq = mg ⇒ Δx_eq = (0.6 × 9.8) / 100 = 0.0588 m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Hooke's law as k / (mg) instead of mg / k.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Adds the oscillation amplitude x₀ to mg / k, finding maximum total stretch rather than static equilibrium extension.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides mass m directly by spring constant k without multiplying by gravitational field strength g.

items.stem: In a physics laboratory light-gate timing pendulum, a simple pendulum of length 0.72 m and bob mass 0.4 kg swings with small arc amplitude 0.1584 m where g = 9.81 m s⁻². Calculate its speed at the equilibrium position.
items.workedSolution: Angular frequency ω = √(g / L) = √(9.81 / 0.72), so maximum speed v_max = ω x₀ = 0.585 m s⁻¹.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts g / L inside √(g / L) when computing ω x₀.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Treats the horizontal arc amplitude x₀ as a vertical free-fall drop height h in √(2gh).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes ω² x₀ = (g / L) x₀ (maximum acceleration) instead of ω x₀ = √(g / L) x₀.

items.stem: During calibration of a piezoelectric laser-mirror dithering stage vibrating at f = 12 Hz and amplitude 0.06 m, a laser sensor records an instantaneous displacement x = 0.027 m. Determine the signed SHM acceleration a at that instant.
items.workedSolution: Angular frequency ω = 2πf = 2π(12) = 75.40 rad s⁻¹. By the defining SHM equation, a = −ω²x = −(75.40)²(0.027) = -153 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ω = 2πf and obtains -153 m s⁻² (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes cyclic frequency f directly for angular frequency ω, computing −f²x instead of −(2πf)²x.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates −ωx instead of −ω²x, forgetting to square the angular frequency.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the restoring minus sign in a = −ω²x, giving acceleration in the same sign as displacement instead of toward equilibrium.

items.stem: For an ultrasonic wire-bonding horn tip executing undamped SHM of mass 0.6 kg, angular frequency 20 rad s⁻¹, and amplitude 0.04 m (reference mark at 0.016 m), determine the positive displacement at which E_k = E_p.
items.workedSolution: Setting E_p = ½E_tot gives ½mω²x² = ½(½mω²x₀²), so x² = x₀² / 2 and x = x₀ / √2 = 0.04 / √2 = 0.0283 m.

markScheme.criterion: Solves x² = x₀² / 2 to obtain x = x₀ / √2 = 0.0283 m (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes (√3 / 2)x₀ (where E_p = ¾E_tot) instead of x₀ / √2.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Assumes E_k = E_p occurs at half the amplitude (x₀ / 2, where E_p = ¼E_tot) instead of x₀ / √2.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Squares the ½ factor to obtain x₀ / 4 instead of taking the square root x₀ / √2.

items.stem: Engineers specifying a borehole geophysical telemetry line test a 40 m step-index optical fiber having n_core = 1.62 and n_clad = 1.51 under a 12.6° test beam from air (n_ext = 1.00). Calculate the minimum angle of incidence to the wall normal required for total internal reflection inside the core.
items.workedSolution: At the core–cladding boundary, sin θ_c = n_clad / n_core = 1.51 / 1.62 = 0.9321, giving θ_c = 68.8°.

items.stem: In a museum conservation inspection magnifier, a thin converging lens of focal length 0.15 m is used as a simple magnifier so that an object of height 0.022 m forms an upright virtual image 0.600 m in front of the lens (v = −0.600 m in the real-is-positive convention). At what object distance u in front of the lens is the object held?
items.workedSolution: For a virtual image in the real-is-positive convention, v = -0.600 m. Thus 1/u = 1/f − 1/v = 1/0.15 − (1/-0.6000) = 8.333 m⁻¹, giving u = 0.120 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes negative v = -0.600 m into 1/u = 1/f − 1/v to obtain u = 0.120 m (D).

items.stem: In a clinical optometry phoropter test cell, an object of height 0.03 m is positioned 1 m from a concave lens of focal length −0.4 m. Calculate the signed linear magnification m = h_i / h_o = −v / u.
items.workedSolution: With f = −0.4 m, 1/v = −1/0.4 − 1/1 gives v = -0.286 m. Therefore m = −v / u = −(-0.2857) / 1 = 0.286 (upright and diminished).

markScheme.criterion: Finds v = -0.286 m and m = −v / u = 0.286 (B).

options.distractorRationale: Assigns a negative magnification as if a diverging lens formed an inverted real image of a real object.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes positive f = +|f| instead of negative f = −|f| into the lens equation before computing magnification.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the magnification ratio as u / |v| (> 1) instead of |v| / u (< 1).

items.stem: Engineers testing an acoustic transducer moving-coil suspension rig hang a 0.5 kg mass from a vertical coil spring (k = 40 N m⁻¹) and excite vertical oscillations of amplitude 0.032 m in a gravitational field g = 9.81 m s⁻². Determine the period T of oscillation.
items.workedSolution: Gravity shifts the equilibrium position without altering effective stiffness k, so T = 2π√(m / k) = 2π√(0.5 / 40) = 0.702 s.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes the oscillation amplitude x₀ into a pendulum-style formula 2π√(x₀ / g) instead of 2π√(m / k).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Swaps m/k and k/m inside the square root.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Incorrectly adds weight mg to spring stiffness k, assuming gravity changes the vertical mass-spring period.

items.stem: In a vibrometer calibration shaker table, an oscillator undergoes SHM at 5 Hz with amplitude 0.08 m (passing through x = -0.06 m). Calculate the peak acceleration magnitude a_max = (2πf)² x₀.
items.workedSolution: With ω = 2π(5) = 31.42 rad s⁻¹, maximum acceleration magnitude a_max = ω² x₀ = 79.0 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ω = 2πf and obtains 79.0 m s⁻² (B).

options.label: D

items.stem: A harmonic oscillator in a marine wave-tank oscillating piston paddle moves with amplitude x₀ = 0.06 m and angular frequency ω = 8 rad s⁻¹. Calculate its speed when passing through displacement x = 0.03 m.
items.workedSolution: Using v = ω√(x₀² − x²) gives v = 8 × √(0.06² − 0.03²) = 0.416 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into v = ω√(x₀² − x²) to obtain 0.416 m s⁻¹ (C).

options.distractorRationale: Adds x₀² + x² inside the square root instead of subtracting x₀² − x².

options.label: B

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses ωx instead of ω√(x₀² − x²), mistakenly assuming speed is directly proportional to displacement.

items.stem: Within a spectrophotometer cuvette wall, monochromatic light (vacuum speed 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) propagating in crystalline zircon (n₁ = 1.92) is incident at 49° to the normal on distilled water (n₂ = 1.33). Determine the critical angle θ_c between these two media.
items.workedSolution: At the critical angle θ_c, sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1.33 / 1.92 = 0.6927, giving θ_c = arcsin(0.6927) = 43.8°.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1.33 / 1.92 to obtain θ_c = 43.8° (C).

items.stem: During alignment of a short-reach datacenter patch cord, monochromatic light from air (n_ext = 1.00) strikes the entry face of a 350 m step-index fiber (n_core = 1.49, n_clad = 1.39) at 14° to the central optic axis. Determine the angle of incidence θ_w at the cylindrical core–cladding boundary relative to its normal.
items.workedSolution: At the entry face, 1 sin 14° = 1.49 sin θ_axis ⇒ θ_axis = 9.34°. Since the core wall is parallel to the axis, its normal is perpendicular to the axis, giving θ_w = 90° − θ_axis = 80.7°.

items.stem: Engineers coupling light from air of refractive index 1.00 into a 750 m step-index fiber (n_core = 1.57, n_clad = 1.46, reference beam at 22.2°) for a cryogenic laboratory optical feedthrough must stay within the acceptance cone. Calculate the acceptance half-angle θ_max in the external medium.
items.workedSolution: At the grazing limit, sin θ_c = 1.46 / 1.57, so inside the core sin θ_axis,max = cos θ_c = √(1 − (n_clad / n_core)²). By Snell's law at the entry face, n_ext sin θ_max = √(n_core² − n_clad²) = 0.5773, giving θ_max = arcsin(0.5773) = 35.3°.

markScheme.criterion: Uses n_ext sin θ_max = √(n_core² − n_clad²) to obtain θ_max = 35.3° (B).

items.stem: In a pulsed-laser divergence compensator, an upright test object of height 0.05 m stands 0.18 m in front of a thin diverging lens of focal length magnitude 0.3 m (f = −0.3 m in the real-is-positive convention). What is the signed image distance v?
items.workedSolution: For a diverging lens, f = −0.3 m. Using 1/f = 1/u + 1/v gives 1/v = −1/0.3 − 1/0.18 = -8.889 m⁻¹, so v = -0.113 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses negative f = −0.3 m in 1/v = 1/f − 1/u to obtain v = -0.113 m (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Stops at 1/v = −1/|f| − 1/u in m⁻¹ without taking the reciprocal to find v in metres.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes the correct magnitude |v| but omits the negative sign required for a virtual image in the real-is-positive convention.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Forgets that a diverging lens has negative focal length f < 0, substituting +|f| into 1/v = 1/f − 1/u.

items.stem: An experimental setup consisting of a robotics compliant-actuator test carriage has oscillating mass 0.25 kg, spring stiffness 45 N m⁻¹, and horizontal amplitude 0.045 m. Calculate the oscillation period T.
items.workedSolution: For an ideal mass-spring oscillator, T = 2π√(m / k) = 2π√(0.25 / 45) = 0.468 s.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Omits the square root and evaluates 2π(m / k).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 2π and calculates √(m / k) = 1 / ω.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Swaps m/k and k/m inside the radical, computing 2π√(k / m) instead of 2π√(m / k).

items.stem: A 0.25 kg brass bob on a 2.4 m suspension wire in a mine-shaft gravity-anomaly survey pendulum oscillates with arc-length amplitude 0.6 m (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Calculate the maximum cord tension at the bottom of the swing.
items.workedSolution: With ω = √(g / L) = √(9.81 / 2.4), peak speed v_max = ω x₀ = 1.21 m s⁻¹. At the lowest point, T_cord = m(g + v_max² / L) = 2.61 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_max = ω x₀ and T_cord = mg + mv_max² / L = 2.61 N (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Equates cord tension at the lowest point to static weight mg, ignoring the upward centripetal force mv_max² / L.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts the centripetal force mv_max² / L from mg instead of adding it at the bottom of the arc.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates only the net radial centripetal force mv_max² / L rather than the total cord tension.

items.stem: A harmonic oscillator in a dynamic mechanical thermal-analyzer probe moves with amplitude x₀ = 0.05 m and angular frequency ω = 24 rad s⁻¹. Calculate its speed when passing through displacement x = 0.018 m.
items.workedSolution: Using v = ω√(x₀² − x²) gives v = 24 × √(0.05² − 0.018²) = 1.12 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into v = ω√(x₀² − x²) to obtain 1.12 m s⁻¹ (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses ωx instead of ω√(x₀² − x²), mistakenly assuming speed is directly proportional to displacement.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates ω(x₀ − x) linearly instead of taking √(x₀² − x²).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the maximum speed ωx₀ at equilibrium (x = 0) instead of the speed at x.

items.stem: In a scanning-probe interferometric calibration stage, an oscillating body of mass 0.25 kg executes simple harmonic motion with angular frequency ω = 10 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude x₀ = 0.12 m. What is its kinetic energy E_k when its displacement from equilibrium is x = 0.06 m?
items.workedSolution: Using E_k = ½mω²(x₀² − x²) gives E_k = 0.5 × 0.25 × 10² × (0.12² − 0.06²) = 0.135 J.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the potential energy ½mω²x² at x rather than the kinetic energy ½mω²(x₀² − x²).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes the total mechanical energy ½mω²x₀² instead of subtracting potential energy at x.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Interpolates energy linearly as E_tot(1 − x / x₀) instead of quadratically as E_tot(1 − x² / x₀²).

items.stem: In an ophthalmic lens-blank inspection jig, an optical beam propagating in crystalline zircon (n₁ = 1.92, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) meets a planar liquid ethanol boundary (n₂ = 1.36) at an angle of incidence of 54° to the normal. Calculate the angular deviation of the beam produced at the interface.
items.workedSolution: Since sin θ_c = 1.36 / 1.92 gives θ_c = 45.1° and θ₁ = 54° > θ_c, the beam undergoes total internal reflection with θ_r = 54°. The angular deviation from the original forward direction is δ = 180° − 2(54°) = 72.0°.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies TIR (θ₁ > θ_c = 45.1°) and computes δ = 180° − 2θ₁ = 72.0° (A).

items.stem: Engineers evaluating bit-rate limits for an autonomous lidar reference delay spool test a 240 m step-index waveguide (n_core = 1.48, n_clad = 1.41, n_ext = 1.00, ray shown at 18.7°). Take c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹. Determine the multipath dispersion delay Δt between extreme guided rays and axial rays.
items.workedSolution: Axial transit time t_min = n_core L / c = (1.48 × 240) / (3.00 × 10⁸) = 1.18 × 10⁻⁶ s. At the critical angle sin θ_c = n_clad / n_core, t_max = t_min / sin θ_c = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 1.24 × 10⁻⁶ s. Modal delay Δt = t_max − t_min = 5.88 × 10⁻⁸ s.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δt = (n_core L / c)(n_core / n_clad − 1) = 5.88 × 10⁻⁸ s (B).

items.stem: A thin converging inspection lens of focal length 0.12 m in a retinal fundus imaging objective rig views an upright feature of height 0.018 m held at object distance u = 0.048 m (< f). What is the height h_i of the virtual upright image?
items.workedSolution: From 1/v = 1/0.12 − 1/0.048, v = -0.0800 m. Linear magnification m = −v / u = 1.667, so upright image height h_i = m h_o = 0.0300 m.

items.stem: During optical testing on an underwater dome-port virtual-image corrector, a 0.02 m illuminated target sits 0.42 m from a thin diverging lens of focal length −0.3 m. Determine the signed image position v under the real-is-positive sign convention.
items.workedSolution: For a diverging lens, f = −0.3 m. Using 1/f = 1/u + 1/v gives 1/v = −1/0.3 − 1/0.42 = -5.714 m⁻¹, so v = -0.175 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses negative f = −0.3 m in 1/v = 1/f − 1/u to obtain v = -0.175 m (C).

options.distractorRationale: Forgets that a diverging lens has negative focal length f < 0, substituting +|f| into 1/v = 1/f − 1/u.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes the correct magnitude |v| but omits the negative sign required for a virtual image in the real-is-positive convention.

options.label: D

items.stem: A vertical helical spring of stiffness 25 N m⁻¹ in an orbital microgravity mass-measurement spring chair suspends a load of mass 0.9 kg that subsequently oscillates vertically with amplitude 0.024 m. Taking g = 9.81 m s⁻², what was the static extension Δx_eq of the spring at equilibrium before oscillation started?
items.workedSolution: At static equilibrium, upward spring tension balances weight: k Δx_eq = mg ⇒ Δx_eq = (0.9 × 9.81) / 25 = 0.353 m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Divides mass m directly by spring constant k without multiplying by gravitational field strength g.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Adds the oscillation amplitude x₀ to mg / k, finding maximum total stretch rather than static equilibrium extension.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Hooke's law as k / (mg) instead of mg / k.

items.stem: A 0.6 kg pendulum bob suspended from a 2.4 m wire in an astronomical observatory sidereal regulator pendulum oscillates in SHM with arc amplitude 0.48 m (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). What is the maximum speed v_max of the bob?
items.workedSolution: Angular frequency ω = √(g / L) = √(9.81 / 2.4), so maximum speed v_max = ω x₀ = 0.970 m s⁻¹.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Treats the horizontal arc amplitude x₀ as a vertical free-fall drop height h in √(2gh).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes ω² x₀ = (g / L) x₀ (maximum acceleration) instead of ω x₀ = √(g / L) x₀.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts g / L inside √(g / L) when computing ω x₀.

items.stem: In a precision optical-chopper resonant blade, an oscillator undergoes SHM at 5 Hz with amplitude 0.05 m (passing through x = 0.0175 m). Calculate the peak acceleration magnitude a_max = (2πf)² x₀.
items.workedSolution: With ω = 2π(5) = 31.42 rad s⁻¹, maximum acceleration magnitude a_max = ω² x₀ = 49.3 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ω = 2πf and obtains 49.3 m s⁻² (B).

items.stem: For a diesel injector needle-valve harmonic test rig executing undamped SHM of mass 0.6 kg, angular frequency 30 rad s⁻¹, and amplitude 0.08 m (reference mark at 0.064 m), determine the positive displacement at which E_k = E_p.
items.workedSolution: Setting E_p = ½E_tot gives ½mω²x² = ½(½mω²x₀²), so x² = x₀² / 2 and x = x₀ / √2 = 0.08 / √2 = 0.0566 m.

markScheme.criterion: Solves x² = x₀² / 2 to obtain x = x₀ / √2 = 0.0566 m (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes (√3 / 2)x₀ (where E_p = ¾E_tot) instead of x₀ / √2.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Assumes E_k = E_p occurs at half the amplitude (x₀ / 2, where E_p = ¼E_tot) instead of x₀ / √2.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Squares the ½ factor to obtain x₀ / 4 instead of taking the square root x₀ / √2.

items.stem: A 200 m step-index optical fiber used in an astronomical echelle-spectrograph feed has core refractive index 1.57 and cladding refractive index 1.46. A laser ray in air (n_ext = 1.00) enters the center of the flat end-face at θ_in = 20.8° to the fiber axis. What angle of incidence θ_w does the refracted ray make with the normal to the core–cladding wall?
items.workedSolution: At the entry face, 1 sin 20.8° = 1.57 sin θ_axis ⇒ θ_axis = 13.1°. Since the core wall is parallel to the axis, its normal is perpendicular to the axis, giving θ_w = 90° − θ_axis = 76.9°.

items.stem: A 2400 m multimode step-index cable in a subterranean pipeline temperature-sensing cable has core index 1.6 and cladding index 1.5 in air (n_ext = 1.00, sample launch angle 13.5°, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹). Calculate the maximum guided transit time through the fiber.
items.workedSolution: Wave speed in the core is v = c / n_core, and the critical-angle ray travels path length L / sin θ_c = L (n_core / n_clad). Therefore t_max = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 1.37 × 10⁻⁵ s.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates t_max = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 1.37 × 10⁻⁵ s (A).

items.stem: In a heads-up display collimating negative element, an object of height 0.045 m is positioned 0.42 m from a concave lens of focal length −0.3 m. Calculate the signed linear magnification m = h_i / h_o = −v / u.
items.workedSolution: With f = −0.3 m, 1/v = −1/0.3 − 1/0.42 gives v = -0.175 m. Therefore m = −v / u = −(-0.1750) / 0.42 = 0.417 (upright and diminished).

markScheme.criterion: Finds v = -0.175 m and m = −v / u = 0.417 (C).

options.distractorRationale: Assigns a negative magnification as if a diverging lens formed an inverted real image of a real object.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes positive f = +|f| instead of negative f = −|f| into the lens equation before computing magnification.

options.label: D

items.stem: A 0.36 kg test mass in a railway bogie secondary-suspension scale model executes horizontal simple harmonic motion of amplitude 0.11 m and period T = 0.444 s. Calculate the stiffness k of the spring.
items.workedSolution: Rearranging T = 2π√(m / k) gives k = 4π²m / T² = 4π²(0.36) / (0.444)² = 72.0 N m⁻¹.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Fails to square 2π / T when rearranging T = 2π√(m / k), computing 2πm / T instead of 4π²m / T².

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Inverts m / T² when rearranging the period equation.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 4π² and computes m / T².

items.stem: The acceleration–displacement line shown models a micro-electro-mechanical resonant beam oscillating harmonically at 8 Hz with amplitude 0.04 m. Using a = −ω²x, calculate the signed acceleration at displacement x = -0.024 m.
items.workedSolution: Angular frequency ω = 2πf = 2π(8) = 50.27 rad s⁻¹. By the defining SHM equation, a = −ω²x = −(50.27)²(-0.024) = 60.6 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ω = 2πf and obtains 60.6 m s⁻² (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Omits the restoring minus sign in a = −ω²x, giving acceleration in the same sign as displacement instead of toward equilibrium.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates −ωx instead of −ω²x, forgetting to square the angular frequency.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes cyclic frequency f directly for angular frequency ω, computing −f²x instead of −(2πf)²x.

items.stem: In an ultrasonic wire-bonding horn tip, a stage oscillates in simple harmonic motion with angular frequency ω = 15 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude x₀ = 0.04 m, tracing the velocity–displacement ellipse shown. What is the speed v of the stage when its displacement from equilibrium is x = 0.032 m?
items.workedSolution: Using v = ω√(x₀² − x²) gives v = 15 × √(0.04² − 0.032²) = 0.360 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into v = ω√(x₀² − x²) to obtain 0.360 m s⁻¹ (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the maximum speed ωx₀ at equilibrium (x = 0) instead of the speed at x.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses ωx instead of ω√(x₀² − x²), mistakenly assuming speed is directly proportional to displacement.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates ω(x₀ − x) linearly instead of taking √(x₀² − x²).

items.stem: In a semiconductor immersion-lithography stage, a light ray inside optical crown glass (n₁ = 1.52, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) approaches a planar interface with distilled water (n₂ = 1.33) at an incident angle of 78° to the normal. What is the critical angle θ_c at this optical crown glass–distilled water boundary?
items.workedSolution: At the critical angle θ_c, sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1.33 / 1.52 = 0.8750, giving θ_c = arcsin(0.8750) = 61.0°.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1.33 / 1.52 to obtain θ_c = 61.0° (B).

items.stem: A 350 m step-index waveguide in a high-voltage substation optical isolator link is fabricated with a core of refractive index 1.57 surrounded by cladding of refractive index 1.46, with light launched from water (n_ext = 1.33) at 17.2° to the axis. What is the critical angle θ_c at the core–cladding interface?
items.workedSolution: At the core–cladding boundary, sin θ_c = n_clad / n_core = 1.46 / 1.57 = 0.9299, giving θ_c = 68.4°.

items.stem: Within an optical-bench crosswire projection setup, an upright scale mark of height 0.022 m sits 0.16 m from a thin convex lens of focal length 0.2 m. Applying 1/f = 1/u + 1/v in the real-is-positive convention, determine the signed image position v.
items.workedSolution: Because u = 0.16 m < f = 0.2 m, 1/v = 1/0.2 − 1/0.16 = -1.250 m⁻¹, giving a signed virtual image distance v = -0.800 m.

markScheme.criterion: Computes 1/v = 1/0.2 − 1/0.16 to obtain signed v = -0.800 m (A).

items.stem: Engineers testing a precision gravimeter spring-mass test stage measure a moving mass of 1.5 kg attached to an ideal horizontal spring of constant 56 N m⁻¹ oscillating with amplitude 0.06 m. Determine the period T of one complete cycle.
items.workedSolution: For an ideal mass-spring oscillator, T = 2π√(m / k) = 2π√(1.5 / 56) = 1.03 s.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 2π and calculates √(m / k) = 1 / ω.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the square root and evaluates 2π(m / k).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Swaps m/k and k/m inside the radical, computing 2π√(k / m) instead of 2π√(m / k).

items.stem: A vertical helical spring of stiffness 32 N m⁻¹ in a high-speed pantograph contact-spring test rig suspends a load of mass 1.2 kg that subsequently oscillates vertically with amplitude 0.032 m. Taking g = 9.81 m s⁻², what was the static extension Δx_eq of the spring at equilibrium before oscillation started?
items.workedSolution: At static equilibrium, upward spring tension balances weight: k Δx_eq = mg ⇒ Δx_eq = (1.2 × 9.81) / 32 = 0.368 m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Divides mass m directly by spring constant k without multiplying by gravitational field strength g.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Adds the oscillation amplitude x₀ to mg / k, finding maximum total stretch rather than static equilibrium extension.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Hooke's law as k / (mg) instead of mg / k.

items.stem: A 0.15 kg brass bob on a 1.05 m suspension wire in a metrology gravimetry pendulum stand oscillates with arc-length amplitude 0.21 m (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Calculate the maximum cord tension at the bottom of the swing.
items.workedSolution: With ω = √(g / L) = √(9.81 / 1.05), peak speed v_max = ω x₀ = 0.642 m s⁻¹. At the lowest point, T_cord = m(g + v_max² / L) = 1.53 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_max = ω x₀ and T_cord = mg + mv_max² / L = 1.53 N (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Equates cord tension at the lowest point to static weight mg, ignoring the upward centripetal force mv_max² / L.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts the centripetal force mv_max² / L from mg instead of adding it at the bottom of the arc.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates only the net radial centripetal force mv_max² / L rather than the total cord tension.

items.stem: In a marine wave-tank oscillating piston paddle, an oscillator undergoes SHM at 5 Hz with amplitude 0.08 m (passing through x = 0.048 m). Calculate the peak acceleration magnitude a_max = (2πf)² x₀.
items.workedSolution: With ω = 2π(5) = 31.42 rad s⁻¹, maximum acceleration magnitude a_max = ω² x₀ = 79.0 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ω = 2πf and obtains 79.0 m s⁻² (D).

options.distractorRationale: Calculates ω x₀ (maximum speed) instead of ω² x₀ (maximum acceleration).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes the acceleration magnitude at x rather than at maximum displacement x₀.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor (2π)² = 4π² and computes f² x₀.

items.stem: In an ultrasonic surgical transducer tip, an oscillating body of mass 0.25 kg executes simple harmonic motion with angular frequency ω = 20 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude x₀ = 0.12 m. What is its kinetic energy E_k when its displacement from equilibrium is x = 0.096 m?
items.workedSolution: Using E_k = ½mω²(x₀² − x²) gives E_k = 0.5 × 0.25 × 20² × (0.12² − 0.096²) = 0.259 J.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes the total mechanical energy ½mω²x₀² instead of subtracting potential energy at x.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the potential energy ½mω²x² at x rather than the kinetic energy ½mω²(x₀² − x²).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Interpolates energy linearly as E_tot(1 − x / x₀) instead of quadratically as E_tot(1 − x² / x₀²).

items.stem: In a planetary lander atmospheric nephelometer, an optical beam propagating in crystalline zircon (n₁ = 1.92, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) meets a planar distilled water boundary (n₂ = 1.33) at an angle of incidence of 52° to the normal. Calculate the angular deviation of the beam produced at the interface.
items.workedSolution: Since sin θ_c = 1.33 / 1.92 gives θ_c = 43.8° and θ₁ = 52° > θ_c, the beam undergoes total internal reflection with θ_r = 52°. The angular deviation from the original forward direction is δ = 180° − 2(52°) = 76.0°.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies TIR (θ₁ > θ_c = 43.8°) and computes δ = 180° − 2θ₁ = 76.0° (C).

items.stem: A thin converging inspection lens of focal length 0.1 m in a refracting telescope objective assembly views an upright feature of height 0.012 m held at object distance u = 0.08 m (< f). What is the height h_i of the virtual upright image?
items.workedSolution: From 1/v = 1/0.1 − 1/0.08, v = -0.400 m. Linear magnification m = −v / u = 5.000, so upright image height h_i = m h_o = 0.0600 m.

items.stem: In an architectural wide-field door viewer, an upright test object of height 0.03 m stands 0.15 m in front of a thin diverging lens of focal length magnitude 0.1 m (f = −0.1 m in the real-is-positive convention). What is the signed image distance v?
items.workedSolution: For a diverging lens, f = −0.1 m. Using 1/f = 1/u + 1/v gives 1/v = −1/0.1 − 1/0.15 = -16.67 m⁻¹, so v = -0.0600 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses negative f = −0.1 m in 1/v = 1/f − 1/u to obtain v = -0.0600 m (B).

items.stem: In a cryogenic cooler linear-compressor piston assembly, a 0.75 kg mass hangs from a vertical spring of constant 50 N m⁻¹ and executes vertical SHM of amplitude 0.018 m (take g = 9.8 m s⁻²). Calculate the static equilibrium extension Δx_eq from the spring's unstretched length.
items.workedSolution: At static equilibrium, upward spring tension balances weight: k Δx_eq = mg ⇒ Δx_eq = (0.75 × 9.8) / 50 = 0.147 m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Divides mass m directly by spring constant k without multiplying by gravitational field strength g.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Adds the oscillation amplitude x₀ to mg / k, finding maximum total stretch rather than static equilibrium extension.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Hooke's law as k / (mg) instead of mg / k.

items.stem: During calibration of a dynamic mechanical thermal-analyzer probe vibrating at f = 2.5 Hz and amplitude 0.04 m, a laser sensor records an instantaneous displacement x = 0.018 m. Determine the signed SHM acceleration a at that instant.
items.workedSolution: Angular frequency ω = 2πf = 2π(2.5) = 15.71 rad s⁻¹. By the defining SHM equation, a = −ω²x = −(15.71)²(0.018) = -4.44 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ω = 2πf and obtains -4.44 m s⁻² (C).

items.stem: In a scanning-probe interferometric calibration stage, a stage oscillates in simple harmonic motion with angular frequency ω = 30 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude x₀ = 0.15 m, tracing the velocity–displacement ellipse shown. What is the speed v of the stage when its displacement from equilibrium is x = 0.075 m?
items.workedSolution: Using v = ω√(x₀² − x²) gives v = 30 × √(0.15² − 0.075²) = 3.90 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into v = ω√(x₀² − x²) to obtain 3.90 m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: An over-angled ray in air (n_ext = 1.00) is launched at 34° to the central axis into a 200 m step-index waveguide (n_core = 1.52, n_clad = 1.46) during a cryogenic laboratory optical feedthrough. At what angle to the cylindrical wall normal does the leaked ray refract into the cladding?
items.workedSolution: At entry, sin θ_axis = (1 sin 34°) / 1.52 ⇒ θ_axis = 21.6°. The angle to the wall normal is θ_w = 90° − θ_axis = 68.4° (< θ_c = 73.8°). Refracting into the cladding: sin θ_clad = (1.52 sin θ_w) / 1.46, giving θ_clad = 75.5°.

markScheme.criterion: Finds θ_w = 68.4° and refracts into cladding to obtain 75.5° (D).

items.stem: In a structural-health bridge sensor lead, light from air (n_ext = 1.00, illustrated at 22.7°) propagates along a 2400 m step-index fiber with n_core = 1.49 and n_clad = 1.39. Taking c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, what is the transit time t_max of the slowest guided ray that meets the core–cladding wall at the critical angle?
items.workedSolution: Wave speed in the core is v = c / n_core, and the critical-angle ray travels path length L / sin θ_c = L (n_core / n_clad). Therefore t_max = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 1.28 × 10⁻⁵ s.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates t_max = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 1.28 × 10⁻⁵ s (D).

items.stem: A thin diverging lens of focal length f = −0.25 m in a high-power excimer beam-shaping negative lens forms a virtual image of an upright object of height 0.02 m placed at u = 0.75 m. What is the linear magnification m = −v / u of the image?
items.workedSolution: With f = −0.25 m, 1/v = −1/0.25 − 1/0.75 gives v = -0.188 m. Therefore m = −v / u = −(-0.1875) / 0.75 = 0.250 (upright and diminished).

markScheme.criterion: Finds v = -0.188 m and m = −v / u = 0.250 (C).

items.stem: During stiffness testing on a cleanroom nanopositioning flexure stage, a 0.64 kg mass oscillates horizontally with amplitude 0.045 m and a measured period of 0.672 s. What is the spring constant k?
items.workedSolution: Rearranging T = 2π√(m / k) gives k = 4π²m / T² = 4π²(0.64) / (0.672)² = 56.0 N m⁻¹.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Inverts m / T² when rearranging the period equation.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Fails to square 2π / T when rearranging T = 2π√(m / k), computing 2πm / T instead of 4π²m / T².

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 4π² and computes m / T².

items.stem: A metrology pendulum in a skyscraper tuned-pendulum damper scale model has suspension length 0.85 m, bob mass 0.5 kg, and arc amplitude 0.187 m. Taking g = 9.81 m s⁻², what is its oscillation period T?

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts L / g inside the square root.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the half-period π√(L / g) instead of the full period 2π√(L / g).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the square root on L / g.

items.stem: In a diesel injector needle-valve harmonic test rig, a stage oscillates in simple harmonic motion with angular frequency ω = 20 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude x₀ = 0.15 m, tracing the velocity–displacement ellipse shown. What is the speed v of the stage when its displacement from equilibrium is x = 0.075 m?
items.workedSolution: Using v = ω√(x₀² − x²) gives v = 20 × √(0.15² − 0.075²) = 2.60 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into v = ω√(x₀² − x²) to obtain 2.60 m s⁻¹ (D).

options.distractorRationale: Calculates the maximum speed ωx₀ at equilibrium (x = 0) instead of the speed at x.

options.label: B

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Adds x₀² + x² inside the square root instead of subtracting x₀² − x².

items.stem: A 1.2 kg resonator in an atomic-force microscope cantilever tip executes simple harmonic motion of amplitude 0.06 m and angular frequency ω = 10 rad s⁻¹ (probed at x = 0.024 m). At what cyclic frequency f_E does its kinetic energy oscillate with time?
items.workedSolution: Mechanical frequency f = ω / (2π) = 10 / (2π) = 1.592 Hz. Because kinetic energy reaches a maximum twice per mechanical period, f_E = 2f = ω / π = 3.18 Hz.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Gives the mechanical displacement frequency f = ω / (2π) instead of recognizing that E_k ∝ cos²(ωt) oscillates at 2f.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Calculates 2ω in rad s⁻¹ without dividing by 2π to convert to hertz.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Halves the mechanical frequency instead of doubling it.

items.stem: In an industrial sugar-brix inline refractometer, a light ray inside crystalline zircon (n₁ = 1.92, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) approaches a planar interface with fused-silica glass (n₂ = 1.46) at an incident angle of 66° to the normal. What is the critical angle θ_c at this crystalline zircon–fused-silica glass boundary?
items.workedSolution: At the critical angle θ_c, sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1.46 / 1.92 = 0.7604, giving θ_c = arcsin(0.7604) = 49.5°.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1.46 / 1.92 to obtain θ_c = 49.5° (D).

items.stem: Engineers coupling light from air of refractive index 1.00 into a 300 m step-index fiber (n_core = 1.58, n_clad = 1.49, reference beam at 14.3°) for a transoceanic telecommunications link must stay within the acceptance cone. Calculate the acceptance half-angle θ_max in the external medium.
items.workedSolution: At the grazing limit, sin θ_c = 1.49 / 1.58, so inside the core sin θ_axis,max = cos θ_c = √(1 − (n_clad / n_core)²). By Snell's law at the entry face, n_ext sin θ_max = √(n_core² − n_clad²) = 0.5256, giving θ_max = arcsin(0.5256) = 31.7°.

markScheme.criterion: Uses n_ext sin θ_max = √(n_core² − n_clad²) to obtain θ_max = 31.7° (A).

items.stem: A watchmaker's converging lens of focal length 0.1 m in a precision machine-vision inspection camera views an object of height 0.012 m placed inside the focal point at u = 0.035 m. Under the real-is-positive convention (v < 0 for virtual images), calculate v.
items.workedSolution: Because u = 0.035 m < f = 0.1 m, 1/v = 1/0.1 − 1/0.035 = -18.57 m⁻¹, giving a signed virtual image distance v = -0.0538 m.

markScheme.criterion: Computes 1/v = 1/0.1 − 1/0.035 to obtain signed v = -0.0538 m (D).
