items.stem: In an orbital microgravity mass-measurement spring chair of mass 1.2 kg and spring constant 72 N m⁻¹, the oscillator is displaced by an amplitude of 0.09 m from equilibrium and released. What is the period T of its simple harmonic motion?
items.workedSolution: For an ideal mass-spring oscillator, T = 2π√(m / k) = 2π√(1.2 / 72) = 0.811 s.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Swaps m/k and k/m inside the radical, computing 2π√(k / m) instead of 2π√(m / k).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 2π and calculates √(m / k) = 1 / ω.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the square root and evaluates 2π(m / k).

items.stem: In a frictionless air-track glider coupled to a calibrated coil spring, a 0.2 kg mass hangs from a vertical spring of constant 100 N m⁻¹ and executes vertical SHM of amplitude 0.032 m (take g = 9.8 m s⁻²). Calculate the static equilibrium extension Δx_eq from the spring's unstretched length.
items.workedSolution: At static equilibrium, upward spring tension balances weight: k Δx_eq = mg ⇒ Δx_eq = (0.2 × 9.8) / 100 = 0.0196 m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Divides mass m directly by spring constant k without multiplying by gravitational field strength g.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Adds the oscillation amplitude x₀ to mg / k, finding maximum total stretch rather than static equilibrium extension.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Hooke's law as k / (mg) instead of mg / k.

items.stem: In a geophysical field-survey simple pendulum, a pendulum bob of mass 0.15 kg hangs on a light cord of length 1.9 m and swings in small-angle SHM with arc amplitude 0.418 m. Taking g = 9.81 m s⁻², what is the tension in the cord as the bob passes through its lowest equilibrium point?
items.workedSolution: With ω = √(g / L) = √(9.81 / 1.9), peak speed v_max = ω x₀ = 0.950 m s⁻¹. At the lowest point, T_cord = m(g + v_max² / L) = 1.54 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_max = ω x₀ and T_cord = mg + mv_max² / L = 1.54 N (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Equates cord tension at the lowest point to static weight mg, ignoring the upward centripetal force mv_max² / L.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts the centripetal force mv_max² / L from mg instead of adding it at the bottom of the arc.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates only the net radial centripetal force mv_max² / L rather than the total cord tension.

items.stem: The acceleration–displacement line shown models an ultrasonic wire-bonding horn tip oscillating harmonically at 6 Hz with amplitude 0.05 m. Using a = −ω²x, calculate the signed acceleration at displacement x = 0.0225 m.
items.workedSolution: Angular frequency ω = 2πf = 2π(6) = 37.70 rad s⁻¹. By the defining SHM equation, a = −ω²x = −(37.70)²(0.0225) = -32.0 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ω = 2πf and obtains -32.0 m s⁻² (D).

options.distractorRationale: Omits the restoring minus sign in a = −ω²x, giving acceleration in the same sign as displacement instead of toward equilibrium.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes cyclic frequency f directly for angular frequency ω, computing −f²x instead of −(2πf)²x.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates −ωx instead of −ω²x, forgetting to square the angular frequency.

items.stem: The parabolic SHM energy graph shown corresponds to a studio loudspeaker voice-coil cone (mass 0.25 kg, angular frequency 10 rad s⁻¹, amplitude 0.12 m). Calculate the kinetic energy E_k at displacement x = 0.072 m.
items.workedSolution: Using E_k = ½mω²(x₀² − x²) gives E_k = 0.5 × 0.25 × 10² × (0.12² − 0.072²) = 0.115 J.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the potential energy ½mω²x² at x rather than the kinetic energy ½mω²(x₀² − x²).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Interpolates energy linearly as E_tot(1 − x / x₀) instead of quadratically as E_tot(1 − x² / x₀²).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes the total mechanical energy ½mω²x₀² instead of subtracting potential energy at x.

items.stem: A 120 m step-index waveguide in a fusion-chamber diagnostic optical relay is fabricated with a core of refractive index 1.48 surrounded by cladding of refractive index 1.41, with light launched from air (n_ext = 1.00) at 15.8° to the axis. What is the critical angle θ_c at the core–cladding interface?
items.workedSolution: At the core–cladding boundary, sin θ_c = n_clad / n_core = 1.41 / 1.48 = 0.9527, giving θ_c = 72.3°.

items.stem: A multimode step-index fiber of length 1200 m in an avionics fly-by-light data bus has n_core = 1.57 and n_clad = 1.46 in air (n_ext = 1.00, illustrated with a 17.6° launch ray). Taking c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹ and neglecting material dispersion, what is the maximum multipath (modal) pulse broadening Δt between the fastest axial ray and the slowest guided ray?
items.workedSolution: Axial transit time t_min = n_core L / c = (1.57 × 1200) / (3.00 × 10⁸) = 6.28 × 10⁻⁶ s. At the critical angle sin θ_c = n_clad / n_core, t_max = t_min / sin θ_c = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 6.75 × 10⁻⁶ s. Modal delay Δt = t_max − t_min = 4.73 × 10⁻⁷ s.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δt = (n_core L / c)(n_core / n_clad − 1) = 4.73 × 10⁻⁷ s (C).

items.stem: In a cinema slide-projector lens mount, a specimen of height 0.012 m is placed 0.144 m in front of a convex magnifying lens of focal length 0.24 m. Calculate the upright virtual image height h_i.
items.workedSolution: From 1/v = 1/0.24 − 1/0.144, v = -0.360 m. Linear magnification m = −v / u = 2.500, so upright image height h_i = m h_o = 0.0300 m.

items.stem: During optical testing on a myopia-corrective ophthalmic spectacle trial, a 0.05 m illuminated target sits 0.15 m from a thin diverging lens of focal length −0.25 m. Determine the signed image position v under the real-is-positive sign convention.
items.workedSolution: For a diverging lens, f = −0.25 m. Using 1/f = 1/u + 1/v gives 1/v = −1/0.25 − 1/0.15 = -10.67 m⁻¹, so v = -0.0937 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses negative f = −0.25 m in 1/v = 1/f − 1/u to obtain v = -0.0937 m (C).

items.stem: In a silicon MEMS accelerometer proof-mass flexure test model, a 1.2 kg mass hangs from a vertical spring of constant 50 N m⁻¹ and executes vertical SHM of amplitude 0.024 m (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Calculate the static equilibrium extension Δx_eq from the spring's unstretched length.
items.workedSolution: At static equilibrium, upward spring tension balances weight: k Δx_eq = mg ⇒ Δx_eq = (1.2 × 9.81) / 50 = 0.235 m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Divides mass m directly by spring constant k without multiplying by gravitational field strength g.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Adds the oscillation amplitude x₀ to mg / k, finding maximum total stretch rather than static equilibrium extension.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Hooke's law as k / (mg) instead of mg / k.

items.stem: In a resonant Coriolis mass-flow sensor tube, an oscillator undergoes SHM at 5 Hz with amplitude 0.08 m (passing through x = 0.06 m). Calculate the peak acceleration magnitude a_max = (2πf)² x₀.
items.workedSolution: With ω = 2π(5) = 31.42 rad s⁻¹, maximum acceleration magnitude a_max = ω² x₀ = 79.0 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ω = 2πf and obtains 79.0 m s⁻² (A).

items.stem: The velocity–displacement phase portrait shown represents an ultrasonic surgical transducer tip oscillating with ω = 20 rad s⁻¹ and x₀ = 0.12 m. Find the oscillator's speed at x = 0.072 m.
items.workedSolution: Using v = ω√(x₀² − x²) gives v = 20 × √(0.12² − 0.072²) = 1.92 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into v = ω√(x₀² − x²) to obtain 1.92 m s⁻¹ (A).

items.stem: A refractometer cell in a bathymetric laser-ranging tank immerses a polished dielectric slab in liquid ethanol (n₂ = 1.36), recording a critical angle of 50.2° relative to the boundary normal. Determine the refractive index n₁ of the dielectric slab.
items.workedSolution: At the critical angle, n₁ sin θ_c = n₂ sin 90° = n₂, so n₁ = 1.36 / sin 50.2° = 1.77.

markScheme.criterion: Computes n₁ = n₂ / sin θ_c = 1.36 / sin 50.2° = 1.77 (A).

items.stem: During alignment of a surgical laser-lithotripsy delivery fiber, monochromatic light from water (n_ext = 1.33) strikes the entry face of a 120 m step-index fiber (n_core = 1.6, n_clad = 1.5) at 16.6° to the central optic axis. Determine the angle of incidence θ_w at the cylindrical core–cladding boundary relative to its normal.
items.workedSolution: At the entry face, 1.33 sin 16.6° = 1.6 sin θ_axis ⇒ θ_axis = 13.7°. Since the core wall is parallel to the axis, its normal is perpendicular to the axis, giving θ_w = 90° − θ_axis = 76.3°.

items.stem: In a structural-health bridge sensor lead, a guided ray from water of refractive index 1.33 enters a straight 450 m step-index fiber (n_core = 1.49, n_clad = 1.39) at launch angle θ_in = 15° to the axis. Neglecting end losses, what total geometric path length does this zig-zagging ray travel through the core?
items.workedSolution: Inside the core, sin θ_axis = (1.33 sin 15°) / 1.49 ⇒ θ_axis = 13.4°. The total zig-zag geometric path length is L_ray = L / cos θ_axis = 450 / cos 13.36° = 463 m.

markScheme.criterion: Finds θ_axis = 13.4° and computes L / cos θ_axis = 463 m (B).

items.stem: In a laboratory autocollimator test rail, a thin converging lens of focal length 0.15 m is used as a simple magnifier so that an object of height 0.008 m forms an upright virtual image 0.319 m in front of the lens (v = −0.319 m in the real-is-positive convention). At what object distance u in front of the lens is the object held?
items.workedSolution: For a virtual image in the real-is-positive convention, v = -0.319 m. Thus 1/u = 1/f − 1/v = 1/0.15 − (1/-0.3187) = 9.804 m⁻¹, giving u = 0.102 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes negative v = -0.319 m into 1/u = 1/f − 1/v to obtain u = 0.102 m (A).

items.stem: A 1.5 kg test mass in a high-speed pantograph contact-spring test rig executes horizontal simple harmonic motion of amplitude 0.025 m and period T = 1.03 s. Calculate the stiffness k of the spring.
items.workedSolution: Rearranging T = 2π√(m / k) gives k = 4π²m / T² = 4π²(1.5) / (1.03)² = 56.0 N m⁻¹.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Inverts m / T² when rearranging the period equation.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Fails to square 2π / T when rearranging T = 2π√(m / k), computing 2πm / T instead of 4π²m / T².

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 4π² and computes m / T².

items.stem: A metrology pendulum in an evacuated bell-jar precision timing pendulum has suspension length 1.05 m, bob mass 0.5 kg, and arc amplitude 0.2625 m. Taking g = 9.81 m s⁻², what is its oscillation period T?

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts L / g inside the square root.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the half-period π√(L / g) instead of the full period 2π√(L / g).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the square root on L / g.

items.stem: In a quartz crystal tuning-fork tine, a stage oscillates in simple harmonic motion with angular frequency ω = 30 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude x₀ = 0.06 m, tracing the velocity–displacement ellipse shown. What is the speed v of the stage when its displacement from equilibrium is x = 0.048 m?
items.workedSolution: Using v = ω√(x₀² − x²) gives v = 30 × √(0.06² − 0.048²) = 1.08 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into v = ω√(x₀² − x²) to obtain 1.08 m s⁻¹ (B).

options.distractorRationale: Calculates the maximum speed ωx₀ at equilibrium (x = 0) instead of the speed at x.

options.label: C

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses ωx instead of ω√(x₀² − x²), mistakenly assuming speed is directly proportional to displacement.

items.stem: In a vibrometer calibration shaker table, a 0.4 kg mass undergoes SHM with ω = 18 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude 0.12 m (with a sensor at x = 0.096 m). Calculate the frequency f_E at which the kinetic energy completes full cycles.
items.workedSolution: Mechanical frequency f = ω / (2π) = 18 / (2π) = 2.865 Hz. Because kinetic energy reaches a maximum twice per mechanical period, f_E = 2f = ω / π = 5.73 Hz.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Halves the mechanical frequency instead of doubling it.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Gives the mechanical displacement frequency f = ω / (2π) instead of recognizing that E_k ∝ cos²(ωt) oscillates at 2f.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates 2ω in rad s⁻¹ without dividing by 2π to convert to hertz.

items.stem: A prism assembly in a precision Abbe refractometer cell places crystalline zircon of refractive index 1.92 in contact with dry air of refractive index 1 (take c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹). A test beam strikes the interface from inside crystalline zircon at 37° to the normal. Calculate the critical angle for total internal reflection at the boundary.
items.workedSolution: At the critical angle θ_c, sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1 / 1.92 = 0.5208, giving θ_c = arcsin(0.5208) = 31.4°.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1 / 1.92 to obtain θ_c = 31.4° (B).

items.stem: Engineers coupling light from air of refractive index 1.00 into a 750 m step-index fiber (n_core = 1.54, n_clad = 1.45, reference beam at 22.5°) for an industrial laser-welding delivery cable must stay within the acceptance cone. Calculate the acceptance half-angle θ_max in the external medium.
items.workedSolution: At the grazing limit, sin θ_c = 1.45 / 1.54, so inside the core sin θ_axis,max = cos θ_c = √(1 − (n_clad / n_core)²). By Snell's law at the entry face, n_ext sin θ_max = √(n_core² − n_clad²) = 0.5187, giving θ_max = arcsin(0.5187) = 31.2°.

markScheme.criterion: Uses n_ext sin θ_max = √(n_core² − n_clad²) to obtain θ_max = 31.2° (C).

items.stem: In a short-reach datacenter patch cord, a short optical pulse enters a 360 m step-index fiber (core index 1.52, cladding index 1.46, n_ext = 1.00, sample launch angle 17.5°). With c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, calculate the modal time delay Δt = t_max − t_axial at the output end.
items.workedSolution: Axial transit time t_min = n_core L / c = (1.52 × 360) / (3.00 × 10⁸) = 1.82 × 10⁻⁶ s. At the critical angle sin θ_c = n_clad / n_core, t_max = t_min / sin θ_c = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 1.90 × 10⁻⁶ s. Modal delay Δt = t_max − t_min = 7.50 × 10⁻⁸ s.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δt = (n_core L / c)(n_core / n_clad − 1) = 7.50 × 10⁻⁸ s (C).

items.stem: Within a metrology profile-projector optical train, an upright scale mark of height 0.008 m sits 0.192 m from a thin convex lens of focal length 0.24 m. Applying 1/f = 1/u + 1/v in the real-is-positive convention, determine the signed image position v.
items.workedSolution: Because u = 0.192 m < f = 0.24 m, 1/v = 1/0.24 − 1/0.192 = -1.042 m⁻¹, giving a signed virtual image distance v = -0.960 m.

markScheme.criterion: Computes 1/v = 1/0.24 − 1/0.192 to obtain signed v = -0.960 m (D).

items.stem: A concave diverging lens with focal length f = −0.25 m in a wide-angle security peephole assembly forms an image of an object of height 0.05 m placed at object distance u = 0.375 m. Using 1/f = 1/u + 1/v, calculate the signed image distance v.
items.workedSolution: For a diverging lens, f = −0.25 m. Using 1/f = 1/u + 1/v gives 1/v = −1/0.25 − 1/0.375 = -6.667 m⁻¹, so v = -0.150 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses negative f = −0.25 m in 1/v = 1/f − 1/u to obtain v = -0.150 m (C).

items.stem: In a structural vibration-isolation test sled on linear bearings, a 0.2 kg mass hangs from a vertical spring of constant 64 N m⁻¹ and executes vertical SHM of amplitude 0.042 m (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Calculate the static equilibrium extension Δx_eq from the spring's unstretched length.
items.workedSolution: At static equilibrium, upward spring tension balances weight: k Δx_eq = mg ⇒ Δx_eq = (0.2 × 9.81) / 64 = 0.0307 m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Adds the oscillation amplitude x₀ to mg / k, finding maximum total stretch rather than static equilibrium extension.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Divides mass m directly by spring constant k without multiplying by gravitational field strength g.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Hooke's law as k / (mg) instead of mg / k.

items.stem: A vibrating element in a diesel injector needle-valve harmonic test rig executes simple harmonic motion of frequency 8 Hz and amplitude 0.1 m (sampled at x = 0.035 m). What is the magnitude a_max of its maximum acceleration?
items.workedSolution: With ω = 2π(8) = 50.27 rad s⁻¹, maximum acceleration magnitude a_max = ω² x₀ = 253 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ω = 2πf and obtains 253 m s⁻² (D).

items.stem: In a tall-building tuned mass damper block, an oscillating body of mass 1.2 kg executes simple harmonic motion with angular frequency ω = 10 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude x₀ = 0.1 m. What is its kinetic energy E_k when its displacement from equilibrium is x = 0.05 m?
items.workedSolution: Using E_k = ½mω²(x₀² − x²) gives E_k = 0.5 × 1.2 × 10² × (0.1² − 0.05²) = 0.450 J.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes the total mechanical energy ½mω²x₀² instead of subtracting potential energy at x.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Interpolates energy linearly as E_tot(1 − x / x₀) instead of quadratically as E_tot(1 − x² / x₀²).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the potential energy ½mω²x² at x rather than the kinetic energy ½mω²(x₀² − x²).

items.stem: A 80 m step-index optical fiber used in a subterranean pipeline temperature-sensing cable has core refractive index 1.49 and cladding refractive index 1.39. A laser ray in air (n_ext = 1.00) enters the center of the flat end-face at θ_in = 14° to the fiber axis. What angle of incidence θ_w does the refracted ray make with the normal to the core–cladding wall?
items.workedSolution: At the entry face, 1 sin 14° = 1.49 sin θ_axis ⇒ θ_axis = 9.34°. Since the core wall is parallel to the axis, its normal is perpendicular to the axis, giving θ_w = 90° − θ_axis = 80.7°.

markScheme.criterion: Uses negative f = −0.4 m in 1/v = 1/f − 1/u to obtain v = -0.257 m (C).

items.stem: A test rig using an earthquake shake-table Tuned spring sled has mass 0.16 kg, horizontal spring constant 14 N m⁻¹, and oscillation amplitude 0.045 m. What is the natural frequency f of the oscillation?
items.workedSolution: Natural frequency f = (1 / 2π)√(k / m) = (1 / 2π)√(14 / 0.16) = 1.49 Hz.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes the period T = 2π√(m / k) instead of frequency f = 1 / T.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Reports angular frequency ω = √(k / m) in rad s⁻¹ without dividing by 2π.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Swaps k/m and m/k, computing (1 / 2π)√(m / k) instead of (1 / 2π)√(k / m).

items.stem: In a museum horology restoration pendulum rig, a simple pendulum of length 0.4 m and bob mass 0.4 kg swings with small arc amplitude 0.112 m where g = 9.81 m s⁻². Calculate its speed at the equilibrium position.
items.workedSolution: Angular frequency ω = √(g / L) = √(9.81 / 0.4), so maximum speed v_max = ω x₀ = 0.555 m s⁻¹.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes ω² x₀ = (g / L) x₀ (maximum acceleration) instead of ω x₀ = √(g / L) x₀.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Treats the horizontal arc amplitude x₀ as a vertical free-fall drop height h in √(2gh).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts g / L inside √(g / L) when computing ω x₀.

items.stem: Engineers monitoring a studio loudspeaker voice-coil cone measure simple harmonic motion of amplitude 0.06 m and angular frequency 24 rad s⁻¹. Determine the speed |v| = ω√(x₀² − x²) at displacement x = 0.0216 m.
items.workedSolution: Using v = ω√(x₀² − x²) gives v = 24 × √(0.06² − 0.0216²) = 1.34 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into v = ω√(x₀² − x²) to obtain 1.34 m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: A refractometer cell in a subsea ROV camera viewport test immerses a polished dielectric slab in liquid ethanol (n₂ = 1.36), recording a critical angle of 34.2° relative to the boundary normal. Determine the refractive index n₁ of the dielectric slab.
items.workedSolution: At the critical angle, n₁ sin θ_c = n₂ sin 90° = n₂, so n₁ = 1.36 / sin 34.2° = 2.42.

markScheme.criterion: Computes n₁ = n₂ / sin θ_c = 1.36 / sin 34.2° = 2.42 (B).

items.stem: A 200 m step-index waveguide in a transoceanic telecommunications link is fabricated with a core of refractive index 1.54 surrounded by cladding of refractive index 1.45, with light launched from air (n_ext = 1.00) at 15.9° to the axis. What is the critical angle θ_c at the core–cladding interface?
items.workedSolution: At the core–cladding boundary, sin θ_c = n_clad / n_core = 1.45 / 1.54 = 0.9416, giving θ_c = 70.3°.

items.stem: A monochromatic ray in water of refractive index 1.33 is coupled at 9.9° to the axis into a straight 300 m optical fiber (n_core = 1.5, n_clad = 1.44) during a borehole geophysical telemetry line. Calculate the total ray path length inside the 300 m fiber.
items.workedSolution: Inside the core, sin θ_axis = (1.33 sin 9.9°) / 1.5 ⇒ θ_axis = 8.77°. The total zig-zag geometric path length is L_ray = L / cos θ_axis = 300 / cos 8.769° = 304 m.

markScheme.criterion: Finds θ_axis = 8.77° and computes L / cos θ_axis = 304 m (B).

items.stem: In a botanical loupe magnifier bench, a thin converging lens of focal length 0.15 m is used as a simple magnifier so that an object of height 0.008 m forms an upright virtual image 0.0808 m in front of the lens (v = −0.0808 m in the real-is-positive convention). At what object distance u in front of the lens is the object held?
items.workedSolution: For a virtual image in the real-is-positive convention, v = -0.0808 m. Thus 1/u = 1/f − 1/v = 1/0.15 − (1/-0.08077) = 19.05 m⁻¹, giving u = 0.0525 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes negative v = -0.0808 m into 1/u = 1/f − 1/v to obtain u = 0.0525 m (C).

options.distractorRationale: Forgets v < 0 for a virtual image and substitutes v = +|v| into 1/u = 1/f − 1/v instead of v = −|v|.

options.distractorRationale: Computes 1/u in m⁻¹ without taking the reciprocal to find u in metres.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts focal length directly from |v| instead of adding reciprocals 1/f + 1/|v|.

items.stem: During stiffness testing on a frictionless air-track glider coupled to a calibrated coil spring, a 1.5 kg mass oscillates horizontally with amplitude 0.045 m and a measured period of 2.06 s. What is the spring constant k?
items.workedSolution: Rearranging T = 2π√(m / k) gives k = 4π²m / T² = 4π²(1.5) / (2.06)² = 14.0 N m⁻¹.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts m / T² when rearranging the period equation.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Fails to square 2π / T when rearranging T = 2π√(m / k), computing 2πm / T instead of 4π²m / T².

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 4π² and computes m / T².

items.stem: Engineers testing an inertial seismometer calibration trolley hang a 0.75 kg mass from a vertical coil spring (k = 100 N m⁻¹) and excite vertical oscillations of amplitude 0.032 m in a gravitational field g = 9.81 m s⁻². Determine the period T of oscillation.
items.workedSolution: Gravity shifts the equilibrium position without altering effective stiffness k, so T = 2π√(m / k) = 2π√(0.75 / 100) = 0.544 s.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Incorrectly adds weight mg to spring stiffness k, assuming gravity changes the vertical mass-spring period.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes the oscillation amplitude x₀ into a pendulum-style formula 2π√(x₀ / g) instead of 2π√(m / k).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Swaps m/k and k/m inside the square root.

items.stem: Engineers timing a physics laboratory light-gate timing pendulum use a 0.5 kg bob on a 1.9 m light cord swinging with arc amplitude 0.418 m (g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Calculate the period T.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the half-period π√(L / g) instead of the full period 2π√(L / g).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Inverts L / g inside the square root.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the square root on L / g.

items.stem: During calibration of a precision optical-chopper resonant blade vibrating at f = 2.5 Hz and amplitude 0.1 m, a laser sensor records an instantaneous displacement x = 0.035 m. Determine the signed SHM acceleration a at that instant.
items.workedSolution: Angular frequency ω = 2πf = 2π(2.5) = 15.71 rad s⁻¹. By the defining SHM equation, a = −ω²x = −(15.71)²(0.035) = -8.64 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ω = 2πf and obtains -8.64 m s⁻² (A).

options.distractorRationale: Evaluates −ωx instead of −ω²x, forgetting to square the angular frequency.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes cyclic frequency f directly for angular frequency ω, computing −f²x instead of −(2πf)²x.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the restoring minus sign in a = −ω²x, giving acceleration in the same sign as displacement instead of toward equilibrium.

items.stem: In a micro-electro-mechanical resonant beam, a 0.8 kg mass undergoes SHM with ω = 10 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude 0.06 m (with a sensor at x = 0.048 m). Calculate the frequency f_E at which the kinetic energy completes full cycles.
items.workedSolution: Mechanical frequency f = ω / (2π) = 10 / (2π) = 1.592 Hz. Because kinetic energy reaches a maximum twice per mechanical period, f_E = 2f = ω / π = 3.18 Hz.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates 2ω in rad s⁻¹ without dividing by 2π to convert to hertz.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Gives the mechanical displacement frequency f = ω / (2π) instead of recognizing that E_k ∝ cos²(ωt) oscillates at 2f.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Halves the mechanical frequency instead of doubling it.

items.stem: In a high-voltage substation optical isolator link, a short optical pulse enters a 750 m step-index fiber (core index 1.6, cladding index 1.5, n_ext = 1.00, sample launch angle 20.3°). With c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, calculate the modal time delay Δt = t_max − t_axial at the output end.
items.workedSolution: Axial transit time t_min = n_core L / c = (1.6 × 750) / (3.00 × 10⁸) = 4.00 × 10⁻⁶ s. At the critical angle sin θ_c = n_clad / n_core, t_max = t_min / sin θ_c = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 4.27 × 10⁻⁶ s. Modal delay Δt = t_max − t_min = 2.67 × 10⁻⁷ s.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δt = (n_core L / c)(n_core / n_clad − 1) = 2.67 × 10⁻⁷ s (C).

items.stem: In a museum conservation inspection magnifier, a small specimen of height 0.022 m is held 0.07 m in front of a thin converging magnifier lens of focal length 0.2 m. Using the real-is-positive sign convention (1/f = 1/u + 1/v), what is the signed image distance v?
items.workedSolution: Because u = 0.07 m < f = 0.2 m, 1/v = 1/0.2 − 1/0.07 = -9.286 m⁻¹, giving a signed virtual image distance v = -0.108 m.

markScheme.criterion: Computes 1/v = 1/0.2 − 1/0.07 to obtain signed v = -0.108 m (B).

items.stem: During optical testing on a clinical optometry phoropter test cell, a 0.036 m illuminated target sits 1.2 m from a thin diverging lens of focal length −0.4 m. Determine the signed image position v under the real-is-positive sign convention.
items.workedSolution: For a diverging lens, f = −0.4 m. Using 1/f = 1/u + 1/v gives 1/v = −1/0.4 − 1/1.2 = -3.333 m⁻¹, so v = -0.300 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses negative f = −0.4 m in 1/v = 1/f − 1/u to obtain v = -0.300 m (B).

items.stem: A vertical helical spring of stiffness 50 N m⁻¹ in a robotics compliant-actuator test carriage suspends a load of mass 1.2 kg that subsequently oscillates vertically with amplitude 0.024 m. Taking g = 9.8 m s⁻², what was the static extension Δx_eq of the spring at equilibrium before oscillation started?
items.workedSolution: At static equilibrium, upward spring tension balances weight: k Δx_eq = mg ⇒ Δx_eq = (1.2 × 9.8) / 50 = 0.235 m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Hooke's law as k / (mg) instead of mg / k.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Adds the oscillation amplitude x₀ to mg / k, finding maximum total stretch rather than static equilibrium extension.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Divides mass m directly by spring constant k without multiplying by gravitational field strength g.

items.stem: In a quartz crystal tuning-fork tine, a component executes simple harmonic motion at frequency f = 12 Hz with amplitude x₀ = 0.08 m, as represented on the acceleration–displacement graph. Taking displacement to the right as positive, what is its signed acceleration a when x = 0.028 m?
items.workedSolution: Angular frequency ω = 2πf = 2π(12) = 75.40 rad s⁻¹. By the defining SHM equation, a = −ω²x = −(75.40)²(0.028) = -159 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ω = 2πf and obtains -159 m s⁻² (D).

options.distractorRationale: Omits the restoring minus sign in a = −ω²x, giving acceleration in the same sign as displacement instead of toward equilibrium.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates −ωx instead of −ω²x, forgetting to square the angular frequency.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes cyclic frequency f directly for angular frequency ω, computing −f²x instead of −(2πf)²x.

items.stem: A harmonic oscillator in a vibrometer calibration shaker table moves with amplitude x₀ = 0.05 m and angular frequency ω = 40 rad s⁻¹. Calculate its speed when passing through displacement x = 0.014 m.
items.workedSolution: Using v = ω√(x₀² − x²) gives v = 40 × √(0.05² − 0.014²) = 1.92 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into v = ω√(x₀² − x²) to obtain 1.92 m s⁻¹ (C).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the maximum speed ωx₀ at equilibrium (x = 0) instead of the speed at x.

items.stem: A collimated ray inside dense flint glass (n₁ = 1.65, vacuum light speed c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) strikes a flat interface with dry air (n₂ = 1) at 50° to the normal during a photovoltaic encapsulant test coupon. Through what angle is the ray deviated from its original forward path at this boundary?
items.workedSolution: Since sin θ_c = 1 / 1.65 gives θ_c = 37.3° and θ₁ = 50° > θ_c, the beam undergoes total internal reflection with θ_r = 50°. The angular deviation from the original forward direction is δ = 180° − 2(50°) = 80.0°.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies TIR (θ₁ > θ_c = 37.3°) and computes δ = 180° − 2θ₁ = 80.0° (B).

options.distractorRationale: Calculates the angle 2θ₁ between the reversed incident ray and the reflected ray rather than the forward deviation 180° − 2θ₁.

options.label: C

options.label: D

items.stem: An over-angled ray in water (n_ext = 1.33) is launched at 33.5° to the central axis into a 350 m step-index waveguide (n_core = 1.52, n_clad = 1.46) during a structural-health bridge sensor lead. At what angle to the cylindrical wall normal does the leaked ray refract into the cladding?
items.workedSolution: At entry, sin θ_axis = (1.33 sin 33.5°) / 1.52 ⇒ θ_axis = 28.9°. The angle to the wall normal is θ_w = 90° − θ_axis = 61.1° (< θ_c = 73.8°). Refracting into the cladding: sin θ_clad = (1.52 sin θ_w) / 1.46, giving θ_clad = 65.7°.

markScheme.criterion: Finds θ_w = 61.1° and refracts into cladding to obtain 65.7° (B).

items.stem: In a railway trackside acoustic-sensing fiber, a short optical pulse enters a 900 m step-index fiber (core index 1.58, cladding index 1.49, n_ext = 1.00, sample launch angle 22.2°). With c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, calculate the modal time delay Δt = t_max − t_axial at the output end.
items.workedSolution: Axial transit time t_min = n_core L / c = (1.58 × 900) / (3.00 × 10⁸) = 4.74 × 10⁻⁶ s. At the critical angle sin θ_c = n_clad / n_core, t_max = t_min / sin θ_c = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 5.03 × 10⁻⁶ s. Modal delay Δt = t_max − t_min = 2.86 × 10⁻⁷ s.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δt = (n_core L / c)(n_core / n_clad − 1) = 2.86 × 10⁻⁷ s (B).

options.distractorRationale: Calculates the total transit time t_max of the slowest critical-angle ray without subtracting the axial transit time t_axial.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies t_axial by (1 − n_clad / n_core) instead of (n_core / n_clad − 1), inverting sin θ_c.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses the vacuum speed c instead of the core wave speed c / n_core when computing transit times.

items.stem: A concave diverging lens with focal length f = −0.12 m in a pulsed-laser divergence compensator forms an image of an object of height 0.036 m placed at object distance u = 0.072 m. Using 1/f = 1/u + 1/v, calculate the signed image distance v.
items.workedSolution: For a diverging lens, f = −0.12 m. Using 1/f = 1/u + 1/v gives 1/v = −1/0.12 − 1/0.072 = -22.22 m⁻¹, so v = -0.0450 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses negative f = −0.12 m in 1/v = 1/f − 1/u to obtain v = -0.0450 m (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Stops at 1/v = −1/|f| − 1/u in m⁻¹ without taking the reciprocal to find v in metres.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Forgets that a diverging lens has negative focal length f < 0, substituting +|f| into 1/v = 1/f − 1/u.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes the correct magnitude |v| but omits the negative sign required for a virtual image in the real-is-positive convention.

items.stem: In a calibration run of a precision marine-chronometer balance-mass rig, a 0.64 kg carriage oscillates horizontally with amplitude 0.045 m on a spring of stiffness 160 N m⁻¹. Determine the frequency f in hertz.
items.workedSolution: Natural frequency f = (1 / 2π)√(k / m) = (1 / 2π)√(160 / 0.64) = 2.52 Hz.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Reports angular frequency ω = √(k / m) in rad s⁻¹ without dividing by 2π.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes the period T = 2π√(m / k) instead of frequency f = 1 / T.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Swaps k/m and m/k, computing (1 / 2π)√(m / k) instead of (1 / 2π)√(k / m).

items.stem: A 0.5 kg pendulum bob suspended from a 2.4 m wire in a mine-shaft gravity-anomaly survey pendulum oscillates in SHM with arc amplitude 0.6 m (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). What is the maximum speed v_max of the bob?
items.workedSolution: Angular frequency ω = √(g / L) = √(9.81 / 2.4), so maximum speed v_max = ω x₀ = 1.21 m s⁻¹.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Treats the horizontal arc amplitude x₀ as a vertical free-fall drop height h in √(2gh).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes ω² x₀ = (g / L) x₀ (maximum acceleration) instead of ω x₀ = √(g / L) x₀.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts g / L inside √(g / L) when computing ω x₀.

items.stem: A harmonic oscillator in a tall-building tuned mass damper block moves with amplitude x₀ = 0.15 m and angular frequency ω = 40 rad s⁻¹. Calculate its speed when passing through displacement x = 0.054 m.
items.workedSolution: Using v = ω√(x₀² − x²) gives v = 40 × √(0.15² − 0.054²) = 5.60 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into v = ω√(x₀² − x²) to obtain 5.60 m s⁻¹ (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses ωx instead of ω√(x₀² − x²), mistakenly assuming speed is directly proportional to displacement.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates ω(x₀ − x) linearly instead of taking √(x₀² − x²).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the maximum speed ωx₀ at equilibrium (x = 0) instead of the speed at x.

items.stem: In a dynamic mechanical thermal-analyzer probe, a 1.2 kg oscillator moves harmonically at ω = 12 rad s⁻¹ with amplitude x₀ = 0.12 m (sampled at 0.096 m). At what positive displacement x from equilibrium is its kinetic energy equal to its potential energy (E_k = E_p)?
items.workedSolution: Setting E_p = ½E_tot gives ½mω²x² = ½(½mω²x₀²), so x² = x₀² / 2 and x = x₀ / √2 = 0.12 / √2 = 0.0849 m.

markScheme.criterion: Solves x² = x₀² / 2 to obtain x = x₀ / √2 = 0.0849 m (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Squares the ½ factor to obtain x₀ / 4 instead of taking the square root x₀ / √2.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Assumes E_k = E_p occurs at half the amplitude (x₀ / 2, where E_p = ¼E_tot) instead of x₀ / √2.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes (√3 / 2)x₀ (where E_p = ¾E_tot) instead of x₀ / √2.

items.stem: On a gemstone goniometer calibration rig, the critical angle for total internal reflection of monochromatic light passing from a transparent crystal into dry air (n₂ = 1) is measured to be 34.4° to the normal. What is the refractive index n₁ of the crystal?
items.workedSolution: At the critical angle, n₁ sin θ_c = n₂ sin 90° = n₂, so n₁ = 1 / sin 34.4° = 1.77.

markScheme.criterion: Computes n₁ = n₂ / sin θ_c = 1 / sin 34.4° = 1.77 (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies n₂ by sin θ_c instead of dividing n₂ by sin θ_c.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Measures the critical angle relative to the boundary surface, dividing n₂ by cos θ_c instead of sin θ_c.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses tan θ_c instead of sin θ_c when inverting the critical-angle relation.

items.stem: In a cryogenic laboratory optical feedthrough, light from air (n_ext = 1.00, illustrated at 14.4°) propagates along a 750 m step-index fiber with n_core = 1.62 and n_clad = 1.51. Taking c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, what is the transit time t_max of the slowest guided ray that meets the core–cladding wall at the critical angle?
items.workedSolution: Wave speed in the core is v = c / n_core, and the critical-angle ray travels path length L / sin θ_c = L (n_core / n_clad). Therefore t_max = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 4.35 × 10⁻⁶ s.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates t_max = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 4.35 × 10⁻⁶ s (D).

items.stem: An observer using a retinal fundus imaging objective rig adjusts the position of a 0.022 m scale mark in front of a thin convex lens of focal length 0.15 m until its virtual image lies at the near point 0.450 m on the object side of the lens (v = −0.450 m). Calculate the object distance u.
items.workedSolution: For a virtual image in the real-is-positive convention, v = -0.450 m. Thus 1/u = 1/f − 1/v = 1/0.15 − (1/-0.4500) = 8.889 m⁻¹, giving u = 0.113 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes negative v = -0.450 m into 1/u = 1/f − 1/v to obtain u = 0.113 m (C).

items.stem: During stiffness testing on a structural vibration-isolation test sled on linear bearings, a 1.5 kg mass oscillates horizontally with amplitude 0.035 m and a measured period of 1.36 s. What is the spring constant k?
items.workedSolution: Rearranging T = 2π√(m / k) gives k = 4π²m / T² = 4π²(1.5) / (1.36)² = 32.0 N m⁻¹.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 4π² and computes m / T².

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Fails to square 2π / T when rearranging T = 2π√(m / k), computing 2πm / T instead of 4π²m / T².

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts m / T² when rearranging the period equation.

items.stem: Engineers testing a railway bogie secondary-suspension scale model hang a 0.75 kg mass from a vertical coil spring (k = 25 N m⁻¹) and excite vertical oscillations of amplitude 0.042 m in a gravitational field g = 9.8 m s⁻². Determine the period T of oscillation.
items.workedSolution: Gravity shifts the equilibrium position without altering effective stiffness k, so T = 2π√(m / k) = 2π√(0.75 / 25) = 1.09 s.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Swaps m/k and k/m inside the square root.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Incorrectly adds weight mg to spring stiffness k, assuming gravity changes the vertical mass-spring period.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes the oscillation amplitude x₀ into a pendulum-style formula 2π√(x₀ / g) instead of 2π√(m / k).

items.stem: A metrology pendulum in an astronomical observatory sidereal regulator pendulum has suspension length 0.85 m, bob mass 0.5 kg, and arc amplitude 0.187 m. Taking g = 9.81 m s⁻², what is its oscillation period T?

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Omits the square root on L / g.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the half-period π√(L / g) instead of the full period 2π√(L / g).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts L / g inside the square root.

items.stem: In a studio loudspeaker voice-coil cone, a component executes simple harmonic motion at frequency f = 2.5 Hz with amplitude x₀ = 0.03 m, as represented on the acceleration–displacement graph. Taking displacement to the right as positive, what is its signed acceleration a when x = -0.0135 m?
items.workedSolution: Angular frequency ω = 2πf = 2π(2.5) = 15.71 rad s⁻¹. By the defining SHM equation, a = −ω²x = −(15.71)²(-0.0135) = 3.33 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ω = 2πf and obtains 3.33 m s⁻² (A).

items.stem: In a magnetic-levitation harmonic test puck, a 0.4 kg mass undergoes SHM with ω = 20 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude 0.12 m (with a sensor at x = 0.048 m). Calculate the frequency f_E at which the kinetic energy completes full cycles.
items.workedSolution: Mechanical frequency f = ω / (2π) = 20 / (2π) = 3.183 Hz. Because kinetic energy reaches a maximum twice per mechanical period, f_E = 2f = ω / π = 6.37 Hz.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates 2ω in rad s⁻¹ without dividing by 2π to convert to hertz.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Gives the mechanical displacement frequency f = ω / (2π) instead of recognizing that E_k ∝ cos²(ωt) oscillates at 2f.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Halves the mechanical frequency instead of doubling it.

items.stem: A 350 m step-index optical fiber used in a transoceanic telecommunications link has core refractive index 1.55 and cladding refractive index 1.47. A laser ray in air (n_ext = 1.00) enters the center of the flat end-face at θ_in = 10.3° to the fiber axis. What angle of incidence θ_w does the refracted ray make with the normal to the core–cladding wall?
items.workedSolution: At the entry face, 1 sin 10.3° = 1.55 sin θ_axis ⇒ θ_axis = 6.62°. Since the core wall is parallel to the axis, its normal is perpendicular to the axis, giving θ_w = 90° − θ_axis = 83.4°.

items.stem: A concave diverging lens with focal length f = −0.15 m in a myopia-corrective ophthalmic spectacle trial forms an image of an object of height 0.02 m placed at object distance u = 0.12 m. Using 1/f = 1/u + 1/v, calculate the signed image distance v.
items.workedSolution: For a diverging lens, f = −0.15 m. Using 1/f = 1/u + 1/v gives 1/v = −1/0.15 − 1/0.12 = -15.00 m⁻¹, so v = -0.0667 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses negative f = −0.15 m in 1/v = 1/f − 1/u to obtain v = -0.0667 m (B).

items.stem: In an inertial seismometer calibration trolley, a 0.4 kg mass hangs from a vertical spring of constant 40 N m⁻¹ and executes vertical SHM of amplitude 0.032 m (take g = 9.8 m s⁻²). Calculate the static equilibrium extension Δx_eq from the spring's unstretched length.
items.workedSolution: At static equilibrium, upward spring tension balances weight: k Δx_eq = mg ⇒ Δx_eq = (0.4 × 9.8) / 40 = 0.0980 m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Divides mass m directly by spring constant k without multiplying by gravitational field strength g.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Adds the oscillation amplitude x₀ to mg / k, finding maximum total stretch rather than static equilibrium extension.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Hooke's law as k / (mg) instead of mg / k.

items.stem: During calibration of an ultrasonic surgical transducer tip vibrating at f = 5 Hz and amplitude 0.05 m, a laser sensor records an instantaneous displacement x = 0.03 m. Determine the signed SHM acceleration a at that instant.
items.workedSolution: Angular frequency ω = 2πf = 2π(5) = 31.42 rad s⁻¹. By the defining SHM equation, a = −ω²x = −(31.42)²(0.03) = -29.6 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ω = 2πf and obtains -29.6 m s⁻² (D).

items.stem: The velocity–displacement phase portrait shown represents a piezoelectric laser-mirror dithering stage oscillating with ω = 16 rad s⁻¹ and x₀ = 0.08 m. Find the oscillator's speed at x = 0.0288 m.
items.workedSolution: Using v = ω√(x₀² − x²) gives v = 16 × √(0.08² − 0.0288²) = 1.19 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into v = ω√(x₀² − x²) to obtain 1.19 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: Engineers designing a beam-turning prism on a microfluidic refractive-index sensor send a ray in polycarbonate polymer (n₁ = 1.58, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) onto distilled water (n₂ = 1.33) at 74° to the normal. What is the angular deflection δ between the incident direction and the emerging reflected ray?
items.workedSolution: Since sin θ_c = 1.33 / 1.58 gives θ_c = 57.3° and θ₁ = 74° > θ_c, the beam undergoes total internal reflection with θ_r = 74°. The angular deviation from the original forward direction is δ = 180° − 2(74°) = 32.0°.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies TIR (θ₁ > θ_c = 57.3°) and computes δ = 180° − 2θ₁ = 32.0° (A).

items.stem: A 350 m step-index waveguide in a flexible medical gastroscope bundle is fabricated with a core of refractive index 1.52 surrounded by cladding of refractive index 1.46, with light launched from air (n_ext = 1.00) at 10.8° to the axis. What is the critical angle θ_c at the core–cladding interface?
items.workedSolution: At the core–cladding boundary, sin θ_c = n_clad / n_core = 1.46 / 1.52 = 0.9605, giving θ_c = 73.8°.

items.stem: In a laboratory autocollimator test rail, a specimen of height 0.018 m is placed 0.0816 m in front of a convex magnifying lens of focal length 0.12 m. Calculate the upright virtual image height h_i.
items.workedSolution: From 1/v = 1/0.12 − 1/0.0816, v = -0.255 m. Linear magnification m = −v / u = 3.125, so upright image height h_i = m h_o = 0.0563 m.

options.distractorRationale: Inverts linear magnification as u / |v| instead of |v| / u.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses the diverging-lens formula f / (f + u) for magnification, obtaining a diminished height smaller than h_o.

options.label: C

items.stem: In a calibration run of a silicon MEMS accelerometer proof-mass flexure test model, a 0.25 kg carriage oscillates horizontally with amplitude 0.11 m on a spring of stiffness 72 N m⁻¹. Determine the frequency f in hertz.
items.workedSolution: Natural frequency f = (1 / 2π)√(k / m) = (1 / 2π)√(72 / 0.25) = 2.70 Hz.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Swaps k/m and m/k, computing (1 / 2π)√(m / k) instead of (1 / 2π)√(k / m).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes the period T = 2π√(m / k) instead of frequency f = 1 / T.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Reports angular frequency ω = √(k / m) in rad s⁻¹ without dividing by 2π.

items.stem: A vertical helical spring of stiffness 40 N m⁻¹ in a robotics compliant-actuator test carriage suspends a load of mass 0.6 kg that subsequently oscillates vertically with amplitude 0.042 m. Taking g = 9.81 m s⁻², what was the static extension Δx_eq of the spring at equilibrium before oscillation started?
items.workedSolution: At static equilibrium, upward spring tension balances weight: k Δx_eq = mg ⇒ Δx_eq = (0.6 × 9.81) / 40 = 0.147 m.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Divides mass m directly by spring constant k without multiplying by gravitational field strength g.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Adds the oscillation amplitude x₀ to mg / k, finding maximum total stretch rather than static equilibrium extension.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Hooke's law as k / (mg) instead of mg / k.

items.stem: A 0.6 kg pendulum bob suspended from a 0.85 m wire in an evacuated bell-jar precision timing pendulum oscillates in SHM with arc amplitude 0.187 m (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). What is the maximum speed v_max of the bob?
items.workedSolution: Angular frequency ω = √(g / L) = √(9.81 / 0.85), so maximum speed v_max = ω x₀ = 0.635 m s⁻¹.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes ω² x₀ = (g / L) x₀ (maximum acceleration) instead of ω x₀ = √(g / L) x₀.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Treats the horizontal arc amplitude x₀ as a vertical free-fall drop height h in √(2gh).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts g / L inside √(g / L) when computing ω x₀.

items.stem: In a vibrometer calibration shaker table, a stage oscillates in simple harmonic motion with angular frequency ω = 24 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude x₀ = 0.12 m, tracing the velocity–displacement ellipse shown. What is the speed v of the stage when its displacement from equilibrium is x = 0.072 m?
items.workedSolution: Using v = ω√(x₀² − x²) gives v = 24 × √(0.12² − 0.072²) = 2.30 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into v = ω√(x₀² − x²) to obtain 2.30 m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: For a marine wave-tank oscillating piston paddle executing undamped SHM of mass 0.8 kg, angular frequency 20 rad s⁻¹, and amplitude 0.04 m (reference mark at 0.02 m), determine the positive displacement at which E_k = E_p.
items.workedSolution: Setting E_p = ½E_tot gives ½mω²x² = ½(½mω²x₀²), so x² = x₀² / 2 and x = x₀ / √2 = 0.04 / √2 = 0.0283 m.

markScheme.criterion: Solves x² = x₀² / 2 to obtain x = x₀ / √2 = 0.0283 m (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes (√3 / 2)x₀ (where E_p = ¾E_tot) instead of x₀ / √2.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Assumes E_k = E_p occurs at half the amplitude (x₀ / 2, where E_p = ¼E_tot) instead of x₀ / √2.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Squares the ½ factor to obtain x₀ / 4 instead of taking the square root x₀ / √2.

items.stem: On a photovoltaic encapsulant test coupon, the critical angle for total internal reflection of monochromatic light passing from a transparent crystal into fused-silica glass (n₂ = 1.46) is measured to be 37.1° to the normal. What is the refractive index n₁ of the crystal?
items.workedSolution: At the critical angle, n₁ sin θ_c = n₂ sin 90° = n₂, so n₁ = 1.46 / sin 37.1° = 2.42.

markScheme.criterion: Computes n₁ = n₂ / sin θ_c = 1.46 / sin 37.1° = 2.42 (D).

items.stem: A monochromatic ray in water of refractive index 1.33 is coupled at 14.7° to the axis into a straight 300 m optical fiber (n_core = 1.58, n_clad = 1.49) during a tethered deep-sea ROV umbilical waveguide. Calculate the total ray path length inside the 300 m fiber.
items.workedSolution: Inside the core, sin θ_axis = (1.33 sin 14.7°) / 1.58 ⇒ θ_axis = 12.3°. The total zig-zag geometric path length is L_ray = L / cos θ_axis = 300 / cos 12.33° = 307 m.

markScheme.criterion: Finds θ_axis = 12.3° and computes L / cos θ_axis = 307 m (B).

items.stem: In a railway trackside acoustic-sensing fiber, light from air (n_ext = 1.00, illustrated at 18.7°) propagates along a 150 m step-index fiber with n_core = 1.54 and n_clad = 1.45. Taking c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, what is the transit time t_max of the slowest guided ray that meets the core–cladding wall at the critical angle?
items.workedSolution: Wave speed in the core is v = c / n_core, and the critical-angle ray travels path length L / sin θ_c = L (n_core / n_clad). Therefore t_max = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 8.18 × 10⁻⁷ s.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates t_max = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 8.18 × 10⁻⁷ s (C).

items.stem: An observer using a metrology profile-projector optical train adjusts the position of a 0.015 m scale mark in front of a thin convex lens of focal length 0.25 m until its virtual image lies at the near point 0.531 m on the object side of the lens (v = −0.531 m). Calculate the object distance u.
items.workedSolution: For a virtual image in the real-is-positive convention, v = -0.531 m. Thus 1/u = 1/f − 1/v = 1/0.25 − (1/-0.5313) = 5.882 m⁻¹, giving u = 0.170 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes negative v = -0.531 m into 1/u = 1/f − 1/v to obtain u = 0.170 m (D).

items.stem: In a wide-angle security peephole assembly, an object of height 0.036 m is positioned 0.27 m from a concave lens of focal length −0.15 m. Calculate the signed linear magnification m = h_i / h_o = −v / u.
items.workedSolution: With f = −0.15 m, 1/v = −1/0.15 − 1/0.27 gives v = -0.0964 m. Therefore m = −v / u = −(-0.09643) / 0.27 = 0.357 (upright and diminished).

markScheme.criterion: Finds v = -0.0964 m and m = −v / u = 0.357 (B).

items.stem: Engineers testing a university mechanics oscillation sled hang a 0.2 kg mass from a vertical coil spring (k = 32 N m⁻¹) and excite vertical oscillations of amplitude 0.032 m in a gravitational field g = 9.8 m s⁻². Determine the period T of oscillation.
items.workedSolution: Gravity shifts the equilibrium position without altering effective stiffness k, so T = 2π√(m / k) = 2π√(0.2 / 32) = 0.497 s.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes the oscillation amplitude x₀ into a pendulum-style formula 2π√(x₀ / g) instead of 2π√(m / k).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Incorrectly adds weight mg to spring stiffness k, assuming gravity changes the vertical mass-spring period.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Swaps m/k and k/m inside the square root.

items.stem: During calibration of an atomic-force microscope cantilever tip vibrating at f = 1.5 Hz and amplitude 0.03 m, a laser sensor records an instantaneous displacement x = -0.0135 m. Determine the signed SHM acceleration a at that instant.
items.workedSolution: Angular frequency ω = 2πf = 2π(1.5) = 9.425 rad s⁻¹. By the defining SHM equation, a = −ω²x = −(9.425)²(-0.0135) = 1.20 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ω = 2πf and obtains 1.20 m s⁻² (D).

items.stem: In a dynamic mechanical thermal-analyzer probe, a 0.15 kg mass undergoes SHM with ω = 15 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude 0.12 m (with a sensor at x = 0.06 m). Calculate the frequency f_E at which the kinetic energy completes full cycles.
items.workedSolution: Mechanical frequency f = ω / (2π) = 15 / (2π) = 2.387 Hz. Because kinetic energy reaches a maximum twice per mechanical period, f_E = 2f = ω / π = 4.77 Hz.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates 2ω in rad s⁻¹ without dividing by 2π to convert to hertz.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Gives the mechanical displacement frequency f = ω / (2π) instead of recognizing that E_k ∝ cos²(ωt) oscillates at 2f.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Halves the mechanical frequency instead of doubling it.

items.stem: In an industrial laser-welding delivery cable, a straight step-index fiber of length 350 m has core index n_core = 1.48 and cladding index n_clad = 1.41. A test ray enters the flat end-face from air (n_ext = 1.00) at a steep angle θ_in = 42.7° to the fiber axis, exceeding the acceptance cone so light refracts into the cladding. What is the angle of refraction in the cladding measured from the core–cladding wall normal?
items.workedSolution: At entry, sin θ_axis = (1 sin 42.7°) / 1.48 ⇒ θ_axis = 27.3°. The angle to the wall normal is θ_w = 90° − θ_axis = 62.7° (< θ_c = 72.3°). Refracting into the cladding: sin θ_clad = (1.48 sin θ_w) / 1.41, giving θ_clad = 68.9°.

markScheme.criterion: Finds θ_w = 62.7° and refracts into cladding to obtain 68.9° (C).

items.stem: In an optical-bench virtual-image calibration rig, an upright test object of height 0.02 m stands 0.3 m in front of a thin diverging lens of focal length magnitude 0.2 m (f = −0.2 m in the real-is-positive convention). What is the signed image distance v?
items.workedSolution: For a diverging lens, f = −0.2 m. Using 1/f = 1/u + 1/v gives 1/v = −1/0.2 − 1/0.3 = -8.333 m⁻¹, so v = -0.120 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses negative f = −0.2 m in 1/v = 1/f − 1/u to obtain v = -0.120 m (B).

items.stem: An experimental setup consisting of a structural vibration-isolation test sled on linear bearings has oscillating mass 0.45 kg, spring stiffness 18 N m⁻¹, and horizontal amplitude 0.06 m. Calculate the oscillation period T.
items.workedSolution: For an ideal mass-spring oscillator, T = 2π√(m / k) = 2π√(0.45 / 18) = 0.993 s.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Swaps m/k and k/m inside the radical, computing 2π√(k / m) instead of 2π√(m / k).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the oscillation frequency f = 1 / T in Hz instead of the period T in seconds.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 2π and calculates √(m / k) = 1 / ω.

items.stem: A 0.5 kg brass bob on a 0.72 m suspension wire in a museum horology restoration pendulum rig oscillates with arc-length amplitude 0.18 m (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Calculate the maximum cord tension at the bottom of the swing.
items.workedSolution: With ω = √(g / L) = √(9.81 / 0.72), peak speed v_max = ω x₀ = 0.664 m s⁻¹. At the lowest point, T_cord = m(g + v_max² / L) = 5.21 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_max = ω x₀ and T_cord = mg + mv_max² / L = 5.21 N (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates only the net radial centripetal force mv_max² / L rather than the total cord tension.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts the centripetal force mv_max² / L from mg instead of adding it at the bottom of the arc.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Equates cord tension at the lowest point to static weight mg, ignoring the upward centripetal force mv_max² / L.

items.stem: Engineers monitoring a precision optical-chopper resonant blade measure simple harmonic motion of amplitude 0.1 m and angular frequency 20 rad s⁻¹. Determine the speed |v| = ω√(x₀² − x²) at displacement x = 0.028 m.
items.workedSolution: Using v = ω√(x₀² − x²) gives v = 20 × √(0.1² − 0.028²) = 1.92 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into v = ω√(x₀² − x²) to obtain 1.92 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: In a magnetic-levitation harmonic test puck, an oscillating body of mass 0.8 kg executes simple harmonic motion with angular frequency ω = 20 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude x₀ = 0.06 m. What is its kinetic energy E_k when its displacement from equilibrium is x = 0.048 m?
items.workedSolution: Using E_k = ½mω²(x₀² − x²) gives E_k = 0.5 × 0.8 × 20² × (0.06² − 0.048²) = 0.207 J.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes the total mechanical energy ½mω²x₀² instead of subtracting potential energy at x.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the potential energy ½mω²x² at x rather than the kinetic energy ½mω²(x₀² − x²).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Interpolates energy linearly as E_tot(1 − x / x₀) instead of quadratically as E_tot(1 − x² / x₀²).

items.stem: A collimated ray inside optical diamond (n₁ = 2.42, vacuum light speed c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) strikes a flat interface with liquid ethanol (n₂ = 1.36) at 51° to the normal during a submarine periscope window assembly. Through what angle is the ray deviated from its original forward path at this boundary?
items.workedSolution: Since sin θ_c = 1.36 / 2.42 gives θ_c = 34.2° and θ₁ = 51° > θ_c, the beam undergoes total internal reflection with θ_r = 51°. The angular deviation from the original forward direction is δ = 180° − 2(51°) = 78.0°.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies TIR (θ₁ > θ_c = 34.2°) and computes δ = 180° − 2θ₁ = 78.0° (A).

items.stem: During alignment of an avionics fly-by-light data bus, monochromatic light from water (n_ext = 1.33) strikes the entry face of a 120 m step-index fiber (n_core = 1.58, n_clad = 1.49) at 15.6° to the central optic axis. Determine the angle of incidence θ_w at the cylindrical core–cladding boundary relative to its normal.
items.workedSolution: At the entry face, 1.33 sin 15.6° = 1.58 sin θ_axis ⇒ θ_axis = 13.1°. Since the core wall is parallel to the axis, its normal is perpendicular to the axis, giving θ_w = 90° − θ_axis = 76.9°.

items.stem: In a botanical loupe magnifier bench, a specimen of height 0.015 m is placed 0.192 m in front of a convex magnifying lens of focal length 0.24 m. Calculate the upright virtual image height h_i.
items.workedSolution: From 1/v = 1/0.24 − 1/0.192, v = -0.960 m. Linear magnification m = −v / u = 5.000, so upright image height h_i = m h_o = 0.0750 m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses the diverging-lens formula f / (f + u) for magnification, obtaining a diminished height smaller than h_o.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Approximates magnification as f / u instead of |v| / u = f / (f − u).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Inverts linear magnification as u / |v| instead of |v| / u.

items.stem: In a calibration run of a spacecraft thruster-valve return-spring test fixture, a 0.8 kg carriage oscillates horizontally with amplitude 0.06 m on a spring of stiffness 32 N m⁻¹. Determine the frequency f in hertz.
items.workedSolution: Natural frequency f = (1 / 2π)√(k / m) = (1 / 2π)√(32 / 0.8) = 1.01 Hz.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Reports angular frequency ω = √(k / m) in rad s⁻¹ without dividing by 2π.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Swaps k/m and m/k, computing (1 / 2π)√(m / k) instead of (1 / 2π)√(k / m).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes the period T = 2π√(m / k) instead of frequency f = 1 / T.

items.stem: A vertical helical spring of stiffness 100 N m⁻¹ in a precision gravimeter spring-mass test stage suspends a load of mass 0.4 kg that subsequently oscillates vertically with amplitude 0.024 m. Taking g = 9.8 m s⁻², what was the static extension Δx_eq of the spring at equilibrium before oscillation started?
items.workedSolution: At static equilibrium, upward spring tension balances weight: k Δx_eq = mg ⇒ Δx_eq = (0.4 × 9.8) / 100 = 0.0392 m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Hooke's law as k / (mg) instead of mg / k.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Adds the oscillation amplitude x₀ to mg / k, finding maximum total stretch rather than static equilibrium extension.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides mass m directly by spring constant k without multiplying by gravitational field strength g.

items.stem: A 0.15 kg pendulum bob suspended from a 0.4 m wire in a physics laboratory light-gate timing pendulum oscillates in SHM with arc amplitude 0.1 m (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). What is the maximum speed v_max of the bob?
items.workedSolution: Angular frequency ω = √(g / L) = √(9.81 / 0.4), so maximum speed v_max = ω x₀ = 0.495 m s⁻¹.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts g / L inside √(g / L) when computing ω x₀.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Treats the horizontal arc amplitude x₀ as a vertical free-fall drop height h in √(2gh).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes ω² x₀ = (g / L) x₀ (maximum acceleration) instead of ω x₀ = √(g / L) x₀.

items.stem: During calibration of a piezoelectric laser-mirror dithering stage vibrating at f = 4 Hz and amplitude 0.02 m, a laser sensor records an instantaneous displacement x = 0.007 m. Determine the signed SHM acceleration a at that instant.
items.workedSolution: Angular frequency ω = 2πf = 2π(4) = 25.13 rad s⁻¹. By the defining SHM equation, a = −ω²x = −(25.13)²(0.007) = -4.42 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ω = 2πf and obtains -4.42 m s⁻² (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates −ωx instead of −ω²x, forgetting to square the angular frequency.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes cyclic frequency f directly for angular frequency ω, computing −f²x instead of −(2πf)²x.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the restoring minus sign in a = −ω²x, giving acceleration in the same sign as displacement instead of toward equilibrium.

items.stem: In an ultrasonic wire-bonding horn tip, a 0.8 kg oscillator moves harmonically at ω = 18 rad s⁻¹ with amplitude x₀ = 0.12 m (sampled at 0.048 m). At what positive displacement x from equilibrium is its kinetic energy equal to its potential energy (E_k = E_p)?
items.workedSolution: Setting E_p = ½E_tot gives ½mω²x² = ½(½mω²x₀²), so x² = x₀² / 2 and x = x₀ / √2 = 0.12 / √2 = 0.0849 m.

markScheme.criterion: Solves x² = x₀² / 2 to obtain x = x₀ / √2 = 0.0849 m (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes (√3 / 2)x₀ (where E_p = ¾E_tot) instead of x₀ / √2.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Squares the ½ factor to obtain x₀ / 4 instead of taking the square root x₀ / √2.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Assumes E_k = E_p occurs at half the amplitude (x₀ / 2, where E_p = ¼E_tot) instead of x₀ / √2.

items.stem: A 40 m step-index waveguide in a borehole geophysical telemetry line is fabricated with a core of refractive index 1.62 surrounded by cladding of refractive index 1.51, with light launched from air (n_ext = 1.00) at 12.6° to the axis. What is the critical angle θ_c at the core–cladding interface?
items.workedSolution: At the core–cladding boundary, sin θ_c = n_clad / n_core = 1.51 / 1.62 = 0.9321, giving θ_c = 68.8°.

items.stem: An observer using a museum conservation inspection magnifier adjusts the position of a 0.012 m scale mark in front of a thin convex lens of focal length 0.12 m until its virtual image lies at the near point 0.0800 m on the object side of the lens (v = −0.0800 m). Calculate the object distance u.
items.workedSolution: For a virtual image in the real-is-positive convention, v = -0.0800 m. Thus 1/u = 1/f − 1/v = 1/0.12 − (1/-0.08000) = 20.83 m⁻¹, giving u = 0.0480 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes negative v = -0.0800 m into 1/u = 1/f − 1/v to obtain u = 0.0480 m (A).

items.stem: A thin diverging lens of focal length f = −0.4 m in a clinical optometry phoropter test cell forms a virtual image of an upright object of height 0.036 m placed at u = 0.24 m. What is the linear magnification m = −v / u of the image?
items.workedSolution: With f = −0.4 m, 1/v = −1/0.4 − 1/0.24 gives v = -0.150 m. Therefore m = −v / u = −(-0.1500) / 0.24 = 0.625 (upright and diminished).

markScheme.criterion: Finds v = -0.150 m and m = −v / u = 0.625 (B).

items.stem: A 0.75 kg mass suspended vertically from a spring of stiffness 80 N m⁻¹ in an acoustic transducer moving-coil suspension rig is pulled down 0.032 m below equilibrium and released (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). What is the period T of the resulting vertical simple harmonic motion?
items.workedSolution: Gravity shifts the equilibrium position without altering effective stiffness k, so T = 2π√(m / k) = 2π√(0.75 / 80) = 0.608 s.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Swaps m/k and k/m inside the square root.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Incorrectly adds weight mg to spring stiffness k, assuming gravity changes the vertical mass-spring period.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes the oscillation amplitude x₀ into a pendulum-style formula 2π√(x₀ / g) instead of 2π√(m / k).

items.stem: In a vibrometer calibration shaker table, an oscillator undergoes SHM at 3 Hz with amplitude 0.08 m (passing through x = -0.028 m). Calculate the peak acceleration magnitude a_max = (2πf)² x₀.
items.workedSolution: With ω = 2π(3) = 18.85 rad s⁻¹, maximum acceleration magnitude a_max = ω² x₀ = 28.4 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ω = 2πf and obtains 28.4 m s⁻² (A).

items.stem: A harmonic oscillator in a marine wave-tank oscillating piston paddle moves with amplitude x₀ = 0.1 m and angular frequency ω = 30 rad s⁻¹. Calculate its speed when passing through displacement x = 0.05 m.
items.workedSolution: Using v = ω√(x₀² − x²) gives v = 30 × √(0.1² − 0.05²) = 2.60 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into v = ω√(x₀² − x²) to obtain 2.60 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: Within a spectrophotometer cuvette wall, monochromatic light (vacuum speed 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) propagating in polycarbonate polymer (n₁ = 1.58) is incident at 66° to the normal on distilled water (n₂ = 1.33). Determine the critical angle θ_c between these two media.
items.workedSolution: At the critical angle θ_c, sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1.33 / 1.58 = 0.8418, giving θ_c = arcsin(0.8418) = 57.3°.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1.33 / 1.58 to obtain θ_c = 57.3° (D).

items.stem: During alignment of a short-reach datacenter patch cord, monochromatic light from air (n_ext = 1.00) strikes the entry face of a 120 m step-index fiber (n_core = 1.62, n_clad = 1.51) at 15.4° to the central optic axis. Determine the angle of incidence θ_w at the cylindrical core–cladding boundary relative to its normal.
items.workedSolution: At the entry face, 1 sin 15.4° = 1.62 sin θ_axis ⇒ θ_axis = 9.43°. Since the core wall is parallel to the axis, its normal is perpendicular to the axis, giving θ_w = 90° − θ_axis = 80.6°.

items.stem: A 450 m step-index optical fiber in a cryogenic laboratory optical feedthrough has core refractive index 1.57 and cladding refractive index 1.46, with its flat input face in air of refractive index 1.00 (currently aligned with a test ray at 22.2°). What is the maximum external launch angle θ_max to the fiber axis for which rays remain guided by total internal reflection?
items.workedSolution: At the grazing limit, sin θ_c = 1.46 / 1.57, so inside the core sin θ_axis,max = cos θ_c = √(1 − (n_clad / n_core)²). By Snell's law at the entry face, n_ext sin θ_max = √(n_core² − n_clad²) = 0.5773, giving θ_max = arcsin(0.5773) = 35.3°.

markScheme.criterion: Uses n_ext sin θ_max = √(n_core² − n_clad²) to obtain θ_max = 35.3° (C).

items.stem: During optical testing on a pulsed-laser divergence compensator, a 0.036 m illuminated target sits 0.15 m from a thin diverging lens of focal length −0.25 m. Determine the signed image position v under the real-is-positive sign convention.
items.workedSolution: For a diverging lens, f = −0.25 m. Using 1/f = 1/u + 1/v gives 1/v = −1/0.25 − 1/0.15 = -10.67 m⁻¹, so v = -0.0937 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses negative f = −0.25 m in 1/v = 1/f − 1/u to obtain v = -0.0937 m (B).

items.stem: Engineers testing a robotics compliant-actuator test carriage measure a moving mass of 0.64 kg attached to an ideal horizontal spring of constant 45 N m⁻¹ oscillating with amplitude 0.06 m. Determine the period T of one complete cycle.
items.workedSolution: For an ideal mass-spring oscillator, T = 2π√(m / k) = 2π√(0.64 / 45) = 0.749 s.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Omits the square root and evaluates 2π(m / k).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 2π and calculates √(m / k) = 1 / ω.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Swaps m/k and k/m inside the radical, computing 2π√(k / m) instead of 2π√(m / k).

items.stem: A 0.6 kg brass bob on a 0.72 m suspension wire in a mine-shaft gravity-anomaly survey pendulum oscillates with arc-length amplitude 0.1584 m (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Calculate the maximum cord tension at the bottom of the swing.
items.workedSolution: With ω = √(g / L) = √(9.81 / 0.72), peak speed v_max = ω x₀ = 0.585 m s⁻¹. At the lowest point, T_cord = m(g + v_max² / L) = 6.17 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_max = ω x₀ and T_cord = mg + mv_max² / L = 6.17 N (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Equates cord tension at the lowest point to static weight mg, ignoring the upward centripetal force mv_max² / L.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts the centripetal force mv_max² / L from mg instead of adding it at the bottom of the arc.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates only the net radial centripetal force mv_max² / L rather than the total cord tension.

items.stem: In a dynamic mechanical thermal-analyzer probe, a stage oscillates in simple harmonic motion with angular frequency ω = 25 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude x₀ = 0.06 m, tracing the velocity–displacement ellipse shown. What is the speed v of the stage when its displacement from equilibrium is x = 0.0216 m?
items.workedSolution: Using v = ω√(x₀² − x²) gives v = 25 × √(0.06² − 0.0216²) = 1.40 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into v = ω√(x₀² − x²) to obtain 1.40 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: A 1.2 kg harmonic proof mass in a scanning-probe interferometric calibration stage vibrates at ω = 12 rad s⁻¹ with amplitude 0.08 m. Determine its kinetic energy at the instant x = 0.04 m.
items.workedSolution: Using E_k = ½mω²(x₀² − x²) gives E_k = 0.5 × 1.2 × 12² × (0.08² − 0.04²) = 0.415 J.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes the total mechanical energy ½mω²x₀² instead of subtracting potential energy at x.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Interpolates energy linearly as E_tot(1 − x / x₀) instead of quadratically as E_tot(1 − x² / x₀²).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the potential energy ½mω²x² at x rather than the kinetic energy ½mω²(x₀² − x²).

items.stem: A collimated ray inside dense flint glass (n₁ = 1.65, vacuum light speed c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) strikes a flat interface with distilled water (n₂ = 1.33) at 66° to the normal during an ophthalmic lens-blank inspection jig. Through what angle is the ray deviated from its original forward path at this boundary?
items.workedSolution: Since sin θ_c = 1.33 / 1.65 gives θ_c = 53.7° and θ₁ = 66° > θ_c, the beam undergoes total internal reflection with θ_r = 66°. The angular deviation from the original forward direction is δ = 180° − 2(66°) = 48.0°.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies TIR (θ₁ > θ_c = 53.7°) and computes δ = 180° − 2θ₁ = 48.0° (B).

items.stem: In an autonomous lidar reference delay spool, a short optical pulse enters a 1200 m step-index fiber (core index 1.48, cladding index 1.41, n_ext = 1.00, sample launch angle 18.7°). With c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, calculate the modal time delay Δt = t_max − t_axial at the output end.
items.workedSolution: Axial transit time t_min = n_core L / c = (1.48 × 1200) / (3.00 × 10⁸) = 5.92 × 10⁻⁶ s. At the critical angle sin θ_c = n_clad / n_core, t_max = t_min / sin θ_c = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 6.21 × 10⁻⁶ s. Modal delay Δt = t_max − t_min = 2.94 × 10⁻⁷ s.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δt = (n_core L / c)(n_core / n_clad − 1) = 2.94 × 10⁻⁷ s (B).

items.stem: A thin converging inspection lens of focal length 0.25 m in a retinal fundus imaging objective rig views an upright feature of height 0.018 m held at object distance u = 0.17 m (< f). What is the height h_i of the virtual upright image?
items.workedSolution: From 1/v = 1/0.25 − 1/0.17, v = -0.531 m. Linear magnification m = −v / u = 3.125, so upright image height h_i = m h_o = 0.0563 m.

items.stem: During optical testing on an underwater dome-port virtual-image corrector, a 0.02 m illuminated target sits 0.56 m from a thin diverging lens of focal length −0.4 m. Determine the signed image position v under the real-is-positive sign convention.
items.workedSolution: For a diverging lens, f = −0.4 m. Using 1/f = 1/u + 1/v gives 1/v = −1/0.4 − 1/0.56 = -4.286 m⁻¹, so v = -0.233 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses negative f = −0.4 m in 1/v = 1/f − 1/u to obtain v = -0.233 m (C).

options.distractorRationale: Forgets that a diverging lens has negative focal length f < 0, substituting +|f| into 1/v = 1/f − 1/u.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes the correct magnitude |v| but omits the negative sign required for a virtual image in the real-is-positive convention.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Stops at 1/v = −1/|f| − 1/u in m⁻¹ without taking the reciprocal to find v in metres.

items.stem: A vertical helical spring of stiffness 25 N m⁻¹ in an orbital microgravity mass-measurement spring chair suspends a load of mass 0.6 kg that subsequently oscillates vertically with amplitude 0.032 m. Taking g = 9.81 m s⁻², what was the static extension Δx_eq of the spring at equilibrium before oscillation started?
items.workedSolution: At static equilibrium, upward spring tension balances weight: k Δx_eq = mg ⇒ Δx_eq = (0.6 × 9.81) / 25 = 0.235 m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Divides mass m directly by spring constant k without multiplying by gravitational field strength g.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Adds the oscillation amplitude x₀ to mg / k, finding maximum total stretch rather than static equilibrium extension.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Hooke's law as k / (mg) instead of mg / k.

items.stem: In an astronomical observatory sidereal regulator pendulum, a simple pendulum of length 0.4 m and bob mass 0.4 kg swings with small arc amplitude 0.088 m where g = 9.81 m s⁻². Calculate its speed at the equilibrium position.
items.workedSolution: Angular frequency ω = √(g / L) = √(9.81 / 0.4), so maximum speed v_max = ω x₀ = 0.436 m s⁻¹.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts g / L inside √(g / L) when computing ω x₀.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Treats the horizontal arc amplitude x₀ as a vertical free-fall drop height h in √(2gh).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes ω² x₀ = (g / L) x₀ (maximum acceleration) instead of ω x₀ = √(g / L) x₀.

items.stem: A vibrating element in a precision optical-chopper resonant blade executes simple harmonic motion of frequency 1.5 Hz and amplitude 0.06 m (sampled at x = 0.045 m). What is the magnitude a_max of its maximum acceleration?
items.workedSolution: With ω = 2π(1.5) = 9.425 rad s⁻¹, maximum acceleration magnitude a_max = ω² x₀ = 5.33 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ω = 2πf and obtains 5.33 m s⁻² (C).

options.distractorRationale: Calculates ω x₀ (maximum speed) instead of ω² x₀ (maximum acceleration).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor (2π)² = 4π² and computes f² x₀.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes the acceleration magnitude at x rather than at maximum displacement x₀.

items.stem: For a diesel injector needle-valve harmonic test rig executing undamped SHM of mass 1.2 kg, angular frequency 20 rad s⁻¹, and amplitude 0.08 m (reference mark at 0.064 m), determine the positive displacement at which E_k = E_p.
items.workedSolution: Setting E_p = ½E_tot gives ½mω²x² = ½(½mω²x₀²), so x² = x₀² / 2 and x = x₀ / √2 = 0.08 / √2 = 0.0566 m.

markScheme.criterion: Solves x² = x₀² / 2 to obtain x = x₀ / √2 = 0.0566 m (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Squares the ½ factor to obtain x₀ / 4 instead of taking the square root x₀ / √2.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Assumes E_k = E_p occurs at half the amplitude (x₀ / 2, where E_p = ¼E_tot) instead of x₀ / √2.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes (√3 / 2)x₀ (where E_p = ¾E_tot) instead of x₀ / √2.

items.stem: In an astronomical echelle-spectrograph feed, an optical pulse enters a 80 m step-index fiber (core index 1.5, cladding index 1.44) from air (n_ext = 1.00) at a launch angle of 14.7° to the axis. Calculate the incident angle θ_w on the core–cladding interface normal.
items.workedSolution: At the entry face, 1 sin 14.7° = 1.5 sin θ_axis ⇒ θ_axis = 9.74°. Since the core wall is parallel to the axis, its normal is perpendicular to the axis, giving θ_w = 90° − θ_axis = 80.3°.

items.stem: In a heads-up display collimating negative element, an object of height 0.05 m is positioned 0.3 m from a concave lens of focal length −0.2 m. Calculate the signed linear magnification m = h_i / h_o = −v / u.
items.workedSolution: With f = −0.2 m, 1/v = −1/0.2 − 1/0.3 gives v = -0.120 m. Therefore m = −v / u = −(-0.1200) / 0.3 = 0.400 (upright and diminished).

markScheme.criterion: Finds v = -0.120 m and m = −v / u = 0.400 (B).
