options.distractorRationale: Assigns a negative magnification as if a diverging lens formed an inverted real image of a real object.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes positive f = +|f| instead of negative f = −|f| into the lens equation before computing magnification.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the magnification ratio as u / |v| (> 1) instead of |v| / u (< 1).

items.stem: During stiffness testing on a railway bogie secondary-suspension scale model, a 1.2 kg mass oscillates horizontally with amplitude 0.09 m and a measured period of 1.22 s. What is the spring constant k?
items.workedSolution: Rearranging T = 2π√(m / k) gives k = 4π²m / T² = 4π²(1.2) / (1.22)² = 32.0 N m⁻¹.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 4π² and computes m / T².

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Fails to square 2π / T when rearranging T = 2π√(m / k), computing 2πm / T instead of 4π²m / T².

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts m / T² when rearranging the period equation.

items.stem: In a micro-electro-mechanical resonant beam, a component executes simple harmonic motion at frequency f = 12 Hz with amplitude x₀ = 0.02 m, as represented on the acceleration–displacement graph. Taking displacement to the right as positive, what is its signed acceleration a when x = -0.009 m?
items.workedSolution: Angular frequency ω = 2πf = 2π(12) = 75.40 rad s⁻¹. By the defining SHM equation, a = −ω²x = −(75.40)²(-0.009) = 51.2 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ω = 2πf and obtains 51.2 m s⁻² (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes cyclic frequency f directly for angular frequency ω, computing −f²x instead of −(2πf)²x.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates −ωx instead of −ω²x, forgetting to square the angular frequency.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the restoring minus sign in a = −ω²x, giving acceleration in the same sign as displacement instead of toward equilibrium.

items.stem: In an ultrasonic wire-bonding horn tip, a stage oscillates in simple harmonic motion with angular frequency ω = 24 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude x₀ = 0.05 m, tracing the velocity–displacement ellipse shown. What is the speed v of the stage when its displacement from equilibrium is x = 0.03 m?
items.workedSolution: Using v = ω√(x₀² − x²) gives v = 24 × √(0.05² − 0.03²) = 0.960 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into v = ω√(x₀² − x²) to obtain 0.960 m s⁻¹ (D).

options.distractorRationale: Calculates the maximum speed ωx₀ at equilibrium (x = 0) instead of the speed at x.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses ωx instead of ω√(x₀² − x²), mistakenly assuming speed is directly proportional to displacement.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates ω(x₀ − x) linearly instead of taking √(x₀² − x²).

items.stem: A prism assembly in a semiconductor immersion-lithography stage places polycarbonate polymer of refractive index 1.58 in contact with liquid ethanol of refractive index 1.36 (take c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹). A test beam strikes the interface from inside polycarbonate polymer at 65° to the normal. Calculate the critical angle for total internal reflection at the boundary.
items.workedSolution: At the critical angle θ_c, sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1.36 / 1.58 = 0.8608, giving θ_c = arcsin(0.8608) = 59.4°.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1.36 / 1.58 to obtain θ_c = 59.4° (A).

options.distractorRationale: Uses tan θ_c = n₂ / n₁ (confusing critical angle with Brewster-like tangent expressions) instead of sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁.

items.stem: A 350 m step-index waveguide in a high-voltage substation optical isolator link is fabricated with a core of refractive index 1.52 surrounded by cladding of refractive index 1.46, with light launched from water (n_ext = 1.33) at 12.4° to the axis. What is the critical angle θ_c at the core–cladding interface?
items.workedSolution: At the core–cladding boundary, sin θ_c = n_clad / n_core = 1.46 / 1.52 = 0.9605, giving θ_c = 73.8°.

items.stem: In an optical-bench crosswire projection setup, a small specimen of height 0.008 m is held 0.102 m in front of a thin converging magnifier lens of focal length 0.15 m. Using the real-is-positive sign convention (1/f = 1/u + 1/v), what is the signed image distance v?
items.workedSolution: Because u = 0.102 m < f = 0.15 m, 1/v = 1/0.15 − 1/0.102 = -3.137 m⁻¹, giving a signed virtual image distance v = -0.319 m.

markScheme.criterion: Computes 1/v = 1/0.15 − 1/0.102 to obtain signed v = -0.319 m (B).

options.distractorRationale: Forgets that v < 0 for a virtual image in the real-is-positive sign convention, reporting +|v| as if a real image formed behind the lens.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Adds 1/f + 1/u instead of evaluating 1/v = 1/f − 1/u.

items.stem: Engineers testing a precision gravimeter spring-mass test stage measure a moving mass of 0.25 kg attached to an ideal horizontal spring of constant 72 N m⁻¹ oscillating with amplitude 0.035 m. Determine the period T of one complete cycle.
items.workedSolution: For an ideal mass-spring oscillator, T = 2π√(m / k) = 2π√(0.25 / 72) = 0.370 s.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Omits the square root and evaluates 2π(m / k).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 2π and calculates √(m / k) = 1 / ω.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Swaps m/k and k/m inside the radical, computing 2π√(k / m) instead of 2π√(m / k).

items.stem: In a high-speed pantograph contact-spring test rig, a 0.5 kg mass hangs from a vertical spring of constant 40 N m⁻¹ and executes vertical SHM of amplitude 0.018 m (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Calculate the static equilibrium extension Δx_eq from the spring's unstretched length.
items.workedSolution: At static equilibrium, upward spring tension balances weight: k Δx_eq = mg ⇒ Δx_eq = (0.5 × 9.81) / 40 = 0.123 m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Adds the oscillation amplitude x₀ to mg / k, finding maximum total stretch rather than static equilibrium extension.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Divides mass m directly by spring constant k without multiplying by gravitational field strength g.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Hooke's law as k / (mg) instead of mg / k.

items.stem: In a metrology gravimetry pendulum stand, a pendulum bob of mass 0.6 kg hangs on a light cord of length 1.6 m and swings in small-angle SHM with arc amplitude 0.4 m. Taking g = 9.81 m s⁻², what is the tension in the cord as the bob passes through its lowest equilibrium point?
items.workedSolution: With ω = √(g / L) = √(9.81 / 1.6), peak speed v_max = ω x₀ = 0.990 m s⁻¹. At the lowest point, T_cord = m(g + v_max² / L) = 6.25 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_max = ω x₀ and T_cord = mg + mv_max² / L = 6.25 N (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts the centripetal force mv_max² / L from mg instead of adding it at the bottom of the arc.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Equates cord tension at the lowest point to static weight mg, ignoring the upward centripetal force mv_max² / L.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates only the net radial centripetal force mv_max² / L rather than the total cord tension.

items.stem: In a marine wave-tank oscillating piston paddle, an oscillator undergoes SHM at 2.5 Hz with amplitude 0.1 m (passing through x = 0.06 m). Calculate the peak acceleration magnitude a_max = (2πf)² x₀.
items.workedSolution: With ω = 2π(2.5) = 15.71 rad s⁻¹, maximum acceleration magnitude a_max = ω² x₀ = 24.7 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ω = 2πf and obtains 24.7 m s⁻² (D).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates ω x₀ (maximum speed) instead of ω² x₀ (maximum acceleration).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes the acceleration magnitude at x rather than at maximum displacement x₀.

items.stem: The parabolic SHM energy graph shown corresponds to an ultrasonic surgical transducer tip (mass 0.25 kg, angular frequency 20 rad s⁻¹, amplitude 0.14 m). Calculate the kinetic energy E_k at displacement x = 0.056 m.
items.workedSolution: Using E_k = ½mω²(x₀² − x²) gives E_k = 0.5 × 0.25 × 20² × (0.14² − 0.056²) = 0.823 J.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes the total mechanical energy ½mω²x₀² instead of subtracting potential energy at x.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Interpolates energy linearly as E_tot(1 − x / x₀) instead of quadratically as E_tot(1 − x² / x₀²).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the potential energy ½mω²x² at x rather than the kinetic energy ½mω²(x₀² − x²).

items.stem: A collimated ray inside dense flint glass (n₁ = 1.65, vacuum light speed c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) strikes a flat interface with liquid ethanol (n₂ = 1.36) at 61° to the normal during a planetary lander atmospheric nephelometer. Through what angle is the ray deviated from its original forward path at this boundary?
items.workedSolution: Since sin θ_c = 1.36 / 1.65 gives θ_c = 55.5° and θ₁ = 61° > θ_c, the beam undergoes total internal reflection with θ_r = 61°. The angular deviation from the original forward direction is δ = 180° − 2(61°) = 58.0°.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies TIR (θ₁ > θ_c = 55.5°) and computes δ = 180° − 2θ₁ = 58.0° (C).

Taking the numerical aperture as NA = √(n_core² − n_clad²), what is the numerical aperture of this fiber?

items.stem: In a flexible medical gastroscope bundle, a short optical pulse enters a 240 m step-index fiber (core index 1.62, cladding index 1.51, n_ext = 1.00, sample launch angle 21.6°). With c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, calculate the modal time delay Δt = t_max − t_axial at the output end.
items.workedSolution: Axial transit time t_min = n_core L / c = (1.62 × 240) / (3.00 × 10⁸) = 1.30 × 10⁻⁶ s. At the critical angle sin θ_c = n_clad / n_core, t_max = t_min / sin θ_c = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 1.39 × 10⁻⁶ s. Modal delay Δt = t_max − t_min = 9.44 × 10⁻⁸ s.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δt = (n_core L / c)(n_core / n_clad − 1) = 9.44 × 10⁻⁸ s (A).

items.stem: In a refracting telescope objective assembly, a specimen of height 0.018 m is placed 0.075 m in front of a convex magnifying lens of focal length 0.1 m. Calculate the upright virtual image height h_i.
items.workedSolution: From 1/v = 1/0.1 − 1/0.075, v = -0.300 m. Linear magnification m = −v / u = 4.000, so upright image height h_i = m h_o = 0.0720 m.

items.stem: During optical testing on an architectural wide-field door viewer, a 0.036 m illuminated target sits 0.3 m from a thin diverging lens of focal length −0.12 m. Determine the signed image position v under the real-is-positive sign convention.
items.workedSolution: For a diverging lens, f = −0.12 m. Using 1/f = 1/u + 1/v gives 1/v = −1/0.12 − 1/0.3 = -11.67 m⁻¹, so v = -0.0857 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses negative f = −0.12 m in 1/v = 1/f − 1/u to obtain v = -0.0857 m (B).

items.stem: In a cryogenic cooler linear-compressor piston assembly, a 0.6 kg mass hangs from a vertical spring of constant 64 N m⁻¹ and executes vertical SHM of amplitude 0.032 m (take g = 9.8 m s⁻²). Calculate the static equilibrium extension Δx_eq from the spring's unstretched length.
items.workedSolution: At static equilibrium, upward spring tension balances weight: k Δx_eq = mg ⇒ Δx_eq = (0.6 × 9.8) / 64 = 0.0919 m.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Adds the oscillation amplitude x₀ to mg / k, finding maximum total stretch rather than static equilibrium extension.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Hooke's law as k / (mg) instead of mg / k.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides mass m directly by spring constant k without multiplying by gravitational field strength g.

items.stem: The acceleration–displacement line shown models a dynamic mechanical thermal-analyzer probe oscillating harmonically at 8 Hz with amplitude 0.03 m. Using a = −ω²x, calculate the signed acceleration at displacement x = 0.0225 m.
items.workedSolution: Angular frequency ω = 2πf = 2π(8) = 50.27 rad s⁻¹. By the defining SHM equation, a = −ω²x = −(50.27)²(0.0225) = -56.8 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ω = 2πf and obtains -56.8 m s⁻² (A).

items.stem: In a scanning-probe interferometric calibration stage, a stage oscillates in simple harmonic motion with angular frequency ω = 30 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude x₀ = 0.06 m, tracing the velocity–displacement ellipse shown. What is the speed v of the stage when its displacement from equilibrium is x = 0.03 m?
items.workedSolution: Using v = ω√(x₀² − x²) gives v = 30 × √(0.06² − 0.03²) = 1.56 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into v = ω√(x₀² − x²) to obtain 1.56 m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: A 350 m step-index optical fiber used in a flexible medical gastroscope bundle has core refractive index 1.57 and cladding refractive index 1.46. A laser ray in air (n_ext = 1.00) enters the center of the flat end-face at θ_in = 20.8° to the fiber axis. What angle of incidence θ_w does the refracted ray make with the normal to the core–cladding wall?
items.workedSolution: At the entry face, 1 sin 20.8° = 1.57 sin θ_axis ⇒ θ_axis = 13.1°. Since the core wall is parallel to the axis, its normal is perpendicular to the axis, giving θ_w = 90° − θ_axis = 76.9°.

items.stem: A 1800 m multimode step-index cable in a structural-health bridge sensor lead has core index 1.49 and cladding index 1.39 in air (n_ext = 1.00, sample launch angle 22.7°, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹). Calculate the maximum guided transit time through the fiber.
items.workedSolution: Wave speed in the core is v = c / n_core, and the critical-angle ray travels path length L / sin θ_c = L (n_core / n_clad). Therefore t_max = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 9.58 × 10⁻⁶ s.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates t_max = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 9.58 × 10⁻⁶ s (A).

items.stem: A thin diverging lens of focal length f = −0.4 m in a high-power excimer beam-shaping negative lens forms a virtual image of an upright object of height 0.036 m placed at u = 1 m. What is the linear magnification m = −v / u of the image?
items.workedSolution: With f = −0.4 m, 1/v = −1/0.4 − 1/1 gives v = -0.286 m. Therefore m = −v / u = −(-0.2857) / 1 = 0.286 (upright and diminished).

markScheme.criterion: Finds v = -0.286 m and m = −v / u = 0.286 (B).

items.stem: During stiffness testing on a cleanroom nanopositioning flexure stage, a 0.36 kg mass oscillates horizontally with amplitude 0.09 m and a measured period of 0.298 s. What is the spring constant k?
items.workedSolution: Rearranging T = 2π√(m / k) gives k = 4π²m / T² = 4π²(0.36) / (0.298)² = 160 N m⁻¹.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts m / T² when rearranging the period equation.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 4π² and computes m / T².

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Fails to square 2π / T when rearranging T = 2π√(m / k), computing 2πm / T instead of 4π²m / T².

items.stem: Engineers timing a skyscraper tuned-pendulum damper scale model use a 0.5 kg bob on a 0.85 m light cord swinging with arc amplitude 0.187 m (g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Calculate the period T.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts L / g inside the square root.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the half-period π√(L / g) instead of the full period 2π√(L / g).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the square root on L / g.

items.stem: A harmonic oscillator in a diesel injector needle-valve harmonic test rig moves with amplitude x₀ = 0.15 m and angular frequency ω = 10 rad s⁻¹. Calculate its speed when passing through displacement x = 0.054 m.
items.workedSolution: Using v = ω√(x₀² − x²) gives v = 10 × √(0.15² − 0.054²) = 1.40 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into v = ω√(x₀² − x²) to obtain 1.40 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: In an atomic-force microscope cantilever tip, a 0.5 kg mass undergoes SHM with ω = 20 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude 0.04 m (with a sensor at x = 0.02 m). Calculate the frequency f_E at which the kinetic energy completes full cycles.
items.workedSolution: Mechanical frequency f = ω / (2π) = 20 / (2π) = 3.183 Hz. Because kinetic energy reaches a maximum twice per mechanical period, f_E = 2f = ω / π = 6.37 Hz.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates 2ω in rad s⁻¹ without dividing by 2π to convert to hertz.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Gives the mechanical displacement frequency f = ω / (2π) instead of recognizing that E_k ∝ cos²(ωt) oscillates at 2f.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Halves the mechanical frequency instead of doubling it.

items.stem: In an industrial sugar-brix inline refractometer, a light ray inside synthetic sapphire (n₁ = 1.77, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) approaches a planar interface with distilled water (n₂ = 1.33) at an incident angle of 65° to the normal. What is the critical angle θ_c at this synthetic sapphire–distilled water boundary?
items.workedSolution: At the critical angle θ_c, sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1.33 / 1.77 = 0.7514, giving θ_c = arcsin(0.7514) = 48.7°.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1.33 / 1.77 to obtain θ_c = 48.7° (D).

items.stem: Within a precision machine-vision inspection camera, an upright scale mark of height 0.022 m sits 0.144 m from a thin convex lens of focal length 0.24 m. Applying 1/f = 1/u + 1/v in the real-is-positive convention, determine the signed image position v.
items.workedSolution: Because u = 0.144 m < f = 0.24 m, 1/v = 1/0.24 − 1/0.144 = -2.778 m⁻¹, giving a signed virtual image distance v = -0.360 m.

markScheme.criterion: Computes 1/v = 1/0.24 − 1/0.144 to obtain signed v = -0.360 m (D).

items.stem: Engineers testing an orbital microgravity mass-measurement spring chair measure a moving mass of 0.16 kg attached to an ideal horizontal spring of constant 120 N m⁻¹ oscillating with amplitude 0.045 m. Determine the period T of one complete cycle.
items.workedSolution: For an ideal mass-spring oscillator, T = 2π√(m / k) = 2π√(0.16 / 120) = 0.229 s.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Omits the square root and evaluates 2π(m / k).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 2π and calculates √(m / k) = 1 / ω.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Swaps m/k and k/m inside the radical, computing 2π√(k / m) instead of 2π√(m / k).

items.stem: A vertical helical spring of stiffness 80 N m⁻¹ in a frictionless air-track glider coupled to a calibrated coil spring suspends a load of mass 0.6 kg that subsequently oscillates vertically with amplitude 0.024 m. Taking g = 9.8 m s⁻², what was the static extension Δx_eq of the spring at equilibrium before oscillation started?
items.workedSolution: At static equilibrium, upward spring tension balances weight: k Δx_eq = mg ⇒ Δx_eq = (0.6 × 9.8) / 80 = 0.0735 m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Hooke's law as k / (mg) instead of mg / k.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Adds the oscillation amplitude x₀ to mg / k, finding maximum total stretch rather than static equilibrium extension.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides mass m directly by spring constant k without multiplying by gravitational field strength g.

items.stem: A 0.25 kg brass bob on a 1.9 m suspension wire in a geophysical field-survey simple pendulum oscillates with arc-length amplitude 0.38 m (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Calculate the maximum cord tension at the bottom of the swing.
items.workedSolution: With ω = √(g / L) = √(9.81 / 1.9), peak speed v_max = ω x₀ = 0.863 m s⁻¹. At the lowest point, T_cord = m(g + v_max² / L) = 2.55 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_max = ω x₀ and T_cord = mg + mv_max² / L = 2.55 N (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates only the net radial centripetal force mv_max² / L rather than the total cord tension.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts the centripetal force mv_max² / L from mg instead of adding it at the bottom of the arc.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Equates cord tension at the lowest point to static weight mg, ignoring the upward centripetal force mv_max² / L.

items.stem: In an ultrasonic wire-bonding horn tip, a component executes simple harmonic motion at frequency f = 5 Hz with amplitude x₀ = 0.04 m, as represented on the acceleration–displacement graph. Taking displacement to the right as positive, what is its signed acceleration a when x = 0.018 m?
items.workedSolution: Angular frequency ω = 2πf = 2π(5) = 31.42 rad s⁻¹. By the defining SHM equation, a = −ω²x = −(31.42)²(0.018) = -17.8 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ω = 2πf and obtains -17.8 m s⁻² (B).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the restoring minus sign in a = −ω²x, giving acceleration in the same sign as displacement instead of toward equilibrium.

items.stem: The parabolic SHM energy graph shown corresponds to a studio loudspeaker voice-coil cone (mass 0.15 kg, angular frequency 10 rad s⁻¹, amplitude 0.14 m). Calculate the kinetic energy E_k at displacement x = 0.07 m.
items.workedSolution: Using E_k = ½mω²(x₀² − x²) gives E_k = 0.5 × 0.15 × 10² × (0.14² − 0.07²) = 0.110 J.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the potential energy ½mω²x² at x rather than the kinetic energy ½mω²(x₀² − x²).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Interpolates energy linearly as E_tot(1 − x / x₀) instead of quadratically as E_tot(1 − x² / x₀²).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes the total mechanical energy ½mω²x₀² instead of subtracting potential energy at x.

items.stem: Engineers evaluating bit-rate limits for an avionics fly-by-light data bus test a 360 m step-index waveguide (n_core = 1.57, n_clad = 1.46, n_ext = 1.00, ray shown at 17.6°). Take c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹. Determine the multipath dispersion delay Δt between extreme guided rays and axial rays.
items.workedSolution: Axial transit time t_min = n_core L / c = (1.57 × 360) / (3.00 × 10⁸) = 1.88 × 10⁻⁶ s. At the critical angle sin θ_c = n_clad / n_core, t_max = t_min / sin θ_c = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 2.03 × 10⁻⁶ s. Modal delay Δt = t_max − t_min = 1.42 × 10⁻⁷ s.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δt = (n_core L / c)(n_core / n_clad − 1) = 1.42 × 10⁻⁷ s (C).

items.stem: In a cinema slide-projector lens mount, a specimen of height 0.015 m is placed 0.12 m in front of a convex magnifying lens of focal length 0.2 m. Calculate the upright virtual image height h_i.
items.workedSolution: From 1/v = 1/0.2 − 1/0.12, v = -0.300 m. Linear magnification m = −v / u = 2.500, so upright image height h_i = m h_o = 0.0375 m.

items.stem: In a myopia-corrective ophthalmic spectacle trial, an upright test object of height 0.03 m stands 0.6 m in front of a thin diverging lens of focal length magnitude 0.2 m (f = −0.2 m in the real-is-positive convention). What is the signed image distance v?
items.workedSolution: For a diverging lens, f = −0.2 m. Using 1/f = 1/u + 1/v gives 1/v = −1/0.2 − 1/0.6 = -6.667 m⁻¹, so v = -0.150 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses negative f = −0.2 m in 1/v = 1/f − 1/u to obtain v = -0.150 m (B).

items.stem: A vertical helical spring of stiffness 50 N m⁻¹ in a silicon MEMS accelerometer proof-mass flexure test model suspends a load of mass 0.75 kg that subsequently oscillates vertically with amplitude 0.018 m. Taking g = 9.81 m s⁻², what was the static extension Δx_eq of the spring at equilibrium before oscillation started?
items.workedSolution: At static equilibrium, upward spring tension balances weight: k Δx_eq = mg ⇒ Δx_eq = (0.75 × 9.81) / 50 = 0.147 m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Hooke's law as k / (mg) instead of mg / k.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Adds the oscillation amplitude x₀ to mg / k, finding maximum total stretch rather than static equilibrium extension.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides mass m directly by spring constant k without multiplying by gravitational field strength g.

items.stem: A vibrating element in a resonant Coriolis mass-flow sensor tube executes simple harmonic motion of frequency 1.5 Hz and amplitude 0.03 m (sampled at x = 0.018 m). What is the magnitude a_max of its maximum acceleration?
items.workedSolution: With ω = 2π(1.5) = 9.425 rad s⁻¹, maximum acceleration magnitude a_max = ω² x₀ = 2.66 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ω = 2πf and obtains 2.66 m s⁻² (A).

items.stem: The velocity–displacement phase portrait shown represents an ultrasonic surgical transducer tip oscillating with ω = 40 rad s⁻¹ and x₀ = 0.12 m. Find the oscillator's speed at x = 0.072 m.
items.workedSolution: Using v = ω√(x₀² − x²) gives v = 40 × √(0.12² − 0.072²) = 3.84 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into v = ω√(x₀² − x²) to obtain 3.84 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: On a bathymetric laser-ranging tank, the critical angle for total internal reflection of monochromatic light passing from a transparent crystal into liquid ethanol (n₂ = 1.36) is measured to be 59.4° to the normal. What is the refractive index n₁ of the crystal?
items.workedSolution: At the critical angle, n₁ sin θ_c = n₂ sin 90° = n₂, so n₁ = 1.36 / sin 59.4° = 1.58.

markScheme.criterion: Computes n₁ = n₂ / sin θ_c = 1.36 / sin 59.4° = 1.58 (B).

items.stem: In a structural-health bridge sensor lead, a guided ray from water of refractive index 1.33 enters a straight 750 m step-index fiber (n_core = 1.49, n_clad = 1.39) at launch angle θ_in = 15° to the axis. Neglecting end losses, what total geometric path length does this zig-zagging ray travel through the core?
items.workedSolution: Inside the core, sin θ_axis = (1.33 sin 15°) / 1.49 ⇒ θ_axis = 13.4°. The total zig-zag geometric path length is L_ray = L / cos θ_axis = 750 / cos 13.36° = 771 m.

markScheme.criterion: Finds θ_axis = 13.4° and computes L / cos θ_axis = 771 m (B).

items.stem: An observer using a laboratory autocollimator test rail adjusts the position of a 0.022 m scale mark in front of a thin convex lens of focal length 0.08 m until its virtual image lies at the near point 0.120 m on the object side of the lens (v = −0.120 m). Calculate the object distance u.
items.workedSolution: For a virtual image in the real-is-positive convention, v = -0.120 m. Thus 1/u = 1/f − 1/v = 1/0.08 − (1/-0.1200) = 20.83 m⁻¹, giving u = 0.0480 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes negative v = -0.120 m into 1/u = 1/f − 1/v to obtain u = 0.0480 m (C).

items.stem: During stiffness testing on a high-speed pantograph contact-spring test rig, a 0.25 kg mass oscillates horizontally with amplitude 0.025 m and a measured period of 0.740 s. What is the spring constant k?
items.workedSolution: Rearranging T = 2π√(m / k) gives k = 4π²m / T² = 4π²(0.25) / (0.740)² = 18.0 N m⁻¹.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 4π² and computes m / T².

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Fails to square 2π / T when rearranging T = 2π√(m / k), computing 2πm / T instead of 4π²m / T².

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts m / T² when rearranging the period equation.

items.stem: Engineers timing an evacuated bell-jar precision timing pendulum use a 0.6 kg bob on a 0.55 m light cord swinging with arc amplitude 0.11 m (g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Calculate the period T.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the half-period π√(L / g) instead of the full period 2π√(L / g).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Inverts L / g inside the square root.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the square root on L / g.

items.stem: Engineers monitoring a quartz crystal tuning-fork tine measure simple harmonic motion of amplitude 0.08 m and angular frequency 30 rad s⁻¹. Determine the speed |v| = ω√(x₀² − x²) at displacement x = 0.064 m.
items.workedSolution: Using v = ω√(x₀² − x²) gives v = 30 × √(0.08² − 0.064²) = 1.44 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into v = ω√(x₀² − x²) to obtain 1.44 m s⁻¹ (B).

options.distractorRationale: Evaluates ω(x₀ − x) linearly instead of taking √(x₀² − x²).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses ωx instead of ω√(x₀² − x²), mistakenly assuming speed is directly proportional to displacement.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the maximum speed ωx₀ at equilibrium (x = 0) instead of the speed at x.

items.stem: A 0.6 kg resonator in a vibrometer calibration shaker table executes simple harmonic motion of amplitude 0.14 m and angular frequency ω = 30 rad s⁻¹ (probed at x = 0.035 m). At what cyclic frequency f_E does its kinetic energy oscillate with time?
items.workedSolution: Mechanical frequency f = ω / (2π) = 30 / (2π) = 4.775 Hz. Because kinetic energy reaches a maximum twice per mechanical period, f_E = 2f = ω / π = 9.55 Hz.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Gives the mechanical displacement frequency f = ω / (2π) instead of recognizing that E_k ∝ cos²(ωt) oscillates at 2f.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Halves the mechanical frequency instead of doubling it.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates 2ω in rad s⁻¹ without dividing by 2π to convert to hertz.

items.stem: Within a precision Abbe refractometer cell, monochromatic light (vacuum speed 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) propagating in synthetic sapphire (n₁ = 1.77) is incident at 43° to the normal on dry air (n₂ = 1). Determine the critical angle θ_c between these two media.
items.workedSolution: At the critical angle θ_c, sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1 / 1.77 = 0.5650, giving θ_c = arcsin(0.5650) = 34.4°.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1 / 1.77 to obtain θ_c = 34.4° (B).

items.stem: In an industrial laser-welding delivery cable, a 300 m step-index waveguide with n_core = 1.54 and n_clad = 1.45 receives light from air of refractive index 1.00 (shown for a 22.5° ray). Determine the maximum external incidence angle θ_max to the axis that still achieves total internal reflection at the core wall.
items.workedSolution: At the grazing limit, sin θ_c = 1.45 / 1.54, so inside the core sin θ_axis,max = cos θ_c = √(1 − (n_clad / n_core)²). By Snell's law at the entry face, n_ext sin θ_max = √(n_core² − n_clad²) = 0.5187, giving θ_max = arcsin(0.5187) = 31.2°.

markScheme.criterion: Uses n_ext sin θ_max = √(n_core² − n_clad²) to obtain θ_max = 31.2° (C).

items.stem: In a short-reach datacenter patch cord, a short optical pulse enters a 750 m step-index fiber (core index 1.52, cladding index 1.46, n_ext = 1.00, sample launch angle 17.5°). With c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, calculate the modal time delay Δt = t_max − t_axial at the output end.
items.workedSolution: Axial transit time t_min = n_core L / c = (1.52 × 750) / (3.00 × 10⁸) = 3.80 × 10⁻⁶ s. At the critical angle sin θ_c = n_clad / n_core, t_max = t_min / sin θ_c = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 3.96 × 10⁻⁶ s. Modal delay Δt = t_max − t_min = 1.56 × 10⁻⁷ s.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δt = (n_core L / c)(n_core / n_clad − 1) = 1.56 × 10⁻⁷ s (C).

items.stem: In a metrology profile-projector optical train, a small specimen of height 0.018 m is held 0.08 m in front of a thin converging magnifier lens of focal length 0.1 m. Using the real-is-positive sign convention (1/f = 1/u + 1/v), what is the signed image distance v?
items.workedSolution: Because u = 0.08 m < f = 0.1 m, 1/v = 1/0.1 − 1/0.08 = -2.500 m⁻¹, giving a signed virtual image distance v = -0.400 m.

markScheme.criterion: Computes 1/v = 1/0.1 − 1/0.08 to obtain signed v = -0.400 m (D).

items.stem: In a wide-angle security peephole assembly, an upright test object of height 0.045 m stands 0.375 m in front of a thin diverging lens of focal length magnitude 0.25 m (f = −0.25 m in the real-is-positive convention). What is the signed image distance v?
items.workedSolution: For a diverging lens, f = −0.25 m. Using 1/f = 1/u + 1/v gives 1/v = −1/0.25 − 1/0.375 = -6.667 m⁻¹, so v = -0.150 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses negative f = −0.25 m in 1/v = 1/f − 1/u to obtain v = -0.150 m (B).

items.stem: In a structural vibration-isolation test sled on linear bearings, a 0.9 kg mass hangs from a vertical spring of constant 50 N m⁻¹ and executes vertical SHM of amplitude 0.055 m (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Calculate the static equilibrium extension Δx_eq from the spring's unstretched length.
items.workedSolution: At static equilibrium, upward spring tension balances weight: k Δx_eq = mg ⇒ Δx_eq = (0.9 × 9.81) / 50 = 0.177 m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Hooke's law as k / (mg) instead of mg / k.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Adds the oscillation amplitude x₀ to mg / k, finding maximum total stretch rather than static equilibrium extension.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides mass m directly by spring constant k without multiplying by gravitational field strength g.

items.stem: In a diesel injector needle-valve harmonic test rig, an oscillator undergoes SHM at 6 Hz with amplitude 0.05 m (passing through x = 0.0175 m). Calculate the peak acceleration magnitude a_max = (2πf)² x₀.
items.workedSolution: With ω = 2π(6) = 37.70 rad s⁻¹, maximum acceleration magnitude a_max = ω² x₀ = 71.1 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ω = 2πf and obtains 71.1 m s⁻² (A).

items.stem: In a tall-building tuned mass damper block, an oscillating body of mass 0.5 kg executes simple harmonic motion with angular frequency ω = 25 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude x₀ = 0.1 m. What is its kinetic energy E_k when its displacement from equilibrium is x = 0.05 m?
items.workedSolution: Using E_k = ½mω²(x₀² − x²) gives E_k = 0.5 × 0.5 × 25² × (0.1² − 0.05²) = 1.17 J.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes the total mechanical energy ½mω²x₀² instead of subtracting potential energy at x.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Interpolates energy linearly as E_tot(1 − x / x₀) instead of quadratically as E_tot(1 − x² / x₀²).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the potential energy ½mω²x² at x rather than the kinetic energy ½mω²(x₀² − x²).

items.stem: In a subterranean pipeline temperature-sensing cable, an optical pulse enters a 350 m step-index fiber (core index 1.49, cladding index 1.39) from air (n_ext = 1.00) at a launch angle of 14° to the axis. Calculate the incident angle θ_w on the core–cladding interface normal.
items.workedSolution: At the entry face, 1 sin 14° = 1.49 sin θ_axis ⇒ θ_axis = 9.34°. Since the core wall is parallel to the axis, its normal is perpendicular to the axis, giving θ_w = 90° − θ_axis = 80.7°.

items.stem: In a tethered deep-sea ROV umbilical waveguide, a short optical pulse enters a 1800 m step-index fiber (core index 1.55, cladding index 1.47, n_ext = 1.00, sample launch angle 11.8°). With c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, calculate the modal time delay Δt = t_max − t_axial at the output end.
items.workedSolution: Axial transit time t_min = n_core L / c = (1.55 × 1800) / (3.00 × 10⁸) = 9.30 × 10⁻⁶ s. At the critical angle sin θ_c = n_clad / n_core, t_max = t_min / sin θ_c = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 9.81 × 10⁻⁶ s. Modal delay Δt = t_max − t_min = 5.06 × 10⁻⁷ s.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δt = (n_core L / c)(n_core / n_clad − 1) = 5.06 × 10⁻⁷ s (C).

items.stem: In a subsea ROV camera viewport test, a narrow monochromatic beam (speed of light in vacuum c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) travels inside synthetic sapphire of refractive index n₁ = 1.77 and strikes a flat boundary with dry air of refractive index n₂ = 1 at an angle of incidence of 47° to the normal.
items.workedSolution: (a) sin θ_c = 1 / 1.77, so θ_c = 34.4°. (b) Because n₁ > n₂ and θ₁ > θ_c, total internal reflection occurs at the interface. (c) Wave speed v₁ = 3.00 × 10⁸ / 1.77 = 1.69 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, and angular deviation δ = 180° − 2(47°) = 86.0°.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1 / 1.77.
States total internal reflection because the ray is in the higher-index medium with incident angle greater than the critical angle.

parts.prompt: Calculate the critical angle θ_c at the synthetic sapphire–dry air boundary.
State and explain the optical phenomenon that occurs when this beam meets the boundary.
parts.expectedAnswer: Total internal reflection occurs because light travels in the medium of higher refractive index and the incident angle exceeds the critical angle.
workingSteps: Compare incident angle with critical angle in the optically denser medium to confirm total internal reflection.

parts.prompt: Calculate the angular deviation of the reflected ray from the incident ray's original forward direction, and find the wave speed in the first medium.
workingSteps: Wave speed in synthetic sapphire: v₁ = c / n₁ = 1.69 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹.
Angular deviation under total internal reflection: δ = 180° − 2(47°) = 86.0°.

items.stem: A straight 750 m step-index optical fiber in a borehole geophysical telemetry line consists of a core of refractive index n_core = 1.48 and cladding of refractive index n_clad = 1.41. Its flat input end sits in air of refractive index 1.00, and a guided test ray is launched at θ_in = 12° to the central axis.
items.workedSolution: (a) θ_c = arcsin(1.41 / 1.48) = 72.3°. (b) Using n_ext sin θ_max = √(n_core² − n_clad²) gives θ_max = 26.7°. (c) For θ_in = 12°, θ_axis = 8.08° and L_ray = 750 / cos θ_axis = 758 m.

markScheme.criterion: Applies 1 sin θ_max = n_core sin(90° − θ_c).
Finds θ_axis = 8.08° and evaluates L / cos θ_axis.

Hence calculate the maximum acceptance angle θ_max in air of refractive index 1.00 for guided total internal reflection.
workingSteps: Maximum axial angle in core = 90° − θ_c; n_ext sin θ_max = n_core cos θ_c = √(1.48² − 1.41²).

items.stem: During close inspection on a cinema slide-projector lens mount, a thin convex lens of focal length 0.15 m is positioned 0.0525 m from a fine detail of height 0.015 m. Adopt the real-is-positive sign convention throughout.
items.workedSolution: (a) 1/v = 1/0.15 − 1/0.0525 ⇒ v = -0.0808 m (virtual, since v < 0). (b) m = −v / u = 1.54. (c) Upright virtual image height h_i = m h_o = 0.0231 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes u = 0.0525 m and f = 0.15 m into 1/v = 1/f − 1/u.
Multiplies magnification m by object height h_o.

items.stem: In a frictionless air-track glider coupled to a calibrated coil spring, a 0.64 kg carriage tethered to a horizontal spring of spring constant 24 N m⁻¹ executes undamped simple harmonic motion of amplitude 0.035 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes m = 0.64 kg and k = 24 N m⁻¹ into T = 2π√(m / k).
Applies Hooke's law F_max = k x₀ = 24 × 0.035.
Divides F_max by m (or multiplies ω² by x₀).

parts.prompt: Calculate the period T of the simple harmonic oscillations.
Calculate the magnitude of the maximum restoring force F_max exerted by the spring.
Determine the magnitude of the maximum acceleration a_max of the oscillating mass.

items.stem: A simple pendulum rig in a lecture-hall rigid-ceiling wire pendulum carries a 0.4 kg sphere on a 2.4 m wire, swinging with small-angle arc amplitude 0.48 m where g = 9.81 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) T = 2π√(2.4 / 9.81) = 3.11 s. (b) v_max = √(9.81 / 2.4) × 0.48 = 0.970 m s⁻¹. (c) Lowest-point cord tension = m(g + v_max² / L) = 4.08 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies v_max = ω x₀ = (2π / T) x₀.
Uses T_cord = mg + mv_max² / L at the bottom of the arc.

parts.prompt: Calculate the period T of the pendulum.
Calculate the maximum speed v_max of the bob as it passes through equilibrium.
Determine the tension in the suspension cord as the bob passes through its lowest point.

items.stem: A 0.4 kg harmonic oscillator in a micro-electro-mechanical resonant beam vibrates with angular frequency 18 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude 0.04 m. Consider its mechanical energy distribution when passing through displacement x = 0.01 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes m = 0.4 kg, ω = 18 rad s⁻¹, and x₀ = 0.04 m into E_tot = ½mω²x₀².
Applies E_k = ½mω²(x₀² − x²) or E_tot − ½mω²x².
Sets E_p = ½E_tot to obtain x = x₀ / √2.

parts.prompt: Calculate the total mechanical energy E_tot of the oscillating mass.
Calculate the kinetic energy E_k of the mass when its displacement is x = 0.01 m.
workingSteps: E_k = E_tot − E_p = ½mω²(x₀² − x²) = 0.0972 J.

parts.prompt: Determine the positive displacement x from equilibrium at which kinetic energy equals potential energy.

items.stem: In a Galilean laser beam-expander input stage, an upright object of height h_o = 0.05 m is placed at a distance u = 0.56 m in front of a thin diverging lens whose focal length is f = −0.4 m under the real-is-positive sign convention.
items.workedSolution: (a) Optical power P = 1 / (−0.4) = -2.50 D. (b) 1/v = −1/0.4 − 1/0.56 ⇒ v = -0.233 m. (c) Axial separation between object and virtual image on the same side = u − |v| = 0.327 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes f = −0.4 m and u = 0.56 m into 1/v = 1/f − 1/u.
Subtracts |v| from u because virtual image and object are on the same side of the lens.

Calculate the signed image distance v using 1/f = 1/u + 1/v.
Determine the axial distance between the object and its virtual image.
workingSteps: Both lie on the input side of the lens, so separation = u − |v| = |u + v| = 0.327 m.

items.stem: The acceleration–displacement phase graph for a quartz crystal tuning-fork tine corresponds to simple harmonic motion of frequency 3 Hz and amplitude 0.02 m, with a measurement taken at displacement x = 0.015 m.
items.workedSolution: (a) ω = 2π(3) = 18.8 rad s⁻¹. (b) At x = 0.015 m, a = −ω²x = -5.33 m s⁻². (c) Maximum acceleration magnitude a_max = ω² x₀ = 7.11 m s⁻².

items.stem: A 80 m step-index waveguide deployed in a structural-health bridge sensor lead comprises a glass core (n_core = 1.6) surrounded by lower-index cladding (n_clad = 1.5). Monochromatic light enters from air (n_ext = 1.00) at an angle of 17.3° to the fiber axis.
items.workedSolution: (a) sin θ_c = 1.5 / 1.6 ⇒ θ_c = 69.6°. (b) By Snell's law at the end-face, sin θ_axis = (1 sin 17.3°) / 1.6, so θ_axis = 10.7°. (c) Wall incident angle θ_w = 90° − θ_axis = 79.3°, which exceeds θ_c so the ray is guided by TIR.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts θ_axis from 90° to obtain θ_w.

items.stem: A beam-steering prism assembly on a gemstone goniometer calibration rig guides light (c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) inside dense flint glass (n₁ = 1.65) toward a planar interface with dry air (n₂ = 1) at an incidence angle of 50° measured from the normal.
items.workedSolution: (a) sin θ_c = 1 / 1.65, so θ_c = 37.3°. (b) Because n₁ > n₂ and θ₁ > θ_c, total internal reflection occurs at the interface. (c) Wave speed v₁ = 3.00 × 10⁸ / 1.65 = 1.82 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, and angular deviation δ = 180° − 2(50°) = 80.0°.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1 / 1.65.
States total internal reflection because the ray is in the higher-index medium with incident angle greater than the critical angle.

Its flat input end sits in air of refractive index 1.00, and a guided test ray is launched at θ_in = 25.9° to the central axis.
items.workedSolution: (a) θ_c = arcsin(1.51 / 1.62) = 68.8°. (b) Using n_ext sin θ_max = √(n_core² − n_clad²) gives θ_max = 35.9°. (c) For θ_in = 25.9°, θ_axis = 15.6° and L_ray = 750 / cos θ_axis = 779 m.

markScheme.criterion: Applies 1 sin θ_max = n_core sin(90° − θ_c).
Finds θ_axis = 15.6° and evaluates L / cos θ_axis.

items.workedSolution: (a) Δx_eq = mg / k = (0.4 × 9.81) / 20 = 0.196 m. (b) T = 2π√(0.4 / 20) = 0.889 s. (c) Maximum net SHM acceleration a_max = (k / m) x₀ = 1.60 m s⁻².

Evaluates a_max = ω² x₀ = (k / m) x₀.

items.workedSolution: (a) ω = 2π(1.5) = 9.42 rad s⁻¹. (b) At x = 0.0135 m, a = −ω²x = -1.20 m s⁻². (c) Maximum acceleration magnitude a_max = ω² x₀ = 2.66 m s⁻².

items.workedSolution: (a) t_axial = n_core L / c = (1.5 × 900) / 3.00 × 10⁸ = 4.50 × 10⁻⁶ s. (b) Longest guided ray has path L / sin θ_c = L n_core / n_clad, giving t_max = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 4.69 × 10⁻⁶ s. (c) Modal pulse delay Δt = t_max − t_axial = 1.87 × 10⁻⁷ s.

items.stem: In an interferometric metrology window, a narrow monochromatic beam (speed of light in vacuum c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) travels inside optical diamond of refractive index n₁ = 2.42 and strikes a flat boundary with fused-silica glass of refractive index n₂ = 1.46 at an angle of incidence of 43° to the normal.
items.workedSolution: (a) sin θ_c = 1.46 / 2.42, so θ_c = 37.1°. (b) Because n₁ > n₂ and θ₁ > θ_c, total internal reflection occurs at the interface. (c) Wave speed v₁ = 3.00 × 10⁸ / 2.42 = 1.24 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, and angular deviation δ = 180° − 2(43°) = 94.0°.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1.46 / 2.42.
States total internal reflection because the ray is in the higher-index medium with incident angle greater than the critical angle.

items.stem: In a coastal lighthouse clockwork escapement pendulum, a pendulum bob of mass m = 0.15 kg suspended on a light cord of length L = 1.3 m oscillates in small-angle simple harmonic motion with arc amplitude x₀ = 0.286 m. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻².

items.stem: The acceleration–displacement phase graph for a tall-building tuned mass damper block corresponds to simple harmonic motion of frequency 4 Hz and amplitude 0.05 m, with a measurement taken at displacement x = 0.03 m.
items.workedSolution: (a) ω = 2π(4) = 25.1 rad s⁻¹. (b) At x = 0.03 m, a = −ω²x = -18.9 m s⁻². (c) Maximum acceleration magnitude a_max = ω² x₀ = 31.6 m s⁻².

items.stem: In a tethered deep-sea ROV umbilical waveguide, a straight 80 m step-index optical fiber has a core of refractive index n_core = 1.49 and a cladding of refractive index n_clad = 1.39. A narrow laser beam in air (n_ext = 1.00) strikes the flat entry face at θ_in = 16.6° to the central axis.
items.workedSolution: (a) sin θ_c = 1.39 / 1.49 ⇒ θ_c = 68.9°. (b) By Snell's law at the end-face, sin θ_axis = (1 sin 16.6°) / 1.49, so θ_axis = 11.1°. (c) Wall incident angle θ_w = 90° − θ_axis = 78.9°, which exceeds θ_c so the ray is guided by TIR.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts θ_axis from 90° to obtain θ_w.

parts.prompt: Determine the angle of incidence θ_w of this ray on the core–cladding wall normal, confirming that total internal reflection occurs.

items.stem: An experimental arrangement of a university mechanics oscillation sled comprises a block of mass m = 0.8 kg attached to an ideal horizontal spring of stiffness k = 56 N m⁻¹. The block oscillates in simple harmonic motion with amplitude x₀ = 0.09 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes m = 0.8 kg and k = 56 N m⁻¹ into T = 2π√(m / k).
Applies Hooke's law F_max = k x₀ = 56 × 0.09.
Divides F_max by m (or multiplies ω² by x₀).

parts.prompt: Calculate the period T of the simple harmonic oscillations.
Calculate the magnitude of the maximum restoring force F_max exerted by the spring.
Determine the magnitude of the maximum acceleration a_max of the oscillating mass.

items.stem: In a magnetic-levitation harmonic test puck, a resonant element executes simple harmonic motion with angular frequency ω = 12 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude x₀ = 0.12 m, as depicted by its velocity–displacement phase ellipse. Measurements are taken when the displacement is x = 0.06 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses T = 2π / ω with ω = 12 rad s⁻¹.
Substitutes x₀ = 0.12 m and x = 0.06 m into v = ω√(x₀² − x²).

items.stem: A beam-steering prism assembly on a deep-ocean optical hydrophone window guides light (c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) inside optical crown glass (n₁ = 1.52) toward a planar interface with dry air (n₂ = 1) at an incidence angle of 47° measured from the normal.
items.workedSolution: (a) sin θ_c = 1 / 1.52, so θ_c = 41.1°. (b) Because n₁ > n₂ and θ₁ > θ_c, total internal reflection occurs at the interface. (c) Wave speed v₁ = 3.00 × 10⁸ / 1.52 = 1.97 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, and angular deviation δ = 180° − 2(47°) = 86.0°.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1 / 1.52.
States total internal reflection because the ray is in the higher-index medium with incident angle greater than the critical angle.

parts.prompt: Calculate the critical angle θ_c at the optical crown glass–dry air boundary.
State and explain the optical phenomenon that occurs when this beam meets the boundary.
parts.expectedAnswer: Total internal reflection occurs because light travels in the medium of higher refractive index and the incident angle exceeds the critical angle.
workingSteps: Compare incident angle with critical angle in the optically denser medium to confirm total internal reflection.

parts.prompt: Calculate the angular deviation of the reflected ray from the incident ray's original forward direction, and find the wave speed in the first medium.
workingSteps: Wave speed in optical crown glass: v₁ = c / n₁ = 1.97 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹.
Angular deviation under total internal reflection: δ = 180° − 2(47°) = 86.0°.

items.stem: Engineers characterizing a fusion-chamber diagnostic optical relay couple a laser beam from water of refractive index 1.33 at 8.3° to the axis into a straight 750 m step-index waveguide (core index 1.52, cladding index 1.46).
items.workedSolution: (a) θ_c = arcsin(1.46 / 1.52) = 73.8°. (b) Using n_ext sin θ_max = √(n_core² − n_clad²) gives θ_max = 18.5°. (c) For θ_in = 8.3°, θ_axis = 7.26° and L_ray = 750 / cos θ_axis = 756 m.

markScheme.criterion: Applies 1.33 sin θ_max = n_core sin(90° − θ_c).
Finds θ_axis = 7.26° and evaluates L / cos θ_axis.

items.stem: In a watchmaker's horological inspection stand, an upright object of height h_o = 0.012 m is held at a distance u = 0.17 m in front of a thin converging magnifying lens of focal length f = 0.25 m. Use the real-is-positive sign convention (1/f = 1/u + 1/v, m = −v/u).
items.workedSolution: (a) 1/v = 1/0.25 − 1/0.17 ⇒ v = -0.531 m (virtual, since v < 0). (b) m = −v / u = 3.13. (c) Upright virtual image height h_i = m h_o = 0.0375 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes u = 0.17 m and f = 0.25 m into 1/v = 1/f − 1/u.
Multiplies magnification m by object height h_o.

items.stem: A vertical suspension stage in a precision watch hairspring linear test bench supports a 0.3 kg mass on an ideal coil spring of stiffness 25 N m⁻¹, oscillating vertically with amplitude 0.024 m about its equilibrium position (take g = 9.8 m s⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) Δx_eq = mg / k = (0.3 × 9.8) / 25 = 0.118 m. (b) T = 2π√(0.3 / 25) = 0.688 s. (c) Maximum net SHM acceleration a_max = (k / m) x₀ = 2.00 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Uses mg = k Δx_eq with g = 9.8 m s⁻².
Evaluates a_max = ω² x₀ = (k / m) x₀.

parts.prompt: Calculate the static extension Δx_eq of the spring when the mass hangs at rest in equilibrium.
Calculate the period T of the vertical simple harmonic oscillations.
Determine the magnitude of the maximum net acceleration a_max of the mass during the oscillation.

items.stem: A simple pendulum rig in a long-case regulator clock calibration rig carries a 0.5 kg sphere on a 0.85 m wire, swinging with small-angle arc amplitude 0.187 m where g = 9.81 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Applies v_max = ω x₀ = (2π / T) x₀.
Uses T_cord = mg + mv_max² / L at the bottom of the arc.

parts.prompt: Calculate the period T of the pendulum.
Calculate the maximum speed v_max of the bob as it passes through equilibrium.
Determine the tension in the suspension cord as the bob passes through its lowest point.

items.stem: A 0.4 kg harmonic oscillator in a violins bridge laser-Doppler vibration target vibrates with angular frequency 10 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude 0.1 m. Consider its mechanical energy distribution when passing through displacement x = 0.08 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes m = 0.4 kg, ω = 10 rad s⁻¹, and x₀ = 0.1 m into E_tot = ½mω²x₀².
Applies E_k = ½mω²(x₀² − x²) or E_tot − ½mω²x².
Sets E_p = ½E_tot to obtain x = x₀ / √2.

parts.prompt: Calculate the total mechanical energy E_tot of the oscillating mass.
Calculate the kinetic energy E_k of the mass when its displacement is x = 0.08 m.
workingSteps: E_k = E_tot − E_p = ½mω²(x₀² − x²) = 0.0720 J.

parts.prompt: Determine the positive displacement x from equilibrium at which kinetic energy equals potential energy.

items.stem: During pulse-broadening tests for a transoceanic telecommunications link, engineers transmit narrow laser pulses from air (n_ext = 1.00, sample launch angle 15.9°) along a 150 m step-index fiber of core index 1.58 and cladding index 1.49. Take c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) t_axial = n_core L / c = (1.58 × 150) / 3.00 × 10⁸ = 7.90 × 10⁻⁷ s. (b) Longest guided ray has path L / sin θ_c = L n_core / n_clad, giving t_max = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 8.38 × 10⁻⁷ s. (c) Modal pulse delay Δt = t_max − t_axial = 4.77 × 10⁻⁸ s.

markScheme.criterion: Uses t_axial = n_core L / c with n_core = 1.58 and L = 150 m.
Applies L_max = L (n_core / n_clad) to find t_max = t_axial (n_core / n_clad).

items.stem: In a precision optical-power dioptre verification bench, an upright object of height h_o = 0.045 m is placed at a distance u = 0.27 m in front of a thin diverging lens whose focal length is f = −0.15 m under the real-is-positive sign convention.
items.workedSolution: (a) Optical power P = 1 / (−0.15) = -6.67 D. (b) 1/v = −1/0.15 − 1/0.27 ⇒ v = -0.0964 m. (c) Axial separation between object and virtual image on the same side = u − |v| = 0.174 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes f = −0.15 m and u = 0.27 m into 1/v = 1/f − 1/u.
Subtracts |v| from u because virtual image and object are on the same side of the lens.

parts.prompt: Calculate the signed optical power P = 1/f of the diverging lens in dioptres (D).
Calculate the signed image distance v using 1/f = 1/u + 1/v.
Determine the axial distance between the object and its virtual image.
workingSteps: Both lie on the input side of the lens, so separation = u − |v| = |u + v| = 0.174 m.

items.stem: A precision oscillator in a resonant Coriolis mass-flow sensor tube undergoes simple harmonic motion of amplitude 0.1 m and angular frequency 20 rad s⁻¹. Consider the instant when its displacement from equilibrium is 0.028 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses T = 2π / ω with ω = 20 rad s⁻¹.
Substitutes x₀ = 0.1 m and x = 0.028 m into v = ω√(x₀² − x²).

items.stem: An experimental arrangement of an acoustic transducer moving-coil suspension rig comprises a block of mass m = 0.36 kg attached to an ideal horizontal spring of stiffness k = 18 N m⁻¹. The block oscillates in simple harmonic motion with amplitude x₀ = 0.025 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes m = 0.36 kg and k = 18 N m⁻¹ into T = 2π√(m / k).
Applies Hooke's law F_max = k x₀ = 18 × 0.025.
Divides F_max by m (or multiplies ω² by x₀).

parts.prompt: Calculate the period T of the simple harmonic oscillations.
Calculate the magnitude of the maximum restoring force F_max exerted by the spring.
Determine the magnitude of the maximum acceleration a_max of the oscillating mass.

items.stem: A simple pendulum rig in a Foucault-style brass sphere suspension apparatus carries a 0.25 kg sphere on a 2.4 m wire, swinging with small-angle arc amplitude 0.528 m where g = 9.81 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) T = 2π√(2.4 / 9.81) = 3.11 s. (b) v_max = √(9.81 / 2.4) × 0.528 = 1.07 m s⁻¹. (c) Lowest-point cord tension = m(g + v_max² / L) = 2.57 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies v_max = ω x₀ = (2π / T) x₀.
Uses T_cord = mg + mv_max² / L at the bottom of the arc.

parts.prompt: Calculate the period T of the pendulum.
Calculate the maximum speed v_max of the bob as it passes through equilibrium.
Determine the tension in the suspension cord as the bob passes through its lowest point.

items.stem: In a quartz crystal tuning-fork tine, a mass m = 0.15 kg oscillates in undamped simple harmonic motion with angular frequency ω = 30 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude x₀ = 0.14 m. The parabolic energy–displacement curves are analyzed at displacement x = 0.035 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes m = 0.15 kg, ω = 30 rad s⁻¹, and x₀ = 0.14 m into E_tot = ½mω²x₀².
Applies E_k = ½mω²(x₀² − x²) or E_tot − ½mω²x².
Sets E_p = ½E_tot to obtain x = x₀ / √2.

parts.prompt: Calculate the total mechanical energy E_tot of the oscillating mass.
Calculate the kinetic energy E_k of the mass when its displacement is x = 0.035 m.
workingSteps: E_k = E_tot − E_p = ½mω²(x₀² − x²) = 1.24 J.

parts.prompt: Determine the positive displacement x from equilibrium at which kinetic energy equals potential energy.

items.stem: In a clinical corneal pachymetry test phantom, a narrow monochromatic beam (speed of light in vacuum c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) travels inside polycarbonate polymer of refractive index n₁ = 1.58 and strikes a flat boundary with distilled water of refractive index n₂ = 1.33 at an angle of incidence of 63° to the normal.
items.workedSolution: (a) sin θ_c = 1.33 / 1.58, so θ_c = 57.3°. (b) Because n₁ > n₂ and θ₁ > θ_c, total internal reflection occurs at the interface. (c) Wave speed v₁ = 3.00 × 10⁸ / 1.58 = 1.90 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, and angular deviation δ = 180° − 2(63°) = 54.0°.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1.33 / 1.58.
States total internal reflection because the ray is in the higher-index medium with incident angle greater than the critical angle.

State and explain the optical phenomenon that occurs when this beam meets the boundary.
parts.expectedAnswer: Total internal reflection occurs because light travels in the medium of higher refractive index and the incident angle exceeds the critical angle.
workingSteps: Compare incident angle with critical angle in the optically denser medium to confirm total internal reflection.

parts.prompt: Calculate the angular deviation of the reflected ray from the incident ray's original forward direction, and find the wave speed in the first medium.
workingSteps: Wave speed in polycarbonate polymer: v₁ = c / n₁ = 1.90 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹.
Angular deviation under total internal reflection: δ = 180° − 2(63°) = 54.0°.

items.stem: A straight 750 m step-index optical fiber in a subterranean pipeline temperature-sensing cable consists of a core of refractive index n_core = 1.6 and cladding of refractive index n_clad = 1.5. Its flat input end sits in water of refractive index 1.33, and a guided test ray is launched at θ_in = 17.8° to the central axis.
items.workedSolution: (a) θ_c = arcsin(1.5 / 1.6) = 69.6°. (b) Using n_ext sin θ_max = √(n_core² − n_clad²) gives θ_max = 24.7°. (c) For θ_in = 17.8°, θ_axis = 14.7° and L_ray = 750 / cos θ_axis = 775 m.

markScheme.criterion: Applies 1.33 sin θ_max = n_core sin(90° − θ_c).
Finds θ_axis = 14.7° and evaluates L / cos θ_axis.

items.stem: During close inspection on a forensic macro-photography stage, a thin convex lens of focal length 0.1 m is positioned 0.035 m from a fine detail of height 0.008 m. Adopt the real-is-positive sign convention throughout.

items.stem: In an undergraduate ray-box bench, a narrow monochromatic beam (speed of light in vacuum c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) travels inside dense flint glass of refractive index n₁ = 1.65 and strikes a flat boundary with fused-silica glass of refractive index n₂ = 1.46 at an angle of incidence of 71° to the normal.
items.workedSolution: (a) sin θ_c = 1.46 / 1.65, so θ_c = 62.2°. (b) Because n₁ > n₂ and θ₁ > θ_c, total internal reflection occurs at the interface. (c) Wave speed v₁ = 3.00 × 10⁸ / 1.65 = 1.82 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, and angular deviation δ = 180° − 2(71°) = 38.0°.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1.46 / 1.65.
States total internal reflection because the ray is in the higher-index medium with incident angle greater than the critical angle.

items.workedSolution: (a) T = 2π√(1.9 / 9.81) = 2.77 s. (b) v_max = √(9.81 / 1.9) × 0.475 = 1.08 m s⁻¹. (c) Lowest-point cord tension = m(g + v_max² / L) = 5.21 N.

items.stem: In a precision marine-chronometer balance-mass rig, a load of mass m = 0.5 kg hangs at rest from a vertical spring of spring constant k = 25 N m⁻¹. It is then pulled vertically downward by x₀ = 0.032 m from equilibrium and released. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Δx_eq = mg / k = (0.5 × 9.8) / 25 = 0.196 m. (b) T = 2π√(0.5 / 25) = 0.889 s. (c) Maximum net SHM acceleration a_max = (k / m) x₀ = 1.60 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Uses mg = k Δx_eq with g = 9.8 m s⁻².
Evaluates a_max = ω² x₀ = (k / m) x₀.

items.workedSolution: (a) sin θ_c = 1.51 / 1.62 ⇒ θ_c = 68.8°. (b) By Snell's law at the end-face, sin θ_axis = (1 sin 12.6°) / 1.62, so θ_axis = 7.74°. (c) Wall incident angle θ_w = 90° − θ_axis = 82.3°, which exceeds θ_c so the ray is guided by TIR.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts θ_axis from 90° to obtain θ_w.

items.stem: In a seismic base-isolation pendulum test frame, a pendulum bob of mass m = 0.6 kg suspended on a light cord of length L = 1.9 m oscillates in small-angle simple harmonic motion with arc amplitude x₀ = 0.532 m. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) T = 2π√(1.9 / 9.81) = 2.77 s. (b) v_max = √(9.81 / 1.9) × 0.532 = 1.21 m s⁻¹. (c) Lowest-point cord tension = m(g + v_max² / L) = 6.35 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies v_max = ω x₀ = (2π / T) x₀.
Uses T_cord = mg + mv_max² / L at the bottom of the arc.

items.stem: In a spectrophotometer cuvette wall, a narrow monochromatic beam (speed of light in vacuum c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) travels inside synthetic sapphire of refractive index n₁ = 1.77 and strikes a flat boundary with distilled water of refractive index n₂ = 1.33 at an angle of incidence of 65° to the normal.
items.workedSolution: (a) sin θ_c = 1.33 / 1.77, so θ_c = 48.7°. (b) Because n₁ > n₂ and θ₁ > θ_c, total internal reflection occurs at the interface. (c) Wave speed v₁ = 3.00 × 10⁸ / 1.77 = 1.69 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, and angular deviation δ = 180° − 2(65°) = 50.0°.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1.33 / 1.77.
States total internal reflection because the ray is in the higher-index medium with incident angle greater than the critical angle.

items.stem: A beam-steering prism assembly on a microfluidic refractive-index sensor guides light (c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) inside dense flint glass (n₁ = 1.65) toward a planar interface with fused-silica glass (n₂ = 1.46) at an incidence angle of 79° measured from the normal.
items.workedSolution: (a) sin θ_c = 1.46 / 1.65, so θ_c = 62.2°. (b) Because n₁ > n₂ and θ₁ > θ_c, total internal reflection occurs at the interface. (c) Wave speed v₁ = 3.00 × 10⁸ / 1.65 = 1.82 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, and angular deviation δ = 180° − 2(79°) = 22.0°.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1.46 / 1.65.
States total internal reflection because the ray is in the higher-index medium with incident angle greater than the critical angle.

Evaluates a_max = ω² x₀ = (k / m) x₀.

items.stem: A beam-steering prism assembly on a subsea ROV camera viewport test guides light (c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) inside synthetic sapphire (n₁ = 1.77) toward a planar interface with liquid ethanol (n₂ = 1.36) at an incidence angle of 63° measured from the normal.
items.workedSolution: (a) sin θ_c = 1.36 / 1.77, so θ_c = 50.2°. (b) Because n₁ > n₂ and θ₁ > θ_c, total internal reflection occurs at the interface. (c) Wave speed v₁ = 3.00 × 10⁸ / 1.77 = 1.69 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, and angular deviation δ = 180° − 2(63°) = 54.0°.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1.36 / 1.77.
States total internal reflection because the ray is in the higher-index medium with incident angle greater than the critical angle.

items.stem: A straight 60 m step-index optical fiber in a borehole geophysical telemetry line consists of a core of refractive index n_core = 1.48 and cladding of refractive index n_clad = 1.41. Its flat input end sits in air of refractive index 1.00, and a guided test ray is launched at θ_in = 12° to the central axis.
items.workedSolution: (a) θ_c = arcsin(1.41 / 1.48) = 72.3°. (b) Using n_ext sin θ_max = √(n_core² − n_clad²) gives θ_max = 26.7°. (c) For θ_in = 12°, θ_axis = 8.08° and L_ray = 60 / cos θ_axis = 60.6 m.

markScheme.criterion: Applies 1 sin θ_max = n_core sin(90° − θ_c).
Finds θ_axis = 8.08° and evaluates L / cos θ_axis.

Hence calculate the maximum acceptance angle θ_max in air of refractive index 1.00 for guided total internal reflection.
workingSteps: Maximum axial angle in core = 90° − θ_c; n_ext sin θ_max = n_core cos θ_c = √(1.48² − 1.41²).

parts.prompt: Calculate the total geometric path length travelled inside the core by the ray launched at 12°.

items.stem: In a cinema slide-projector lens mount, an upright object of height h_o = 0.012 m is held at a distance u = 0.028 m in front of a thin converging magnifying lens of focal length f = 0.08 m. Use the real-is-positive sign convention (1/f = 1/u + 1/v, m = −v/u).
items.workedSolution: (a) 1/v = 1/0.08 − 1/0.028 ⇒ v = -0.0431 m (virtual, since v < 0). (b) m = −v / u = 1.54. (c) Upright virtual image height h_i = m h_o = 0.0185 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes u = 0.028 m and f = 0.08 m into 1/v = 1/f − 1/u.
Multiplies magnification m by object height h_o.

parts.prompt: Calculate the signed image distance v and hence state why the image is virtual.
workingSteps: v = -0.0431 m (negative v indicates a virtual image on the object side).

parts.prompt: Calculate the linear magnification m = −v / u of the virtual image.
Determine the height h_i of the upright virtual image.

items.stem: An experimental arrangement of a frictionless air-track glider coupled to a calibrated coil spring comprises a block of mass m = 0.25 kg attached to an ideal horizontal spring of stiffness k = 14 N m⁻¹. The block oscillates in simple harmonic motion with amplitude x₀ = 0.09 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes m = 0.25 kg and k = 14 N m⁻¹ into T = 2π√(m / k).
Applies Hooke's law F_max = k x₀ = 14 × 0.09.
Divides F_max by m (or multiplies ω² by x₀).

parts.prompt: Calculate the period T of the simple harmonic oscillations.
Calculate the magnitude of the maximum restoring force F_max exerted by the spring.
Determine the magnitude of the maximum acceleration a_max of the oscillating mass.

items.stem: In a lecture-hall rigid-ceiling wire pendulum, a pendulum bob of mass m = 0.6 kg suspended on a light cord of length L = 1.9 m oscillates in small-angle simple harmonic motion with arc amplitude x₀ = 0.532 m. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) T = 2π√(1.9 / 9.81) = 2.77 s. (b) v_max = √(9.81 / 1.9) × 0.532 = 1.21 m s⁻¹. (c) Lowest-point cord tension = m(g + v_max² / L) = 6.35 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies v_max = ω x₀ = (2π / T) x₀.
Uses T_cord = mg + mv_max² / L at the bottom of the arc.

parts.prompt: Calculate the period T of the pendulum.
Calculate the maximum speed v_max of the bob as it passes through equilibrium.
Determine the tension in the suspension cord as the bob passes through its lowest point.

items.stem: In a micro-electro-mechanical resonant beam, a mass m = 0.6 kg oscillates in undamped simple harmonic motion with angular frequency ω = 25 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude x₀ = 0.04 m. The parabolic energy–displacement curves are analyzed at displacement x = 0.02 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes m = 0.6 kg, ω = 25 rad s⁻¹, and x₀ = 0.04 m into E_tot = ½mω²x₀².
Applies E_k = ½mω²(x₀² − x²) or E_tot − ½mω²x².
Sets E_p = ½E_tot to obtain x = x₀ / √2.

parts.prompt: Calculate the total mechanical energy E_tot of the oscillating mass.
Calculate the kinetic energy E_k of the mass when its displacement is x = 0.02 m.
workingSteps: E_k = E_tot − E_p = ½mω²(x₀² − x²) = 0.225 J.

parts.prompt: Determine the positive displacement x from equilibrium at which kinetic energy equals potential energy.

items.stem: During pulse-broadening tests for a high-voltage substation optical isolator link, engineers transmit narrow laser pulses from air (n_ext = 1.00, sample launch angle 16.2°) along a 1800 m step-index fiber of core index 1.49 and cladding index 1.39. Take c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) t_axial = n_core L / c = (1.49 × 1800) / 3.00 × 10⁸ = 8.94 × 10⁻⁶ s. (b) Longest guided ray has path L / sin θ_c = L n_core / n_clad, giving t_max = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 9.58 × 10⁻⁶ s. (c) Modal pulse delay Δt = t_max − t_axial = 6.43 × 10⁻⁷ s.

markScheme.criterion: Uses t_axial = n_core L / c with n_core = 1.49 and L = 1800 m.
Applies L_max = L (n_core / n_clad) to find t_max = t_axial (n_core / n_clad).

Calculate the transit time t_max of the slowest guided ray that strikes the core–cladding boundary just above the critical angle.
workingSteps: sin θ_c = n_clad / n_core = 1.39 / 1.49, so L_max = L / sin θ_c = L (n_core / n_clad).

parts.prompt: Determine the maximum multipath (modal) pulse broadening Δt over this fiber length.

items.stem: In a Galilean laser beam-expander input stage, an upright object of height h_o = 0.02 m is placed at a distance u = 0.08 m in front of a thin diverging lens whose focal length is f = −0.1 m under the real-is-positive sign convention.
items.workedSolution: (a) Optical power P = 1 / (−0.1) = -10.0 D. (b) 1/v = −1/0.1 − 1/0.08 ⇒ v = -0.0444 m. (c) Axial separation between object and virtual image on the same side = u − |v| = 0.0356 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes f = −0.1 m and u = 0.08 m into 1/v = 1/f − 1/u.
Subtracts |v| from u because virtual image and object are on the same side of the lens.

items.stem: The acceleration–displacement phase graph for a quartz crystal tuning-fork tine corresponds to simple harmonic motion of frequency 2.5 Hz and amplitude 0.02 m, with a measurement taken at displacement x = 0.012 m.
items.workedSolution: (a) ω = 2π(2.5) = 15.7 rad s⁻¹. (b) At x = 0.012 m, a = −ω²x = -2.96 m s⁻². (c) Maximum acceleration magnitude a_max = ω² x₀ = 4.93 m s⁻².

items.stem: In a gemstone goniometer calibration rig, a narrow monochromatic beam (speed of light in vacuum c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) travels inside dense flint glass of refractive index n₁ = 1.65 and strikes a flat boundary with liquid ethanol of refractive index n₂ = 1.36 at an angle of incidence of 72° to the normal.
items.workedSolution: (a) sin θ_c = 1.36 / 1.65, so θ_c = 55.5°. (b) Because n₁ > n₂ and θ₁ > θ_c, total internal reflection occurs at the interface. (c) Wave speed v₁ = 3.00 × 10⁸ / 1.65 = 1.82 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, and angular deviation δ = 180° − 2(72°) = 36.0°.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1.36 / 1.65.
States total internal reflection because the ray is in the higher-index medium with incident angle greater than the critical angle.

items.workedSolution: (a) Optical power P = 1 / (−0.2) = -5.00 D. (b) 1/v = −1/0.2 − 1/0.36 ⇒ v = -0.129 m. (c) Axial separation between object and virtual image on the same side = u − |v| = 0.231 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes f = −0.2 m and u = 0.36 m into 1/v = 1/f − 1/u.
Subtracts |v| from u because virtual image and object are on the same side of the lens.

Calculate the signed image distance v using 1/f = 1/u + 1/v.
Determine the axial distance between the object and its virtual image.
workingSteps: Both lie on the input side of the lens, so separation = u − |v| = |u + v| = 0.231 m.

items.stem: In a micro-electro-mechanical resonant beam, a resonant element executes simple harmonic motion with angular frequency ω = 15 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude x₀ = 0.05 m, as depicted by its velocity–displacement phase ellipse. Measurements are taken when the displacement is x = 0.018 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses T = 2π / ω with ω = 15 rad s⁻¹.
Substitutes x₀ = 0.05 m and x = 0.018 m into v = ω√(x₀² − x²).

items.stem: A beam-steering prism assembly on an interferometric metrology window guides light (c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) inside dense flint glass (n₁ = 1.65) toward a planar interface with distilled water (n₂ = 1.33) at an incidence angle of 62° measured from the normal.
items.workedSolution: (a) sin θ_c = 1.33 / 1.65, so θ_c = 53.7°. (b) Because n₁ > n₂ and θ₁ > θ_c, total internal reflection occurs at the interface. (c) Wave speed v₁ = 3.00 × 10⁸ / 1.65 = 1.82 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, and angular deviation δ = 180° − 2(62°) = 56.0°.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1.33 / 1.65.
States total internal reflection because the ray is in the higher-index medium with incident angle greater than the critical angle.

parts.prompt: Calculate the critical angle θ_c at the dense flint glass–distilled water boundary.
State and explain the optical phenomenon that occurs when this beam meets the boundary.
parts.expectedAnswer: Total internal reflection occurs because light travels in the medium of higher refractive index and the incident angle exceeds the critical angle.
workingSteps: Compare incident angle with critical angle in the optically denser medium to confirm total internal reflection.

parts.prompt: Calculate the angular deviation of the reflected ray from the incident ray's original forward direction, and find the wave speed in the first medium.
workingSteps: Wave speed in dense flint glass: v₁ = c / n₁ = 1.82 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹.
Angular deviation under total internal reflection: δ = 180° − 2(62°) = 56.0°.

items.stem: Engineers characterizing a railway trackside acoustic-sensing fiber couple a laser beam from water of refractive index 1.33 at 12.4° to the axis into a straight 450 m step-index waveguide (core index 1.54, cladding index 1.45).
items.workedSolution: (a) θ_c = arcsin(1.45 / 1.54) = 70.3°. (b) Using n_ext sin θ_max = √(n_core² − n_clad²) gives θ_max = 23.0°. (c) For θ_in = 12.4°, θ_axis = 10.7° and L_ray = 450 / cos θ_axis = 458 m.

markScheme.criterion: Applies 1.33 sin θ_max = n_core sin(90° − θ_c).
Finds θ_axis = 10.7° and evaluates L / cos θ_axis.

Hence calculate the maximum acceptance angle θ_max in water of refractive index 1.33 for guided total internal reflection.
workingSteps: Maximum axial angle in core = 90° − θ_c; n_ext sin θ_max = n_core cos θ_c = √(1.54² − 1.45²).

items.stem: An experimental arrangement of an inertial seismometer calibration trolley comprises a block of mass m = 1.5 kg attached to an ideal horizontal spring of stiffness k = 45 N m⁻¹. The block oscillates in simple harmonic motion with amplitude x₀ = 0.11 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes m = 1.5 kg and k = 45 N m⁻¹ into T = 2π√(m / k).
Applies Hooke's law F_max = k x₀ = 45 × 0.11.
Divides F_max by m (or multiplies ω² by x₀).

parts.prompt: Calculate the period T of the simple harmonic oscillations.
Calculate the magnitude of the maximum restoring force F_max exerted by the spring.
Determine the magnitude of the maximum acceleration a_max of the oscillating mass.

items.stem: A simple pendulum rig in a coastal lighthouse clockwork escapement pendulum carries a 0.25 kg sphere on a 0.85 m wire, swinging with small-angle arc amplitude 0.238 m where g = 9.81 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Applies v_max = ω x₀ = (2π / T) x₀.
Uses T_cord = mg + mv_max² / L at the bottom of the arc.

parts.prompt: Calculate the period T of the pendulum.
Calculate the maximum speed v_max of the bob as it passes through equilibrium.
Determine the tension in the suspension cord as the bob passes through its lowest point.

items.stem: In a resonant Coriolis mass-flow sensor tube, a mass m = 0.6 kg oscillates in undamped simple harmonic motion with angular frequency ω = 20 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude x₀ = 0.06 m. The parabolic energy–displacement curves are analyzed at displacement x = 0.03 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes m = 0.6 kg, ω = 20 rad s⁻¹, and x₀ = 0.06 m into E_tot = ½mω²x₀².
Applies E_k = ½mω²(x₀² − x²) or E_tot − ½mω²x².
Sets E_p = ½E_tot to obtain x = x₀ / √2.

parts.prompt: Calculate the total mechanical energy E_tot of the oscillating mass.
Calculate the kinetic energy E_k of the mass when its displacement is x = 0.03 m.
workingSteps: E_k = E_tot − E_p = ½mω²(x₀² − x²) = 0.324 J.

parts.prompt: Determine the positive displacement x from equilibrium at which kinetic energy equals potential energy.

items.stem: During pulse-broadening tests for a surgical laser-lithotripsy delivery fiber, engineers transmit narrow laser pulses from air (n_ext = 1.00, sample launch angle 17.7°) along a 1800 m step-index fiber of core index 1.55 and cladding index 1.47. Take c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) t_axial = n_core L / c = (1.55 × 1800) / 3.00 × 10⁸ = 9.30 × 10⁻⁶ s. (b) Longest guided ray has path L / sin θ_c = L n_core / n_clad, giving t_max = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 9.81 × 10⁻⁶ s. (c) Modal pulse delay Δt = t_max − t_axial = 5.06 × 10⁻⁷ s.

markScheme.criterion: Uses t_axial = n_core L / c with n_core = 1.55 and L = 1800 m.
Applies L_max = L (n_core / n_clad) to find t_max = t_axial (n_core / n_clad).

items.stem: In an aerial reconnaissance camera test collimator, an upright object of height h_o = 0.022 m is held at a distance u = 0.1 m in front of a thin converging magnifying lens of focal length f = 0.25 m. Use the real-is-positive sign convention (1/f = 1/u + 1/v, m = −v/u).
items.workedSolution: (a) 1/v = 1/0.25 − 1/0.1 ⇒ v = -0.167 m (virtual, since v < 0). (b) m = −v / u = 1.67. (c) Upright virtual image height h_i = m h_o = 0.0367 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes u = 0.1 m and f = 0.25 m into 1/v = 1/f − 1/u.
Multiplies magnification m by object height h_o.

items.stem: A beam-steering prism assembly on a deep-ocean optical hydrophone window guides light (c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) inside optical diamond (n₁ = 2.42) toward a planar interface with liquid ethanol (n₂ = 1.36) at an incidence angle of 43° measured from the normal.
items.workedSolution: (a) sin θ_c = 1.36 / 2.42, so θ_c = 34.2°. (b) Because n₁ > n₂ and θ₁ > θ_c, total internal reflection occurs at the interface. (c) Wave speed v₁ = 3.00 × 10⁸ / 2.42 = 1.24 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, and angular deviation δ = 180° − 2(43°) = 94.0°.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1.36 / 2.42.
States total internal reflection because the ray is in the higher-index medium with incident angle greater than the critical angle.

items.stem: In a long-case regulator clock calibration rig, a pendulum bob of mass m = 0.4 kg suspended on a light cord of length L = 2.4 m oscillates in small-angle simple harmonic motion with arc amplitude x₀ = 0.48 m. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) T = 2π√(2.4 / 9.81) = 3.11 s. (b) v_max = √(9.81 / 2.4) × 0.48 = 0.970 m s⁻¹. (c) Lowest-point cord tension = m(g + v_max² / L) = 4.08 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies v_max = ω x₀ = (2π / T) x₀.

items.stem: A 0.4 kg harmonic oscillator in a violins bridge laser-Doppler vibration target vibrates with angular frequency 18 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude 0.08 m. Consider its mechanical energy distribution when passing through displacement x = 0.02 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes m = 0.4 kg, ω = 18 rad s⁻¹, and x₀ = 0.08 m into E_tot = ½mω²x₀².

items.stem: In a clinical corneal pachymetry test phantom, a narrow monochromatic beam (speed of light in vacuum c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) travels inside polycarbonate polymer of refractive index n₁ = 1.58 and strikes a flat boundary with dry air of refractive index n₂ = 1 at an angle of incidence of 52° to the normal.
items.workedSolution: (a) sin θ_c = 1 / 1.58, so θ_c = 39.3°. (b) Because n₁ > n₂ and θ₁ > θ_c, total internal reflection occurs at the interface. (c) Wave speed v₁ = 3.00 × 10⁸ / 1.58 = 1.90 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, and angular deviation δ = 180° − 2(52°) = 76.0°.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1 / 1.58.
States total internal reflection because the ray is in the higher-index medium with incident angle greater than the critical angle.

items.stem: In an earthquake shake-table Tuned spring sled, a load of mass m = 0.5 kg hangs at rest from a vertical spring of spring constant k = 20 N m⁻¹. It is then pulled vertically downward by x₀ = 0.055 m from equilibrium and released. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Δx_eq = mg / k = (0.5 × 9.81) / 20 = 0.245 m. (b) T = 2π√(0.5 / 20) = 0.993 s. (c) Maximum net SHM acceleration a_max = (k / m) x₀ = 2.20 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Uses mg = k Δx_eq with g = 9.81 m s⁻².
Evaluates a_max = ω² x₀ = (k / m) x₀.
