items.stem: The acceleration–displacement phase graph for a magnetic-levitation harmonic test puck corresponds to simple harmonic motion of frequency 6 Hz and amplitude 0.08 m, with a measurement taken at displacement x = -0.036 m.
items.workedSolution: (a) ω = 2π(6) = 37.7 rad s⁻¹. (b) At x = -0.036 m, a = −ω²x = 51.2 m s⁻². (c) Maximum acceleration magnitude a_max = ω² x₀ = 114 m s⁻².

items.stem: A 80 m step-index waveguide deployed in a wind-turbine blade strain-monitoring waveguide comprises a glass core (n_core = 1.6) surrounded by lower-index cladding (n_clad = 1.5). Monochromatic light enters from air (n_ext = 1.00) at an angle of 17.3° to the fiber axis.
items.workedSolution: (a) sin θ_c = 1.5 / 1.6 ⇒ θ_c = 69.6°. (b) By Snell's law at the end-face, sin θ_axis = (1 sin 17.3°) / 1.6, so θ_axis = 10.7°. (c) Wall incident angle θ_w = 90° − θ_axis = 79.3°, which exceeds θ_c so the ray is guided by TIR.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts θ_axis from 90° to obtain θ_w.

items.stem: During pulse-broadening tests for an industrial laser-welding delivery cable, engineers transmit narrow laser pulses from air (n_ext = 1.00, sample launch angle 12.5°) along a 360 m step-index fiber of core index 1.54 and cladding index 1.45. Take c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) t_axial = n_core L / c = (1.54 × 360) / 3.00 × 10⁸ = 1.85 × 10⁻⁶ s. (b) Longest guided ray has path L / sin θ_c = L n_core / n_clad, giving t_max = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 1.96 × 10⁻⁶ s. (c) Modal pulse delay Δt = t_max − t_axial = 1.15 × 10⁻⁷ s.

markScheme.criterion: Uses t_axial = n_core L / c with n_core = 1.54 and L = 360 m.
Applies L_max = L (n_core / n_clad) to find t_max = t_axial (n_core / n_clad).

items.stem: A beam-steering prism assembly on an undergraduate ray-box bench guides light (c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) inside synthetic sapphire (n₁ = 1.77) toward a planar interface with fused-silica glass (n₂ = 1.46) at an incidence angle of 72° measured from the normal.
items.workedSolution: (a) sin θ_c = 1.46 / 1.77, so θ_c = 55.6°. (b) Because n₁ > n₂ and θ₁ > θ_c, total internal reflection occurs at the interface. (c) Wave speed v₁ = 3.00 × 10⁸ / 1.77 = 1.69 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, and angular deviation δ = 180° − 2(72°) = 36.0°.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1.46 / 1.77.
States total internal reflection because the ray is in the higher-index medium with incident angle greater than the critical angle.

parts.expectedAnswer: Total internal reflection occurs because light travels in the medium of higher refractive index and the incident angle exceeds the critical angle.
workingSteps: Compare incident angle with critical angle in the optically denser medium to confirm total internal reflection.

parts.prompt: Calculate the angular deviation of the reflected ray from the incident ray's original forward direction, and find the wave speed in the first medium.
workingSteps: Wave speed in synthetic sapphire: v₁ = c / n₁ = 1.69 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹.
Angular deviation under total internal reflection: δ = 180° − 2(72°) = 36.0°.

items.stem: A straight 150 m step-index optical fiber in a flexible medical gastroscope bundle consists of a core of refractive index n_core = 1.62 and cladding of refractive index n_clad = 1.51. Its flat input end sits in air of refractive index 1.00, and a guided test ray is launched at θ_in = 19.4° to the central axis.
items.workedSolution: (a) θ_c = arcsin(1.51 / 1.62) = 68.8°. (b) Using n_ext sin θ_max = √(n_core² − n_clad²) gives θ_max = 35.9°. (c) For θ_in = 19.4°, θ_axis = 11.8° and L_ray = 150 / cos θ_axis = 153 m.

markScheme.criterion: Applies 1 sin θ_max = n_core sin(90° − θ_c).
Finds θ_axis = 11.8° and evaluates L / cos θ_axis.

items.stem: An experimental arrangement of a precision watch hairspring linear test bench comprises a block of mass m = 0.8 kg attached to an ideal horizontal spring of stiffness k = 72 N m⁻¹. The block oscillates in simple harmonic motion with amplitude x₀ = 0.035 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes m = 0.8 kg and k = 72 N m⁻¹ into T = 2π√(m / k).
Applies Hooke's law F_max = k x₀ = 72 × 0.035.
Divides F_max by m (or multiplies ω² by x₀).

parts.prompt: Calculate the period T of the simple harmonic oscillations.
Calculate the magnitude of the maximum restoring force F_max exerted by the spring.
Determine the magnitude of the maximum acceleration a_max of the oscillating mass.

items.stem: A simple pendulum rig in a lecture-hall rigid-ceiling wire pendulum carries a 0.25 kg sphere on a 0.4 m wire, swinging with small-angle arc amplitude 0.112 m where g = 9.81 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) T = 2π√(0.4 / 9.81) = 1.27 s. (b) v_max = √(9.81 / 0.4) × 0.112 = 0.555 m s⁻¹. (c) Lowest-point cord tension = m(g + v_max² / L) = 2.64 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies v_max = ω x₀ = (2π / T) x₀.
Uses T_cord = mg + mv_max² / L at the bottom of the arc.

parts.prompt: Calculate the period T of the pendulum.
Calculate the maximum speed v_max of the bob as it passes through equilibrium.
Determine the tension in the suspension cord as the bob passes through its lowest point.

items.stem: In a piezoelectric laser-mirror dithering stage, a mass m = 0.6 kg oscillates in undamped simple harmonic motion with angular frequency ω = 18 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude x₀ = 0.04 m. The parabolic energy–displacement curves are analyzed at displacement x = 0.024 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes m = 0.6 kg, ω = 18 rad s⁻¹, and x₀ = 0.04 m into E_tot = ½mω²x₀².
Applies E_k = ½mω²(x₀² − x²) or E_tot − ½mω²x².
Sets E_p = ½E_tot to obtain x = x₀ / √2.

parts.prompt: Calculate the total mechanical energy E_tot of the oscillating mass.
Calculate the kinetic energy E_k of the mass when its displacement is x = 0.024 m.
workingSteps: E_k = E_tot − E_p = ½mω²(x₀² − x²) = 0.0995 J.

parts.prompt: Determine the positive displacement x from equilibrium at which kinetic energy equals potential energy.

items.stem: A 1200 m multimode step-index optical fiber in a borehole geophysical telemetry line has a core of refractive index n_core = 1.5 and cladding of refractive index n_clad = 1.44 in air (n_ext = 1.00, shown with a guided ray launched at 14.9°). Take the speed of light in vacuum to be c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) t_axial = n_core L / c = (1.5 × 1200) / 3.00 × 10⁸ = 6.00 × 10⁻⁶ s. (b) Longest guided ray has path L / sin θ_c = L n_core / n_clad, giving t_max = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 6.25 × 10⁻⁶ s. (c) Modal pulse delay Δt = t_max − t_axial = 2.50 × 10⁻⁷ s.

markScheme.criterion: Uses t_axial = n_core L / c with n_core = 1.5 and L = 1200 m.
Applies L_max = L (n_core / n_clad) to find t_max = t_axial (n_core / n_clad).

items.stem: A vertical suspension stage in a precision gravimeter spring-mass test stage supports a 0.5 kg mass on an ideal coil spring of stiffness 25 N m⁻¹, oscillating vertically with amplitude 0.055 m about its equilibrium position (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) Δx_eq = mg / k = (0.5 × 9.81) / 25 = 0.196 m. (b) T = 2π√(0.5 / 25) = 0.889 s. (c) Maximum net SHM acceleration a_max = (k / m) x₀ = 2.75 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Uses mg = k Δx_eq with g = 9.81 m s⁻².
Evaluates a_max = ω² x₀ = (k / m) x₀.

parts.prompt: Calculate the static extension Δx_eq of the spring when the mass hangs at rest in equilibrium.
Calculate the period T of the vertical simple harmonic oscillations.
Determine the magnitude of the maximum net acceleration a_max of the mass during the oscillation.

items.stem: In a scanning-probe interferometric calibration stage, a component oscillates in simple harmonic motion at frequency f = 5 Hz with amplitude x₀ = 0.08 m. Its instantaneous state is examined when the displacement from equilibrium is x = -0.028 m.
items.workedSolution: (a) ω = 2π(5) = 31.4 rad s⁻¹. (b) At x = -0.028 m, a = −ω²x = 27.6 m s⁻². (c) Maximum acceleration magnitude a_max = ω² x₀ = 79.0 m s⁻².

Calculate the signed acceleration a when the displacement is x = -0.028 m.

items.stem: In a cryogenic cooler linear-compressor piston assembly, a 0.16 kg carriage tethered to a horizontal spring of spring constant 90 N m⁻¹ executes undamped simple harmonic motion of amplitude 0.09 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes m = 0.16 kg and k = 90 N m⁻¹ into T = 2π√(m / k).
Applies Hooke's law F_max = k x₀ = 90 × 0.09.
Divides F_max by m (or multiplies ω² by x₀).

parts.prompt: Calculate the period T of the simple harmonic oscillations.
Calculate the magnitude of the maximum restoring force F_max exerted by the spring.
Determine the magnitude of the maximum acceleration a_max of the oscillating mass.

items.stem: A simple pendulum rig in a seismic base-isolation pendulum test frame carries a 0.5 kg sphere on a 1.6 m wire, swinging with small-angle arc amplitude 0.352 m where g = 9.81 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) T = 2π√(1.6 / 9.81) = 2.54 s. (b) v_max = √(9.81 / 1.6) × 0.352 = 0.872 m s⁻¹. (c) Lowest-point cord tension = m(g + v_max² / L) = 5.14 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies v_max = ω x₀ = (2π / T) x₀.
Uses T_cord = mg + mv_max² / L at the bottom of the arc.

parts.prompt: Calculate the period T of the pendulum.
Calculate the maximum speed v_max of the bob as it passes through equilibrium.
Determine the tension in the suspension cord as the bob passes through its lowest point.

items.stem: A precision oscillator in an atomic-force microscope cantilever tip undergoes simple harmonic motion of amplitude 0.08 m and angular frequency 10 rad s⁻¹. Consider the instant when its displacement from equilibrium is 0.04 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses T = 2π / ω with ω = 10 rad s⁻¹.
Substitutes x₀ = 0.08 m and x = 0.04 m into v = ω√(x₀² − x²).

items.stem: In an immersion-microscopy optical stage, a narrow monochromatic beam (speed of light in vacuum c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) travels inside polycarbonate polymer of refractive index n₁ = 1.58 and strikes a flat boundary with distilled water of refractive index n₂ = 1.33 at an angle of incidence of 70° to the normal.
items.workedSolution: (a) sin θ_c = 1.33 / 1.58, so θ_c = 57.3°. (b) Because n₁ > n₂ and θ₁ > θ_c, total internal reflection occurs at the interface. (c) Wave speed v₁ = 3.00 × 10⁸ / 1.58 = 1.90 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, and angular deviation δ = 180° − 2(70°) = 40.0°.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1.33 / 1.58.
States total internal reflection because the ray is in the higher-index medium with incident angle greater than the critical angle.

parts.prompt: Calculate the critical angle θ_c at the polycarbonate polymer–distilled water boundary.
State and explain the optical phenomenon that occurs when this beam meets the boundary.
parts.expectedAnswer: Total internal reflection occurs because light travels in the medium of higher refractive index and the incident angle exceeds the critical angle.
workingSteps: Compare incident angle with critical angle in the optically denser medium to confirm total internal reflection.

parts.prompt: Calculate the angular deviation of the reflected ray from the incident ray's original forward direction, and find the wave speed in the first medium.
workingSteps: Wave speed in polycarbonate polymer: v₁ = c / n₁ = 1.90 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹.
Angular deviation under total internal reflection: δ = 180° − 2(70°) = 40.0°.

items.stem: A straight 450 m step-index optical fiber in an avionics fly-by-light data bus consists of a core of refractive index n_core = 1.57 and cladding of refractive index n_clad = 1.46. Its flat input end sits in air of refractive index 1.00, and a guided test ray is launched at θ_in = 15.9° to the central axis.
items.workedSolution: (a) θ_c = arcsin(1.46 / 1.57) = 68.4°. (b) Using n_ext sin θ_max = √(n_core² − n_clad²) gives θ_max = 35.3°. (c) For θ_in = 15.9°, θ_axis = 10.0° and L_ray = 450 / cos θ_axis = 457 m.

markScheme.criterion: Applies 1 sin θ_max = n_core sin(90° − θ_c).
Finds θ_axis = 10.0° and evaluates L / cos θ_axis.

parts.prompt: Calculate the critical angle θ_c at the core–cladding boundary.
Hence calculate the maximum acceptance angle θ_max in air of refractive index 1.00 for guided total internal reflection.
workingSteps: Maximum axial angle in core = 90° − θ_c; n_ext sin θ_max = n_core cos θ_c = √(1.57² − 1.46²).

parts.prompt: Calculate the total geometric path length travelled inside the core by the ray launched at 15.9°.
